title: Forget iPhone Duo: Ashwini Vaishnaw sets October 2028 deadline for India’s own smartphone brand
content: India could have its own homegrown smartphone brand by October 23, 2028, with Indian design, manufacturing and intellectual property at its core. The declaration of the objective was made during the NDTV World Summit on 23rd October 2026 by the Union Electronics and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. The government will expand the country's existing hardware design skills and create smartphones that can compete with international brands like Apple and Samsung, Vaishnaw said. The move coincides with India's push to become a world-class smartphone maker. Vaishnaw said an Indian company had already designed and delivered a 5G smartphone to a major US telecom operator. The plan is to leverage such capabilities to develop a phone with an Indian brand, but the government hasn't revealed its name, specifications, price tag or plans for releasing the phone. Ashwini Vaishnaw sets an October 2028 target for Indian smartphones Speaking at the NDTV World Summit on Friday, October 23, 2026, Vaishnaw set a two-year deadline for the proposed development. “This is 23 October 2026. Please note it: 23 October 2028. You will have Indian-designed, Indian-manufactured, Indian-branded mobile phones,” the minister said, as reported by NDTV. The government had challenged designers in India to create smartphone hardware about three and a half years ago, Vaishnaw said. He says two companies responded to the challenge, and one company designed a solution that was chosen by a big US telecom service provider. The company then created, produced and supplied the operator with a 5G mobile phone. Using this experience, India would now ensure that the smartphone design and its IP would remain within its shores, Vaishnaw said. Also Read | iPhone Duo sells out within 5 minutes on Blinkit; How much you could pay monthly What will it take to build an Indian smartphone? Assembling components is not enough to develop a smartphone. Processors, memory, displays, cameras, antenna and radio-frequency systems and power-management hardware need to be integrated in a small package. Engineers also need to ensure the reliability of connectivity, efficiency of battery life and overall performance. While talking about the proposed initiative, Vaishnaw pointed out these engineering challenges. However, he did not specify the Indian firm or the US telecom infrastructure operator that allegedly got its device. It wasn't to say all the parts of an Indian-designed smartphone will be made in India. The electronics industry needs to rely on international suppliers, and there is no indication of how much of the proposed phone will come from the local market. Also Read | Vivo Y600 packs 10,000mAh battery, sets Guinness World Record for livestream Can an Indian brand compete with Apple and Samsung? India has expanded smartphone manufacturing significantly, but owning a brand and its underlying intellectual property would represent a further step up the value chain. If a homegrown competitor is to be considered for purchase, it would be required to offer competitive pricing, hardware, software support and distribution network. Apple and Samsung already have established brand and product recognition, plus impressive product ecosystems. The current plan is for Vaishnaw to become the first commercial success in 2028, though that time frame has been pushed back from the initial 2020 timeline. The next two years will now decide whether India can shrug off its current design and manufacturing prowess and emerge as a competitive smartphone brand in the market.

title: Ever heard of a touchscreen garment? World's 1st is here - washable, breathable; it responds to finger presses, wireless
content: Ever wondered if your clothes could do more than just keep you warm? Researchers at the National University of Singapore have developed a touchscreen sleeve that lets you perform tasks you would normally reach for your phone to do. According to NUS, the sleeve was created by scientists at the university’s College of Design and Engineering (CDE) and consists of electronic fibres that display images and detect touch. By incorporating 54 of these fibres into a sleeve, the team says it has made the world’s first touchscreen built into clothing. Additionally, the sleeve can show images and videos, respond to taps, and connect wirelessly to other devices. It remains washable, breathable, and flexible, allowing users to interact with digital devices and view health information through their clothing without a rigid screen. Here's what the sleeve can do According to the findings, the sleeve can perform simple tasks familiar from early smartphones , including running a calculator, displaying photos, playing videos, acting as a compass, and responding to voice commands. Additionally, it can receive images via Bluetooth and automatically adjust the screen's orientation and brightness. Further, after placing a temperature sensor under the arm, the team found that the sleeve could measure body temperature and display the reading. View full Image NUS team created touch-sensitive and pixel layers within a thread just one millimetre thick and 10 metres long ( National University of Singapore ) How is the touchscreen built into clothing? Phone and laptop screens use flat, rigid panels to display information and respond to users. Fabric, made from individual fibres, has not offered the same capability, according to the findings. The researchers’ work makes it possible to build a full-colour touchscreen using electronic fibres that can be worked into clothing like ordinary yarn. The team behind the sleeve was led by Tural Khudiyev, an assistant professor in CDE’s Department of Materials Science and Engineering. The researchers published their findings on Wednesday. Commenting on the development, Khudiyev said, "What made this possible was our ability to construct the GUI system from electronic building blocks in fibre form — similar to traditional yarn, but with the sophisticated electronic functionality built directly into the fibres." Also Read | Apple Home Hub, new HomePod Mini and Apple TV could debut on 13 October To build a fibre-enabled garment display, the team used a laser to expose small sections of insulated wires where microchips needed to connect. They then used melted solder to join the components at those points and linked over 5,000 chips through over 20,000 electrical connections. The connected LEDs were built into a layered fibre using a process that heats and draws materials into thin threads. The resulting fibre was just one millimetre thick and 10 metres long. A touch-sensitive layer beneath the LEDs detects where the fibre is pressed and lights up the nearest pixel. The researchers built the screen into the forearm of a sleeve using 54 electronic fibres, each containing 96 tiny LED lights. The display measures 168 mm by 105 mm and can detect several touches at once. Each fibre works independently, so if one stops working, the others can continue to function. They also added a microphone, a speaker, and sensors that detect movement, direction, temperature, and surrounding light. View full Image Asst Prof Tural Khudiyev (second from the right) from the College of Design and Engineering, NUS, with his team members Heng Fu, PhD student (first from the right), Ziang Li, PhD candidate (second from the left), and Swetika Chaturvedi, Research Associate (first from the left). Together, they have created the world’s first touchscreen integrated into a garment ( National University of Singapore ) How does the sleeve withstand washing and bending? Despite the electronics, the sleeve remains flexible and breathable. Its brightness and touch response changed very little after 50 machine washes with detergent and 1,000 tight bends. The researchers also found that the display was as breathable as cotton, polyester, and denim, and met established safety limits for contact with skin. The team now plans to improve the screen’s resolution, add more sensors, and bring artificial intelligence (AI) into the fabric itself. These advances could eventually allow clothing to monitor the wearer and their surroundings, offering useful information and assistance when needed.

title: Google Play System update latest Version download: How to check updates and fix the January 2027 date
content: Several Android smartphones, including the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Google Pixel 8 Pro and Vivo X300 Ultra, are displaying an unexpected January 1, 2027 date for their Google Play System update. The problem came up months prior to the displayed date, in October 2026. According to reports on Reddit, the issue is impacting Android 12 users, including older phones. The incorrect time on the device seems to be related to the Google Play System update, not a new Android OS update. Affected Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra devices with the stable The One UI 9.0 interface has been updated with 100 MB in size, reports indicate. Google has not released a detailed changelog which explains the odd date. Here is everything users need to know about the update, its possible impact and how to check it on their phones. Why are Android phones showing a January 2027 update date? Google Play System updates let Google update selected Android components without requiring a complete operating system upgrade. These updates can enhance services, security-related elements and compatibility on compatible devices. However, the January 1, 2027 date is not an indication that Google has already published a future version of Android. According to reports, the date is probably a labelling/metadata mistake in the update. It's not just Samsung phones; there have been similar dates reported from users of Pixel, Vivo and other Android devices. Also Read | iPhone Duo sells out within 5 minutes on Blinkit; How much you could pay monthly Does the incorrect date affect phone performance or security? At this point these false time stamps have not been proven to impact the normal operation of the phone, installed applications, or the performance of the device. It doesn't imply that the phone is getting Android security patches for January 2027 as well. The Google Play System update date is not correlated with the Android version and the security patch level. Users should check these details independently before assessing whether their devices are up to date. The primary concern is that if the date is wrong, it is more difficult to determine which Google Play System update is installed. Google hasn't stated in the reports it has released the cause of the issue or a specific fix. How to check the Google Play System update on your phone Go to Settings on your mobile phone. Go to Security and Privacy or About Phone (depending on device). Tap Google Play System update. See the date and install the update if one is provided. For Samsung, it's usually listed under Settings > Security and privacy > Updates > Google Play system update, but it can be under a different menu depending on the software version. Also Read | Sundar Pichai reveals how he uses AI agents to track Google’s operations Should you reset your phone to fix the issue? No. Reports suggest that changing the date and time settings or resetting the device does not correct the displayed timestamp. Users don't need to reset their phones to factory settings just because it has a January 1, 2027, date. Google has not confirmed when a correction will arrive.

title: Gone in 300 seconds! ₹3 lakh iPhone Duo foldable phone sells out on Blinkit; Is Apple's monthly lease worth it?
content: Apple’s first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, sold out within five minutes of going on sale on quick-commerce platform Blinkit in Delhi-NCR on Friday, October 23, 2026. The device is available for ₹ 299,900 in India and hikes to ₹ 449,900 for the highest configuration. The rapid sellout drew comments on social media, with some users asking about the number of units available and others commenting that it was a sign of India's increased purchasing power. The iPhone Duo debuted on Blinkit at 8:15 am yesterday, with all the units sold in just five minutes, Albinder Dhindsa, the founder of Blinkit, said on X. He further noted that Blinkit is on the path to getting more stock in the coming weeks but offered no idea about the quantity of the inventories sold. For those who are interested, meanwhile, the Upgrade leasing programme launched by Apple provides an alternative route to Apple's high-powered foldable handset to those who live in eligible markets by paying for the phone in monthly instalments. iPhone Duo price in India and specifications The iPhone Duo comes in four storage sizes in India. The 256GB model costs ₹ 299,900, while the 512GB variant is priced at ₹ 324,900. The 1TB version costs ₹ 374,900, and the top-end 2TB model is priced at ₹ 449,900. The phone has a 7.6-inch foldable screen inside and a 5.4-inch screen on the outside. Fitted with Apple's A20 Pro chip with a 48MP Dual Fusion camera system. It is also available with a titanium frame. Also Read | iPhone 17 Pro gets ₹62,850 discount on Flipkart, but there’s a catch Apple upgrade offers monthly payments for iPhone Duo Leasing gives buyers an option other than paying the price upfront in markets where Apple Upgrade is offered. PCMag reports the price for the iPhone Duo to be $57.99 per month (around ₹ 5,100/month) for a 24-month lease and $82.99 per month (around ₹ 7,300/month) for a 12-month lease, at an indicative rate of ₹ 88/dollar. However, these monthly payments do not include AppleCare+ coverage. Buyers must buy eligible protection separately so that they can factor in repair and accidental damage costs if they're going to opt for the leasing option. Apple Upgrade, launched in partnership with buy-now-pay-later platform Klarna on July 28, allows eligible customers to return their device, purchase it at the end of the lease or upgrade to another product. Approval requires a credit check, and iPhones have to be paired with AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon in the U.S. Also Read | iPhone Duo hits nearly ₹4 lakh in India as shortage drives up grey-market prices Is leasing the iPhone Duo worth it? Leasing can lower upfront costs, but it doesn't mean that the buyer will actually be the owner of the telephone after paying off month after month. According to PCMag, 24 payments of $57.99 would total $1,391.76 (around ₹ 1.23 lakh). The $1,999 device would still have to be paid for an extra $607.24 (approx. ₹ 53,400), including applicable taxes, cover and other charges. For Indian buyers, the reported US leasing prices should not be treated as an available financing offer in India.

title: Polish PM Donald Tusk seeks deeper technology cooperation with India across AI, digital and space sectors
content: Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], October 23 (ANI): Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has called for stronger technology partnerships between India and Poland, highlighting opportunities for companies from both countries across sectors including artificial intelligence (AI) solutions, digital products and space technology. Addressing the Global Investors Meet 2027, Tusk said Polish companies could contribute specialised technologies and expertise in European markets, while Indian firms could leverage their capabilities to scale production and services and expand their reach in international markets. “We see an opportunity for partnerships in which Polish and Indian companies combine their research and development teams, technologies, and capital to jointly introduce new digital products to the market,” he said. Noting that India and Poland have the capabilities to jointly develop AI systems for manufacturing, automation, data analysis, diagnostics and infrastructure management, Tusk said, “We can also create tools available to small and medium-sized enterprises which often lack their own research capabilities.” He also called for stronger collaboration between universities and research institutions in machine learning, data analysis and the safe use of AI. Highlighting cooperation in the space sector, Tusk said, “Polish space sector companies are already finding partners in India for joint technology development in the field of satellite components, earth observation, navigation, software, data analytics, space security, and dual use solutions.” Highlighting the potential for deeper cooperation, Tusk said India and Poland could move beyond traditional trade to jointly develop technologies and expand their presence in global markets. “Now it is time to translate these declarations into joint ventures.” He noted that the two countries had elevated their bilateral ties to a strategic partnership, with an action plan covering technological cooperation, cybersecurity and the space sector. Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Friday invited Poland to participate as a country partner in the state’s Global Investors Meet 2027. The CM said the state was keen to deepen bilateral cooperation in investment, technology, innovation and employment, building on Bengaluru’s technology ecosystem and Poland’s expertise in advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence and green energy. He welcomed the TZMO Group’s proposed investment of approximately ₹ 80 crore in the KIADB Vemgal Industrial Area in Kolar district, spread across five acres. The project has the potential to generate around 1,000 jobs and introduce the manufacture of smart adult incontinence pads in India for the first time, as per the release. “Karnataka has considerable scope for further Polish investment, particularly in medical products, healthcare and advanced manufacturing,” he said. Shivakumar also encouraged Polish technology companies to explore Bengaluru’s opportunities in artificial intelligence, software, gaming, robotics, smart manufacturing and start-up innovation. He called for stronger partnerships in research, education and technology transfer to generate skilled employment. The Chief Minister identified renewable energy, waste-to-energy, sludge management, wastewater treatment and circular economy solutions as major areas for cooperation. Apart from this, the CM also invited Polish companies, including Asseco and Polpharma, to explore partnerships in information technology, software services, pharmaceuticals and research and development. Companies such as ORLEN and KGHM Polska Miedź were encouraged to consider investment and technology collaboration in Karnataka’s energy, petrochemical and advanced manufacturing sectors. Shivakumar urged Polish companies to explore Karnataka’s districts and take advantage of the state’s industrial ecosystem. As per Shivkumar, Poland’s Honorary Consulate in Bengaluru could play an important role in strengthening business and institutional ties and facilitating closer engagement between Polish enterprises and Karnataka’s industries. (ANI)

title: iPhone Duo shortage in India: Why buyers are paying up to ₹1 lakh extra for Apple's foldable
content: Apple’s first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, is in short supply in India as demand outstrips initial stock. The 256GB variant is officially priced at ₹ 2,99,900, but some retailers are reportedly selling it at a premium of ₹ 70,000 to ₹ 1 lakh, bringing the effective price close to ₹ 4 lakh. Retailers in Ghaziabad, Noida and Delhi report shortages after the phone went on sale on Friday, 23 October 2026. India Today, which spoke to more than 17 retailers, reported that several received only about 10 units each. Apple iPhone Duo shortage leaves retailers struggling The All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA), which represents over 1.5 lakh mainline mobile retailers, also pointed to limited initial supplies. It said some top retailers expected around 100 units across variants but received only five to seven. AIMRA said buyers were willing to pay ₹ 25,000 to ₹ 1 lakh above the maximum retail price. Some shops are still selling at the official price to loyal customers, without a premium . Also Read | Want Apple’s first foldable iPhone? iPhone Duo pre-orders start today at 5:30 pm Global supply constraints push delivery estimates into 2027 The shortage is not limited to India. According to Bloomberg, limited production capacity, advanced hinge engineering and new display technology have created manufacturing challenges, and only a few facilities in China make the device. A report ahead of the launch had also flagged production yields stuck at 60%. Apple’s US and India websites showed delivery dates in 2027 within hours of orders opening. title: Quantum computing could generate up to USD 2.7 trillion in economic value by 2035: McKinsey
content: New Delhi [India], October 23 (ANI): Quantum computing could generate between USD 1.3 trillion and USD 2.7 trillion in economic value worldwide by 2035, but businesses need to invest in talent, technology and partnerships now to secure an early advantage, according to a report by McKinsey & Company. The report said quantum technology was moving from experimental projects towards commercial applications, with more than 300 organisations worldwide already working with quantum technology providers. The report warned that companies delaying investment risk losing access to the partnerships, talent and intellectual property needed to compete as the technology develops. It also highlighted potential security risks, as sufficiently advanced quantum computers could eventually break the public-key encryption systems used to protect sensitive information. “Waiting to invest is risky,” the report said, adding that companies could face serious security challenges when quantum computers reach the stage of being able to break existing encryption methods. McKinsey outlined three stages of development, from early commercial adoption to the establishment of competitive positions by 2035 and a wider quantum-enabled economy by 2040. Investment in the sector is already increasing. Equity investment in quantum technology rose from USD 2.5 billion in 2024 to USD 13.3 billion in 2025, the report said. Combined revenue of quantum computing companies crossed USD 1 billion in 2025 and could rise to as much as USD 4.4 billion by 2028. The report estimated that the global market for quantum computing hardware, software and services could reach USD 60 billion to USD 100 billion by 2035. Quantum communication could represent a market worth USD 11 billion to USD 15 billion, while quantum sensing could reach USD 7 billion to USD 10 billion by the same year. However, McKinsey cautioned that the timeline remains uncertain because of manufacturing constraints, shortages of specialised talent and a lack of consensus on which quantum computing technology will scale most effectively. The report also identified cybersecurity, pharmaceuticals, chemicals and robotics as areas where quantum technology could create significant value. Quantum computing could generate up to USD 400 billion in value for the pharmaceutical industry and unlock up to USD 800 billion in the chemicals industry by 2035, it estimated. McKinsey further said businesses should focus on building partnerships, testing potential applications and developing internal expertise before large-scale quantum systems become commercially available. It added that quantum computing could also help address computing and energy constraints affecting the expansion of artificial intelligence (AI). (ANI)

title: What to know about the AI-detected security bug impacting wide swaths of the internet
content: The language that's known as the backbone of the internet is now subject to what experts describe as one of the most notable vulnerabilities in recent memory. PHP is a widely used general-purpose scripting language that is geared toward web development, and thus, it powers the majority of websites around the world. When the organization behind the language and the FBI’s cyber division warned Wednesday of significant vulnerabilities in the language , government agencies, corporations and other organizations were sent into a flurry. The episode also highlights how artificial intelligence is changing the game when it comes to web security. Here's what to make of the discovery of the vulnerabilities and the fallout. The official website for PHP and several other organizations and agencies released security advisories Wednesday urging PHP users to patch two critical vulnerabilities or shut down their sites if they couldn’t update them immediately. The PHP Foundation, which works to provide transparency and accountability with the language, said the vulnerabilities could be exploited and allow bad actors to get unauthenticated access to sites running PHP. This would mean attackers could control a web server remotely without needing a password, said James Sullivan, director of cyber and tech at the Royal United Services Institute in London. That could allow a hacker to steal data, alter data or use the system as a platform from which to launch other attacks, he said. PHP powers about 70% of websites globally, so the possible exposure to vulnerability was immense. The language is free and open-source, which contributes to its prevalence online. PHP is behind the content management systems WordPress and Drupal, which are commonly used by governments for their sites, and MediaWiki, the software that runs Wikipedia. In accordance with the security advisories issued this week, several websites were taken offline to prevent exposure while they fixed the problem. There has been disruption to some government services and websites, including in the United Kingdom, Finland and Japan. Some websites may still be down because there are multiple patches available for different types of software, and some organizations may still be waiting to receive them. They also need to be tested to make sure they work. Charl van der Walt, the head of security research at Orange Cyberdefense, said he believes the reaction to the vulnerabilities is just the “early tremors” of the disruption they could cause in the weeks and months ahead. He said there likely will be further service disruptions as bad actors scan the internet for vulnerable systems. The vulnerabilities have been known about since at least 2024, according to the PHP Foundation. A security team developed several competing approaches to solutions, but each had downsides. It seemed there wasn't a practical or concrete way attackers could exploit the vulnerabilities, so progress on a fix stalled, the foundation said. The group took responsibility for not coming up with a fix sooner, saying: “We won’t pretend otherwise: the delay was a structural failure, caused by both the security team’s decision process and its lack of resources.” Some experts say the discovery of the vulnerability could have been even earlier than 2024. Although humans first discovered the vulnerabilities, artificial intelligence agents helped to identify how they could be exploited, and also supported the process of testing and validating the fixes. In a blog post, OpenAI said it had led a coalition of researchers, security providers and others to address vulnerabilities in PHP over the past two months. Researchers at Wiz, a cloud security platform, also said they independently used AI to identify the vulnerabilities. The accessibility of AI means that many organizations big and small now have more advanced ways to proactively and reactively respond to security threats. But it also means bad actors have more advanced ways to exploit digital weak points, and at great scale and speed. “It’s not quite as easy for defenders as it is for attackers,” van der Walt said. “You find the vulnerability in something. You replace it. But with what? Is there an alternative that is patched and robust and tested and approved?” Sullivan, of the Royal United Services Institute in London, said while the push-and-pull can be worrisome, he's focused on the positive side. “We’ve actually seen quite a decent use case here where AI can discover some critical vulnerabilities and then the community can come together to remediate them,” he said.

title: US banks are blocking third-party AI agents access to customer accounts, sources say
content: Oct 22 (Reuters) - Major US banks have been blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside customer accounts and making transactions, two people familiar with the situation said, following a report that AI agents were accessing bank accounts and taking actions independent of user instructions. The banking industry has become increasingly concerned that sophisticated AI agents could harm the banking system and the institutions trusted to hold people's wealth. An Axios report on Thursday said some AI agents attempted to take actions that appeared to be independent of user instructions, citing people familiar with the matter. In some cases, bank customers have shared their login ID and password with agents, with banks typically flagging and blocking those transactions, a person in the banking industry said. Still, such transactions cannot be deemed unauthorized if credentials were shared by the customer. Morgan Stanley has blocked third-party agents from accessing its platforms, but it had not seen any instances of unauthorized or rogue AI agents, according to a person familiar with the matter. Top banking executives earlier this month discussed the risks of AI agents acting on customers' behalf, with some warning the technology is adding significant risks for both customers and banks. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon earlier this month said the largest US lender was developing tools to navigate the risk of AI agents carrying out tasks on their own. "We're not going to allow just any outside agent to come in inside the company because that's just too risky for clients and for JPMorgan," he said at the time. Charles Schwab CEO Richard Wurster earlier this month also said the brokerage was blocking unauthorized agents. "I get a report every day tracking how many times we've had to block one of the different agents, and it's not many because I think people aren't using it in that way in their financial life. We are blocking it because we want to have control over authentication and the experience," Wurster said. (Reporting by Devika Nair and Arasu Kannagi Basil in Bengaluru, Tatiana Bautzer and Nupur Anand in New York; Editing by Jochelle Mendonca, Chris Sanders and David Gaffen)

title: Samsung brings 14 refurbished Galaxy S24, S25 smartphones to Amazon in US, prices start at $489
content: Samsung Electronics America has expanded its Certified Re-Newed smartphone programme, bringing select refurbished Galaxy devices to Amazon.com while adding the Galaxy S26, Galaxy S26+ and Galaxy S26 Ultra to its refurbished lineup on Samsung.com. The expansion gives customers another option to buy Samsung smartphones at lower prices than new devices, with the company offering refurbished models that undergo repairs, testing and quality checks before being sold. The Amazon lineup includes 14 models from the Galaxy S24 and Galaxy S25 series, covering standard, Plus, FE and Ultra variants. Prices start at $489, excluding taxes and fees. The devices come with a one-year limited manufacturer warranty and are eligible for Samsung Care+ protection. Samsung uses genuine parts and new batteries Samsung said every smartphone sold under its Certified Re-Newed programme is serviced by its specialists using 100% genuine Samsung parts, including a certified new battery. Each device must also pass 147 quality checkpoints before receiving the Certified Re-Newed label. The smartphones are packaged in 100% recyclable materials and include a quick-start guide, data cable and SIM ejector pin. The Amazon listing includes the Galaxy S24 FE, Galaxy S24, Galaxy S24+, Galaxy S24 Ultra, Galaxy S25, Galaxy S25+ and Galaxy S25 Ultra, with select storage and colour options. Galaxy S26 series refurbished phones start at $759 Samsung has also added the Galaxy S26 series to its Certified Re-Newed programme, with the devices available exclusively through Samsung.com. The refurbished Galaxy S26 starts at $759, while the Galaxy S26+ starts at $929. The Galaxy S26 Ultra is priced from $1,099. All three models are available in six colour options: White, Sky Blue, Pink Gold, Black, Silver Shadow and Cobalt Violet. Samsung said the S26 series devices are assembled by its engineers using genuine Samsung parts and feature brand-new batteries. They also carry the same one-year limited warranty offered with new smartphones. Customers can additionally opt for Samsung Care+ with Theft and Loss, which provides protection against accidents and damage. The plan includes unlimited battery repairs and repairs for cracked screens and back glass at no charge, according to Samsung. Galaxy AI features remain a key selling point The Galaxy S26 series is powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 Mobile Platform for Galaxy, which Samsung says delivers improvements in CPU, GPU and neural processing unit performance over the previous generation. The devices also offer Galaxy AI features, including Now Nudge, which provides contextual suggestions, and Now Brief, which delivers reminders about important events. With its Certified Re-Newed programme, Samsung is extending the availability of its smartphones to customers seeking refurbished devices backed by manufacturer servicing and warranty support. The company's latest expansion spans two sales channels: Amazon.com for select Galaxy S24 and S25 models, and Samsung.com for the refurbished Galaxy S26 lineup. The refurbished phones are not available on Amazon in India and when selected from Amazon.com, it shows the message that it can't be delivered to the current location.

title: WhatsApp, Telegram SIM binding rules from January 1, 2027: Who will be affected in India?
content: WhatsApp, Telegram and other messaging apps may face new access restrictions in India as the government prepares to implement SIM-binding rules from January 1, 2027. The Department of Telecom (DoT) has issued guidelines requiring the covered platforms to integrate the accounts with the live SIMs used for registration by December 31, 2026. The rules are to prevent cyber fraud using Indian mobile numbers. Under the new regulation, messaging services should ensure that accounts are associated with the registered SIM card that is installed in the device. This may impact the users of WhatsApp or Telegram over Wi-Fi without their registered SIMs, and those who use more than one device or often change their SIM cards. The DoT issued the directive on November 28, 2025, under the Telecom Cyber Security Rules. However, the precise impact on individual devices will depend on how platforms implement the requirements. What is SIM binding, and why is the government introducing it? Like the others, most messaging apps will use a one-time SMS code to verify your number. Users are usually able to retain access to their accounts even if they remove or disable the SIM card. SIM binding is designed to overcome this by ensuring the SIM card is activated and in the device. According to the Ministry of Communications, cybercriminals exploit this gap to commit digital fraud, including scams involving callers impersonating government officials. Last year, losses from cyber fraud accounted for more than ₹ 22,800 crore, the ministry said. The rules will enhance traceability and stop misuse of telecom identifiers, the government says. Also Read | How eight ‘weak’ eMudhra certificates could let attackers impersonate websites Which messaging apps are covered by the new rules? As per the order, the covered apps include WhatsApp , Telegram, Snapchat, Arattai , ShareChat, Josh, JioChat and Signal. The impact on WhatsApp's user base in India, estimated to be in the range of 500 million, could be significant. It is possible that the compliance requirements and their implementation could vary between platforms. According to reports, WhatsApp has now started beta testing SIM binding on Android. How will SIM binding affect WhatsApp Web and other devices? Removing a registered SIM, disabling a number or sending messages from a device without a SIM may disrupt users. Additionally, people who travel overseas often or change their phones frequently or use only Wi-Fi on their tablets may want to make adjustments as well. The DoT has revised another part of the directive. The earlier idea of logging users out of Web sessions every six hours has been removed and replaced with a risk-based logout requirement. This translates to no more automatic logouts every six hours. Also Read | Vivo X500 Ultra leak hints at major camera upgrade, 8,000mAh battery What happens if messaging apps fail to comply? Platforms that fail to comply with the requirements may be subject to the provisions of the Telecommunications Act, 2023 and the Telecom Cyber Security Rules, 2024. According to a survey conducted by CUTS International, 80% of consumers and over 60% of small businesses were anticipating disruption due to SIM binding. The DoT also intends to launch an MNV platform to verify phone numbers to ensure that they belong to legitimate users. It's important for users to be aware that it's reported as an operational start date (after the compliance date of December 31, 2026). The rules don't say that all WhatsApp or Telegram accounts will stop functioning on that day. The actual impact will depend on platform compliance and how SIM verification is enforced.

title: Explained: What is PHP? Why govt websites went dark? International advisory issued as AI exposes serious cyber glitch
content: Governments and companies around the world shut down websites on Thursday as they raced to protect themselves against hacking after artificial intelligence uncovered critical flaws in a widely used programming language called PHP. The discovery has triggered international advisories and forced websites to go offline worldwide, marking a new phase in cybersecurity in which increasingly powerful AI can uncover software vulnerabilities that humans have missed for years. What is PHP? PHP, which originally stood for "personal home page" but is now known as "hypertext preprocessor", is a foundational programming language that sits beneath popular web design platforms. It helps run approximately 70 to 75% of all websites globally, spanning from online stores and news outlets to critical government services. Also Read | Why PHP bug is a business risk, not just an IT problem: ‘Next step could be…’ PHP vulnerabilities The current crisis stems from two critical vulnerabilities—CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619—hidden deep within PHP's core engine, specifically in its memory management and error handling. CVE-2026-109618 is an out-of-memory error where PHP can leave partially initialised internal data behind if a request reaches the memory limit at the wrong moment, leading to memory corruption and potential remote code execution. CVE-2026-109619 involves stale global state issues in which a fatal error could leave internal state pointing to memory from a previous request, allowing a later request to use that freed memory for remote code execution. These flaws are considered memory-safety bugs that can allow attackers to access servers without authorisation, steal sensitive data, or execute malicious code, bypassing usernames or passwords entirely. Also Read | PHP2Shell vulnerability: How Google, OpenAI and Amazon respond How AI exposed a decade-old flaw The bugs had been hiding in PHP's source code for years. While concerns over out-of-memory errors were raised by a core PHP developer during a 2024 audit, no working exploit was discovered, and the fix was delayed due to the complexity of patching without breaking backward compatibility. The vulnerabilities were finally exposed independently by two cybersecurity entities in August 2026, both utilising advanced artificial intelligence: Ryan Austin, a researcher at the California-based security firm Calif, identified the flaws using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model as part of the "Patch the Planet" project. Google-owned Wiz Research independently found the flaws weeks later, utilising their autonomous AI tool, Wiz Atlas, alongside Google's Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol. Wiz stated that pre-AI, the manual work required to study failures and refine exploitation techniques would have been difficult to scale, but with AI, this barrier has been removed. Why did government websites go dark? Details of the vulnerabilities leaked online on Tuesday, 20 October, just ahead of PHP's planned emergency security release on Wednesday. This leak fuelled fears that hackers could use AI to quickly exploit the flaws at a massive scale. To shield themselves, many countries and companies mobilised as a precaution, pulling vulnerable systems offline to prevent attackers from reaching and exploiting the flaw while administrators installed the necessary security patches. Also Read | Decade-old PHP bug puts websites at risk: How AI uncovered it | Explained International advisories and global impact The discovery triggered emergency responses, service outages, and strict advisories across the globe: The United States : The White House was informed of the vulnerability. Amazon's security chief reported attempts to exploit flaws in one of its decoy systems on October 17 and warned that the flaws were being "broadly exploited in the wild". The US National Security Agency and the FBI urged organisations to isolate affected systems and take them offline if immediate patching is not feasible. Europe : Governments in Finland and the Netherlands took public-facing national and local government websites offline. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre advised organisations to check systems for malicious activity and consider taking them offline. Japan : The crisis highlighted the country's struggle with ageing digital infrastructure. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged immediate patching, while the finance and health ministries halted certain webpages. Private entities, including Mizuho Financial Group, ANA Holdings, Japan Airlines, East Japan Railway, and Seven-Eleven Japan, suspended various online services and apps. Asia-Pacific : South Korea raised its private-sector cybersecurity alert level and activated emergency measures. With data showing approximately 1.5 million internet hosts running PHP versions for which no fix is available, experts warn that smaller websites run by individuals and organisations with limited technical resources could face greater risks in the coming weeks. ( With agency inputs )

title: Flexible grid connections can cut AI data centre power wait to 2-4 years from 5-10 years: BCG
content: New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Data centres supporting artificial intelligence (AI) could reduce their electricity connection waiting time from 5-10 years or more to 2-4 years by accepting flexible grid connections and using their own power generation and storage systems, according to a report by Boston Consulting Group (BCG). “Flexible access can reduce time to power from 5-10 years to 2-4 years by lowering the need for (major) grid reinforcement,” the report said. The report noted that this approach could help data centres become operational earlier while reducing pressure on electricity grids and limiting additional costs for other power consumers. The analysis focuses on five Northwest European markets — the UK, Germany, France, Belgium and the Netherlands — over the 2030-2035 investment period. BCG said power availability has become a major constraint on data centre expansion, with connection queues in several markets stretching for years. Global data centre power demand is projected to reach around 210 gigawatts by 2030, compared with 84 gigawatts in 2025, according to the report's estimates. Under the proposed approach, data centres could accept non-firm electricity connections, under which power supply may be reduced during periods of grid congestion, instead of waiting for a guaranteed connection. They could use on-site generation, batteries and flexible computing workloads to maintain operations during such periods. The report said connecting earlier could unlock significant financial benefits. For a modelled 150-megawatt AI inference data centre in Northwest Europe, connecting three years earlier could generate an estimated USD 1.28 billion in additional profits, before accounting for the costs of on-site power assets. However, the approach also involves trade-offs. BCG estimated that an off-grid setup could increase annual power supply costs by 70-230 per cent compared with a firm grid connection, depending on how the cost of power assets is accounted for. The report said such arrangements may be useful where flexible grid connections are unavailable or would require substantial additional investment. BCG also said grid-positive data centres could help spread fixed electricity network costs across a larger base of consumption and reduce the need for additional power generation and grid infrastructure. "Whether a data center burdens or strengthens the system depends on how and where it connects, and how it runs once it is online," the report said. The report called for governments to develop national data centre strategies, guide projects towards locations with available grid capacity and speed up approvals for on-site power assets. It also recommended that grid operators make flexible connections a standard option rather than an exception. BCG said faster connections would require changes to how data centres are located, connected and operated, alongside clear rules for on-site power generation. (ANI)

title: Indias AI financing demand to shift towards data centres, but GPU, regulatory risks persist: Report
content: New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): India’s AI market is expected to see a shift in demand towards debt financing for data centres and computing infrastructure. At the same time, the sector faces several risks, including the rapid obsoleteness of graphics processing units (GPUs), uncertain revenue models and evolving governance regulations, according to a report by Union Bank of India. The report says India's AI market is expected to witness strong growth, driven by its expanding internet and smartphone user base and rising adoption of generative AI by enterprises. India currently has around 880-900 million internet users, with a target of reaching 1.2 billion by 2030, while its smartphone user base stands at approximately 700-750 million. “India brings a huge talent pool and one of the world's largest internet user bases to this race, but still lags in indigenous compute infrastructure and foundational models,” it said. Also, generative AI is now part of over 60 per cent of large IT deals and India's share of global mobile data traffic is among the highest in the world, which further provides support for AI development and adoption. The lender highlighted several strengths of India's AI sector, including “World's largest tech talent pool feeding AI development,” a massive internet and smartphone user base generating valuable data, and strong IT services capabilities that enable the adoption and implementation of AI solutions across enterprises. However, the lender pointed out several weaknesses in India's AI sector, including limited domestic manufacturing capacity for computing infrastructure and graphics processing units (GPUs). It noted that India's capabilities in developing foundational AI models are still at an early stage compared to the US and China, while regulatory frameworks related to data privacy and AI governance are still evolving, posing challenges to the sector's growth. “Rapid global AI hardware obsolescence (18-24 month cycles),” along with global talent poaching to US and Gulf AI labs and regulatory uncertainty on data and AI governance, remain the biggest threats to the overall sector. According to the report, India's AI sector offers diverse financing opportunities, with GPU and computing infrastructure requiring high capital investment through structured debt, sale-leaseback arrangements and hyperscaler funding. Foundational AI model development, on the other hand, relies on venture capital, private equity, government grants and corporate R&D funding, while AI SaaS and applications attract venture capital, venture debt and revenue-based financing. Notably, AI skilling and Centres of Excellence (CoEs), which require lower investment, are primarily supported by government grants, CSR funding and public-private partnerships. Overall, the lender recommended developing structured and equipment-financing products for GPU clusters and expanding venture-debt partnerships to support AI application companies. Over the next three to five years, financing demand is expected to shift towards debt funding for data centres and computing infrastructure, it said. (ANI)

title: Meta puts Muse agent at heart of AI strategy, plans new stock to power investments
content: By Jaspreet Singh and Katie Paul Oct 21 - Meta introduced new non-voting shares on Wednesday to help fund the social media giant's costly AI expansion, as executives laid out their vision for organizing the company's future around its nascent AI agent business. Shares of the Facebook and Instagram parent rose more than 4% in extended trading. Meta also forecast fourth-quarter revenue above Wall Street estimates and reported strong growth of its new consumer AI agent app Muse. The company has been pouring money into advanced chips and data centers to compete more aggressively with AI market leaders OpenAI and Anthropic, propelling it to the vanguard of an emerging consumer AI agent race while also eroding its historically strong free cash flow. Meta will issue a new class of non-voting Class C common stock in January 2027, effectively resulting in a two-for-one split, to fund acquisitions and retain top talent while maintaining CEO Mark Zuckerberg's control. Zuckerberg said more than 10 million people in the US and Canada have set up Muse accounts in a month and a half and growth remained strong. He said he expected Muse would eventually serve "billions of people" who would potentially generate more revenue than the average Meta user, forecasting the venture would give rise to the kind of network effect that helped build his social media empire. "Part of the reason why we're not just charging everyone up front to use this is we want to establish this Muse network, and we think that it's going to be more valuable for people at scale when there are a lot of people and businesses using Muse," Zuckerberg said on a conference call after Meta published its third-quarter financial report. HIGHER COSTS Still, Zuckerberg acknowledged that the costs of offering Muse were higher than those associated with many of Meta's other new products over the years, and said the company would move to monetize the agent "somewhat sooner on this than our normal playbook." Meta CFO Susan Li forecast the company's AI businesses would begin contributing incremental revenue in 2027 and become "a meaningful source of revenue diversification over time." The executives also emphasized that AI would be the focus moving forward for Meta’s loss-making Reality Labs unit, which had led the charge on the company’s vision to build the “metaverse,” an immersive digital world that inspired its name change from Facebook to Meta in 2021. In their financial report, they said they “remain focused on improving Reality Labs profitability” and forecast its losses would narrow next year to around $15 billion “as we reallocate investment toward other priority areas, primarily AI.” The company raised the lower end of its annual spending forecast, now expecting capital expenditure to be between $135 billion and $145 billion this year, up from $130 billion to $145 billion expected previously. It reported a free cash flow deficit of $2.12 billion in the third quarter, compared with positive free cash flow of $10.63 billion a year earlier. Revenue for the third quarter came in better than expected at $64.60 billion, ahead of Wall Street estimates of $63.37 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. Meta also projected fourth-quarter revenue between $73 billion and $76 billion, above estimates of $73.73 billion. The early popularity of Muse and the release of a competitive new series of AI models have helped Meta justify its spending to investors, even though some enterprises are restricting the agent's access over security concerns. "The market has shifted from punishing Meta for spending to rewarding it for having a compelling product story," said Jesse Cohen, senior analyst at Investing.com. LEGAL CHALLENGES Legal challenges are mounting, including a $25 billion penalty ordered by a judge in New Mexico earlier on Wednesday after a jury found Meta misled the state's residents about ​how it shared user data with third parties and enforced policies on hate speech and misinformation in a case related to British political consulting firm Cambridge Analytica. The $25 billion penalty is a "stark reminder of the current legal challenges Meta faces, which will continue into next year," Emarketer senior analyst Minda Smiley said. "Questions and concerns related to privacy and safety will only ramp up should AI agents become more mainstream, which could ultimately hurt Meta considering its reputation in this area." In August, Meta agreed to pay as much as $18 billion over a decade and restrict teenagers' use of Facebook and Instagram to settle claims by nearly all US states alleging that Meta's platforms were designed to addict children. Meta posted diluted earnings per share of $3.83 in the quarter, a figure that would have been $7.40 had it not been for a $9.89 billion charge related to the August settlement. The agreement removed a significant regulatory hurdle that had weighed on Meta's stock and allowed the company to avoid a potentially lengthy trial that could have exposed more internal documents about its treatment of young users. Still, Meta warned in its guidance on Wednesday that it continued to face scrutiny and US trials around "youth-related issues" that could impact its financial results. title: Nasdaq climbs over 1% as SpaceX, Super Micro boost AI sentiment
content: (Updates prices to late afternoon) * Indexes up: Dow 0.58%, S&P 0.73%, Nasdaq 1.28% * Netflix slides after bleak forecast * AT&T falls despite topping quarterly estimates * Super Micro Computer's results lift peers HPE, Dell By Sinéad Carew and Purvi Agarwal Oct 21 (Reuters) - The tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street's gains on Wednesday after quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer improved investor appetite for stocks related to artificial intelligence, while Netflix slipped as its forecast disappointed investors. SpaceX shares were up 7% after Elon Musk's rocket and space technology firm posted its first profit as a public company. Musk said a merger of SpaceX and Tesla would be "a good idea," sending Tesla shares up 3.5%. Super Micro jumped more than 9% and was among the S&P 500's top gainers after the AI server maker forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin above Wall Street estimates, signaling that AI demand remained resilient. Its peers rose too, HPE by 4.2% and Dell by 5%. The reports provided some reassurance to investors who have been worried about the sustainability of massive spending on AI buildouts and their profitability. The technology sector was hammered last week by a selloff in AI-linked stocks, with data center operator CoreWeave at the center of the storm. "It's really a positive technology story for almost anyone that is somewhat involved in the artificial intelligence ecosystem," said Marc Dizard, chief investment officer at Huntington Bank. He noted that SpaceX had "crushed" expectations. "The technology market reaction has been a reaffirmation that the artificial intelligence trade is still intact." Dizard said sentiment can quickly shift around AI, and that investors will seek reaffirmation when they monitor earnings reports from companies such as Meta, due out after the market close when Tesla is also scheduled to report results. At 2:21 p.m. ET (1821 GMT), the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 304.97 points, or 0.58%, to 52,800.85, the S&P 500 gained 55.99 points, or 0.73%, to 7,768.65 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 337.67 points, or 1.28%, to 26,762.48. The S&P 500 information technology sector rose 1.3%, lifting the benchmark index, as most chip stocks rebounded. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index was up 1.3%. The index has had a volatile month so far, with its longest losing streak in 18 years, eight straight sessions of declines. The overall rise on the S&P 500 was contained by a 1.2% drop in communication services stocks, dragged down by a 6.3% slide in telecom operator AT&T even after it beat third-quarter revenue and profit expectations. Other telecommunications service providers fell along with AT&T. Dizard said the strong results from SpacEx may have fanned worries that it will become a more formidable competitor after a recent wireless spectrum purchase. Netflix shares sank 4.5% after the video streaming company issued a weaker-than-expected forecast for its fourth-quarter profit. Google's parent Alphabet also lost 1.6%. Abbott Laboratories fell 3.7% after the medical device maker cut its 2026 sales growth forecast. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.56-to-1 ratio on the NYSE where there were 90 new highs and 161 new lows. On the Nasdaq, 2,883 stocks rose and 1,818 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.59-to-1 ratio. The S&P 500 posted 21 new 52-week highs and 2 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 48 new highs and 168 new lows. (Reporting by Sinead Carew in New York, Purvi Agarwal and Tharuniyaa Lakshmi in Bengaluru; Editing by Maju Samuel and David Gregorio)

title: Tech giants AI spending to exceed USD 1 trillion in 2027, lift US growth: UBS
content: New Delhi [India], October 21 (ANI): Investment by major technology companies in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is expected to exceed USD 1 trillion in 2027 as demand for computing capacity continues to outstrip supply, supporting US economic growth despite rising financing needs, according to a report by UBS. The report estimates that AI-related capital expenditure by major technology companies will exceed USD 600 billion in 2026 before crossing USD 1 trillion in 2027. “Demand has exceeded capacity ahead of schedule,” the report said, noting that companies have raised their investment plans as demand for computing power continues to grow. UBS expects spending to keep rising over the next year, although the pace of growth could peak in 2027 as higher investment puts pressure on cash flows and increases the need for additional financing. AI investment has also become a significant contributor to US economic growth. UBS estimates that spending on AI infrastructure contributed around 0.75 percentage points to US GDP growth in the first half of 2026, while rising equity prices linked to AI companies provided an additional boost to household wealth and consumption. However, the report said there is still little clear evidence that AI has materially increased overall productivity or caused substantial job displacement. Its estimated impact on the overall unemployment rate remains limited, at around 0.2 percentage points or less. The effects are more visible in certain industries. Employment in selected high-technology sectors, including software and computer systems design, fell 1.4 per cent year-on-year, while construction industries supporting data centre infrastructure recorded employment growth of nearly 3 per cent. UBS also flagged emerging financing pressures as companies spend more on AI infrastructure. Cash flows at major technology companies have weakened, while demand for their bond issuances has become less robust. The report said investors expect free cash flow to return to positive territory in 2028, provided companies can generate sufficient revenue from AI services. The report added that AI demand is currently contributing to higher prices in some areas, including software, digital goods and electricity, even though productivity gains could reduce inflation over time. UBS said the outlook for the AI investment cycle will depend on whether demand continues to exceed available computing capacity and whether companies can turn their investments into sustainable revenue growth. (ANI)

title: OpenAI says its AI agents weakened internal monitoring system
content: By Carlos Méndez Oct 20 (Reuters) - OpenAI said on Tuesday that two of its AI agents weakened parts of an internal monitoring system designed to detect misbehavior, the latest case of AI agents acting in ways their developers did not intend them to. While the ChatGPT maker said the incidents happened during internal coding tasks and were not deemed its most severe, the disclosure highlights even the systems developers rely on to catch AI misbehavior are vulnerable to the agents they monitor. The disclosure also comes amid growing concerns that AI safety efforts are lagging behind the rapid development of increasingly powerful systems. Researchers have warned that advanced AI agents could become harder to monitor and control as they gain greater autonomy. Developers, including IPO-bound rivals OpenAI and Anthropic, have revealed in recent months instances of their AI agents accessing external systems without authorization. OpenAI said On Tuesday a GPT-6.1 Sol agent working on an internal testing task on October 3 suppressed automatic security alerts after deciding an earlier instruction not to send Slack messages also covered safety notifications. In a separate incident on October 6, a GPT-6 Astra agent removed a safety monitor while copying an existing piece of code and later incorrectly claimed it had not done so, OpenAI said. "In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them," the company said. OpenAI said it was making it harder for models to disable monitoring, adding that it does not "yet have a satisfying explanation for this behavior". The San Francisco-based company said it was testing whether its models might have a tendency to avoid being monitored and look for reasons to justify doing so. (Reporting by Carlos Méndez in Mexico City; Editing by Subhranshu Sahu)
