title: New UN initiative will aim to tackle the military uses of AI
content: The United Nations is launching a new initiative on the military uses of artificial intelligence, aimed at addressing some dire concerns about the threat the rapidly developing technology could pose to humanity. The initiative by the U.N. Institute for Disarmament Research plans to launch Thursday, establishing the first international forum for key players to try to tackle the issue . Robin Geiss, head of the Geneva-based institute known as UNIDIR, warned at a U.N. press conference Tuesday that “the margin for human judgment is increasingly narrow, including in the nuclear domain .” It’s difficult to assess how close the world is to machines possibly acting outside of human control , Geiss said, and that uncertainty “is the issue we’re trying to resolve here.” One problem is that AI is increasingly creeping into so many areas — early warning systems , information gathering and reconnaissance, to name a few — “and it’s quite difficult to say at which point we’re actually really losing control,” he said. For a long time, he said, there was widespread reluctance to deal with AI guardrails, but the proliferation of its capabilities and the potential impact have led to “a growing realization that we stand at a crossroad — that now is the time to act, including on military AI .” Geiss said the U.N. recognizes that global competition to lead on AI poses serious obstacles. “But concerns about AI’s impact are already transcending geopolitical blocs, and they’re prompting action from major powers,” he said, pointing to a proposal last month for the U.S. and China to set up an AI safety alert system for issues that could threaten national security. The risks posed by AI were a major topic in speeches by leaders of many of the U.N.’s 193 member nations at their annual high-level meeting last month. UNIDIR this summer established a Center of Excellence on AI, Peace and Security, the first permanent platform by the world body focused on those issues. Geiss said it received funding from all five major nuclear powers — the U.S., Russia, China, Britain and France. On Thursday, UNIDIR will launch a new forum as part of the center to bring together “actors from every relevant sector and all over the world” to work on AI in military uses. Geiss was vague on exactly what the initiative will do, but he said it will be part of other AI efforts being launched by the center this week. Another will focus on the role of industry and aims to develop “a framework for responsible industry behavior,” he said. Decisions by companies on design and development “determine whether AI-enabled military capabilities are ultimately reliable, predictable and whether they can operate in line with international law,” Geiss said. For that reason, he said, UNIDIR is developing a framework of responsible industry behavior that will “provide practical, voluntary guidelines" that follow international law and ensure human rights. The U.N. agency will hold consultations this week with defense technology companies, software developers, subcontractors, investors and others that will work alongside governments, civil society, academia and experts, Geiss said. UNIDIR also is launching an initiative focused on the risks of AI misuse by armed groups , he said, warning that such actors are already using the technology to support operational planning, execution and logistics. “The urgent issue of AI in the military domain will certainly no longer be allowed to linger in the shadows,” Geiss said. “The time has come to pull our strengths and confront AI in the military head-on.”

title: eMudhra security incident: MeitY orders probe, says impact on Indian websites and apps was limited; details here
content: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) on Wednesday, 21 October, constituted a special team to investigate a security incident involving eMudhra's Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), while maintaining that its impact on Indian websites and applications was limited. The incident came to light after concerns emerged over the compromise of eight intermediate Certificate Authority (CA) certificates associated with eMudhra . These certificates form part of the digital trust infrastructure used to authenticate websites and secure online communications. In a series of posts on X, MeitY said it had taken serious note of the incident but cautioned against fear-mongering on social media. The ministry clarified that the incident concerned eMudhra's internationally trusted digital certificate operations, which are separate from its domestic digital signature and eSign services. The ministry said the impact on Indian websites and applications had been very limited and lasted for a short interval. It added that CERT-In had issued an advisory outlining mitigation measures. What MeitY said about the eMudhra security incident According to the ministry, eMudhra operates in two distinct areas, each governed by a different regulatory framework. The first involves issuing Digital Signature Certificates (DSCs) and providing eSign services. These activities are regulated by the Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA) under MeitY. The second involves issuing digital certificates trusted by major internet browsers and operating systems. These certificates are used to secure websites, software and online communications. MeitY clarified that the reported security incident concerned only the second area of operations. This function is international in nature and operates under a global trust framework. It is governed by international standards and subject to independent audits, including WebTrust audits conducted by BDO International Limited. The ministry also clarified that it is not involved in auditing this international certificate-issuing operation. The distinction is significant because eMudhra's domestic digital signature and eSign services operate under a separate regulatory framework. The ministry did not identify these services as being affected by the reported incident. "However, some social media accounts are indulging in fear mongering about the impact of this incident," MeitY said in its statement. How were Indian websites and applications affected? MeitY said the incident had a very limited impact on Indian websites and applications, lasting only a short period. However, the ministry did not disclose the number of affected websites or applications, the precise duration of the impact, or the full technical findings of the investigation. Public Key Infrastructure is used to establish trust between websites, users and digital services through cryptographic keys and digital certificates. These certificates help browsers verify website identities and establish encrypted connections. A compromise involving certificate infrastructure can potentially undermine that trust and expose online communications to security risks. CERT-In has issued an advisory concerning the incident, outlining mitigation measures for affected systems. MeitY said it remained engaged with all stakeholders to resolve the incident at the earliest. The ministry's clarification indicates that the reported incident was confined to eMudhra's internationally trusted digital certificate operations and did not concern the company's separately regulated domestic digital signature and eSign services. However, the complete technical impact and circumstances surrounding the incident remain subject to investigation. "Further details will be shared upon completion of the investigation," the ministry said.

title: eMudhra intermediate CA certificates compromised: What happened, who is affected and what users need to know | Explained
content: CERT-In has issued a security advisory warning that eight intermediate certification authority (CA) certificates associated with eMudhra have been compromised, raising concerns about the security of encrypted internet communications and the authenticity of website certificates. The advisory, CIAD-2026-0050, issued on 21 October 2026, says the incident involves weak cryptographic private keys that could potentially allow attackers to issue fraudulent TLS certificates, impersonate legitimate websites and intercept or modify encrypted communications. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said eMudhra Limited, an India-based certification authority, reported that private keys associated with eight intermediate CA certificates in its public key infrastructure (PKI) had been compromised. The development has prompted browser vendors, including Google and Mozilla, to take steps to block the affected certificates and prevent their misuse. However, eMudhra has stated that none of the affected intermediate CAs had issued end-entity certificates and that the incident was limited to the intermediates. It also said the compromise did not involve its root CA private keys or other intermediate CAs. What happened to eMudhra's certificates? According to CERT-In, the affected private keys were generated using insufficient cryptographic randomness. The P-384 elliptic-curve private keys had exceptionally small values, making them potentially recoverable almost instantly. In a secure certificate system, private keys are meant to remain secret and computationally difficult to derive. Weaknesses in how these keys are generated can undermine that protection. An intermediate CA acts as a link between a trusted root certification authority and the certificates used by websites and other services. If an attacker obtains an intermediate CA's private key, they may be able to issue certificates that appear to come from a legitimate certification authority. Such certificates could potentially be used to impersonate websites or facilitate attacks on encrypted connections. CERT-In warned that attackers exploiting the compromised keys could intercept or modify communications, potentially exposing sensitive information such as financial data. The compromised keys could also be misused to sign malicious software, making it appear to originate from a trusted publisher. What have Google and Mozilla done? The advisory outlines measures taken by two major browser vendors to limit the risks associated with the affected certificates. Mozilla: Mozilla blocked the six affected TLS intermediate certificates through its OneCRL certificate block list. It released Firefox 158.0.1 for desktop and Android, Firefox ESR 115.45.1 and Firefox ESR 153.5.1 to protect users whose configurations prevent them from receiving OneCRL updates. Mozilla also updated the trusted certificate list in Network Security Services (NSS) 3.131.1 to remove the root certificate that signed the affected intermediates. Google: Google blocked the public keys of the affected TLS intermediates through a Certificate Revocation List Set (CRLSet) update. Google also announced the removal of emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from the Chrome Root Store, scheduled for release to living Chrome Root Store users on 27 October 2026. The changes are intended to protect applications and devices that do not receive or enforce intermediate certificate revocation information. What does this mean for ordinary internet users? TLS certificates help browsers establish encrypted connections with websites. They also help verify that users are communicating with the intended website. If the certificate system is compromised, attackers may be able to impersonate legitimate websites or interfere with encrypted communications under suitable attack conditions. However, the advisory does not establish that users' banking details, passwords or other personal information have already been stolen. It also does not say that all eMudhra certificates are compromised. The reported incident concerns eight intermediate CA certificates, with eMudhra stating that no end-entity certificates were issued by the affected intermediates. For ordinary users, the immediate precaution is to keep browsers, operating systems and applications updated so that the latest certificate restrictions and security protections are applied. What should website owners and organisations do? CERT-In has recommended several measures for organisations, website administrators and technology service providers. Install security updates: Update Firefox, Firefox ESR, other affected browsers, applications and operating systems to the latest available security releases. Update certificate trust stores: Ensure that operating systems, applications, servers and devices receive the latest certificate revocation and distrust information. Review certificate chains: Identify certificates and services that depend on the affected intermediate CAs or emSign ECC Root CA - G3. Replace affected certificates where necessary: Obtain replacement TLS certificates from an unaffected and trusted certificate hierarchy. Administrators should also replace legitimate certificates chaining to the affected root if clients will no longer trust it. Verify TLS certificates: Check certificate chains, issuers, validity periods and revocation status. CERT-In has warned against bypassing certificate validation warnings or disabling certificate verification. CERT-In has also advised organisations to monitor Certificate Transparency logs for unauthorised certificate issuance and strengthen CA key management practices through secure random number generation, hardware security modules and regular reviews. The advisory highlights how weaknesses in certificate infrastructure can create security risks beyond a single website. While browser vendors have introduced protective measures, keeping software updated and ensuring that certificate trust chains remain valid will be important for users and organisations relying on encrypted communications.

title: Elon Musk's X to pay creators ₹2.85 lakh for 15 videos in 30 days: Check eligibility, rules and deadline to enrol
content: Elon Musk-owned X, formerly known as Twitter, is testing a creator incentive programme called the Video Kickstart Bonus. Under the pilot, eligible creators will receive a fixed payment of $3,000, or around ₹ 2.85 lakh, for regularly posting original videos on the social media platform. Announcing the pilot on X, SpaceXAI's Creator Product Lead, Allegra Jacchia, said that access to the programme would be limited to invited content creators and the payout will not depend on video views or engagement. “We’re doubling down on video on X . Today, we're piloting Video Kickstart Bonus, an invite-only program that rewards creators for posting their video content here,” the executive wrote in the post. Who are eligible and the last date to enrol X has not revealed the criteria for selecting creators for the programme, thus meeting any specific follower count or view target does not guarantee an invitation from the company. Those who receive an invitation can find the programme under the Programmes section in Creator Studio, where they must enrol by October 30, 2026 if they are interested in the incentive. X will be sending out invitations over the days following the announcement, and there is no minimum view or engagement requirement to qualify for the incentive, according to Jacchia. The pilot also does not carry the conditions reported for X’s separate Original Content Rewards programme, such as a Premium subscription, 500 verified followers and 500,000 impressions. Rules eligible creators must follow Creators enroling in the Video Kickstart Bonus must meet certain requirements related to video format, originality and posting frequency. These include: Each video must be in vertical format, run for less than three minutes and must feature original content created by the participant. Also Read | OpenClaw creator turns to X after app review delay; Sundar Pichai responds Videos previously posted on other social media platforms are allowed, provided they do not carry any watermarks. Content creators must publish at least 15 videos across 15 different days within a 30-day campaign window. Posting all 15 videos on a single day will not meet the requirement. How the payout works The $3,000 bonus is a fixed payment for creators who meet the posting requirements, regardless of how many followers they have or the number of views and likes their videos receive. Also Read | Delhi content creator, 23, reveals ₹1.12 lakh monthly income This differs from X’s Original Content Rewards programme, where earnings are linked to engagement from X Premium subscribers. Creators participating in the pilot also get fast-track access to Original Content Rewards, subject to that programme’s rules. However, since the programme is still in its pilot phase, X has not announced whether it will expand access to more creators or make it available to the public.

title: iPhone 17 Pro 256GB gets a big discount: How to buy it at ₹56,990 on Reliance Digital? Check eligibility and more
content: Apple's iPhone 17 Pro, which was launched in India at ₹ 1,34,900 for the 256GB variant, is now available at an effective price of ₹ 56,990 under a promotional offer by Reliance Digital. However, buyers looking to get their hands on Apple's premium smartphone at this price will have to meet certain conditions, including exchanging an eligible old smartphone and qualifying for bank cashback. The advertised price is not a flat discount available to all customers. Instead, Reliance Digital is combining an in-store discount, an exchange value, an additional exchange bonus and bank cashback to bring down the effective cost of the device. iPhone 17 Pro price breakdown: How does it come down to ₹ 56,990? The 256GB iPhone 17 Pro carries an original retail price of ₹ 1,34,900 in India. Under the Reliance Digital offer, customers first get an in-store discount of ₹ 9,910, bringing the price down to ₹ 1,24,990. Also Read | Thought Apple was too expensive? These Great Indian Festival deals may surprise The remaining savings come through exchanging an existing smartphone, an additional exchange bonus and bank cashback. Who is eligible for the iPhone 17 Pro deal? Customers must fulfil the applicable exchange and payment conditions to get the advertised price of ₹ 56,990. The key conditions include: 1. Exchange of an old smartphone: The maximum exchange value of ₹ 55,000 in the advertised calculation is based on an iPhone 15 Pro. The value offered for other devices will vary. 2. Additional exchange bonus: Eligible customers can receive an exchange bonus of up to ₹ 10,000 over and above the exchange value. 3. Bank cashback: The offer includes cashback of up to ₹ 3,000 on eligible bank cards. Customers should check the participating banks and payment conditions at the store. Also Read | Ahead of launch, strong grey market demand for iPhone Duo 4. In-store discount: An additional discount of ₹ 9,910 is included in the advertised price calculation. 5. Final valuation: The actual amount payable will depend on the exchange assessment and eligibility for the additional benefits. Here is how the advertised effective price is calculated: Offer component Amount Original price (256GB) ₹ 1,34,900 In-store discount - ₹ 9,910 Price after in-store discount ₹ 1,24,990 Exchange value (iPhone 15 Pro) - ₹ 55,000 Additional exchange bonus - ₹ 10,000 Bank cashback - ₹ 3,000 Effective price ₹ 56,990 As the exchange valuation of ₹ 55,000 used in this calculation is based on an iPhone 15 Pro , customers trading in other smartphones may receive a different amount depending on the device's model, age and physical condition. The exchange bonus and cashback are subject to the applicable terms and conditions. Buyers should confirm the eligible bank cards, exchange valuation and final billing amount with Reliance Digital before completing the purchase. Should you buy the iPhone 17 Pro at ₹ 56,990? The advertised price could make the iPhone 17 Pro an attractive upgrade for customers who already own an eligible older iPhone and can benefit from the maximum exchange valuation. Also Read | iPhone 18 Pro vs Sony ZV-E10 II: Which is better for photography and video? However, those planning to exchange an older Android smartphone or a device in poor condition may not receive the same exchange value. The ₹ 56,990 figure should therefore be treated as an effective promotional price rather than the standard selling price. Is the iPhone 17 Pro Max also available at a discounted price? Yes, Reliance Digital is also advertising an effective price of ₹ 71,990 for the 256GB iPhone 17 Pro Max, which was originally launched in India at ₹ 1,49,900. Similar to the iPhone 17 Pro deal, the discounted price combines an in-store discount, exchange value, an additional exchange bonus and bank cashback. The exchange calculation also uses an iPhone 15 Pro as the reference device.

title: Dell's latest 14-inch laptop brings 120Hz screen and long battery life at lower starting price — details here

title: Google, Apple and Mozilla block 8 eMudhra certificates over weak keys: What users need to know
content: Google, Apple and Mozilla have blocked eight digital certificates issued by Indian certificate authority eMudhra after researchers discovered dangerously weak private keys that could allow attackers to impersonate websites. The security incident came to light on October 17, 2026, with Cloudflare confirming on October 19 at around 17:00 UTC that the compromised keys posed a serious risk to internet security. The vulnerability would enable hackers to produce fake certificates for any domain and possibly to hijack or manipulate Internet traffic. Major browsers, operating systems and internet infrastructure providers trusted the certificates. Cloudflare and other tech firms have implemented emergency patches to mitigate the danger, and developers and organisations have been urged to patch vulnerable software or security systems. eMudhra security flaw exposed dangerously weak keys Eight intermediate certificates have been issued by eMudhra in the incident. Security researcher Wayne, who brought the problem to light on October 17, said the certificates had private keys that could be compromised with just three to eight bits of effective key space. To demonstrate the problem, Wayne created a website at emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com and published a digitally signed message reading, “We have a problem here – Wayne.” The demo showcased how a malicious party with access to the keys could generate trusted certificates for websites and lull users into entering passwords, credit card numbers and other personal data. BGP.tools director Ben Cartwright-Cox termed it “bonkers” and suggested that example code could have been accidentally introduced into production systems. Also Read | Apple’s October 28 event: What to expect Google, Apple and Cloudflare roll out emergency fixes Google , Apple and Mozilla are planning to block the affected certificates in their Chrome, Safari and Firefox browsers as of October 20. In addition, Cloudflare rolled out mitigations throughout its content delivery network, developer services and Zero Trust products. Cloudflare was alerted to the stolen keys in its security update around 17:00 UTC on October 19. The company said that, through a security review, it had not identified any active exploitation of the problem on its own services. Cloudflare published updates for the Cloudflare WARP and 1.1.1.1 apps and for “cloudflared”, the Cloudflare Tunnel. It recommended that individuals update any impacted applications and organisations review their certificate trust stores and server configurations. The Go programming language maintainers also published security updates for Go 1.27.3 and Go 1.26.10, which reject the compromised keys. Why the incident could have a lasting impact Cryptography engineer Filippo Valsorda warned that cleaning up the vulnerability could be more challenging than resolving the 2014 Heartbleed bug. Other software can accept the compromised certificates and continue to trust them in the case of outdated operating systems, embedded devices, smart home products or background services. Other work was underway to remediate the issue, Cloudflare said, and some systems would require manual updates or redeployment. Also Read | ‘Cyber fraud does not respect borders’: PM Modi seeks global mechanism at IMC What users need to know Certificate transparency logs have shown no evidence, so far, that the weak keys were used to issue malicious certificates. This doesn't necessarily mean that all types of misuse are excluded. It's typically not possible to exploit certificates and impersonate a site without being positioned between the user and the real site. For everyday users, the immediate precaution is to install the latest available browser, operating system and security application updates.

title: Britain seeks to break Apples grip on contactless payments
content: By Paul Sandle LONDON, Oct 20 (Reuters) - Britain's competition regulator said on Tuesday it was seeking to loosen Apple's grip on contactless payments by proposing that the company lower fees and remove technical barriers, helping rival services compete with Apple Pay. The Competition and Markets Authority said its proposals would result in "substantially lower access fees" and easier access to Apple's contactless technology, opening the market to competition from digital banks and other providers. The proposed measures are less onerous than those imposed by the European Union in 2024, which included giving third-party wallet developers free access. Since then, companies including Vipps, PayPal, Klarna, Curve and BBVA have launched alternative payment apps, the CMA said. CMA Chief Executive Sarah Cardell said the proposals would open the door to more innovation and more choice, as well as boosting Britain's important fintech sector. "We have heard that high fees, strict terms, and technical restrictions relating to Apple's contactless technology make it too difficult for challengers to innovate and compete," she said. "By removing barriers to entry, we can help create the conditions for brilliant British businesses with great ideas to develop new products and services here - from payment apps and digital IDs to travel passes and digital keys." The CMA is consulting on the proposals until November 17, before making a final decision. Contactless payments have grown rapidly in popularity, accounting for 39% of all payments, compared with just 3% a decade ago, the CMA said. More than 60% of adults use a digital wallet, with Apple Wallet the most popular in Britain, it added. Apple said it had already made it possible for developers to offer contactless payments in their apps through NFC, which allows an iPhone to talk to a payments terminal or reader, and through its secure element, which stores sensitive material such as card credentials and cryptographic keys. The company said this allowed developers to create products and services, including in-store payments, transit passes and event tickets, while ensuring users' sensitive data remained protected by the highest security standards. "We do not believe the CMA should require Apple to adopt an approach with lower privacy and security protections," an Apple spokesperson said. "We will continue to engage constructively to reach an outcome that is in the best interest of our users." (Reporting by Paul Sandle; editing by William James)

title: Enterprise software costs threaten AI investment, innovation as firms spend 28% of budgets on unwanted changes: Report
content: New Delhi [India], October 20 (ANI): Large enterprises may face growing constraints on innovation and artificial intelligence (AI) investments as vendor-driven software upgrades, migrations and licensing changes consume an average of 28 per cent of their software budgets, according to a report by Origina published in collaboration with Thinkers50. The research found that vendor-driven costs had made a major contribution to decisions to slow, pause or cancel AI or data programmes for 34 per cent of respondents, while 56 per cent said the costs had a moderate contribution. The findings highlight how recurring software expenses could limit enterprises' ability to redirect resources towards technology development, hiring and security. The survey of 2,018 senior IT decision-makers in the United States and the United Kingdom found that 95 per cent of respondents said their organisations had paid for a vendor-driven upgrade, migration or licensing change in the past three years that they believed would reduce performance, reliability or business value. More than half, or 53 per cent, said this had happened more than once. The most recent vendor-driven change cost respondents' organisations an average of USD 12.87 million, according to the report. Innovation was the budget most frequently identified as being affected by these costs, followed by hiring and security, indicating that the financial burden extends beyond software expenditure. Tomás O'Leary, CEO and Founder of Origina and co-author of the report, said organisations often had little practical choice but to accept unwanted upgrades when the alternative was losing support for business-critical systems. The report also found that 78 per cent of IT leaders believed their primary software vendor, rather than their organisation, determined the timing and terms of changes, while 76 per cent reported having little negotiating leverage with major vendors. The consequences also extend to engineering resources and hardware. Around 84 per cent of respondents said senior engineering talent always or often spent time on vendor-driven upgrades instead of developing future capabilities. Additionally, 91 per cent said their organisations had scrapped functional hardware in the past three years solely to meet a software vendor's support deadline, resulting in an average loss of 1.65 years of useful hardware life. Marshall Van Alstyne, Professor at Boston University and co-author of the report, said organisations should negotiate exit options before entering vendor relationships, adding that the ability to leave could strengthen their negotiating position even if they chose to remain. The report also found support for regulatory intervention, with 91 per cent of respondents favouring legislation providing enterprise software customers protections comparable to those in long-term residential rental relationships. (ANI)

title: Deepinder Goyal’s Temple wearable pre-orders open November 1: How to order, expected price, colours and features
content: Temple, the wearable device associated with Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal, will open pre-orders on November 1, 2026, according to an email sent to people who registered for early access. The device is meant to monitor optical sensors for changes in cerebral blood flow. It is designed to assess physiological strain beyond the common fitness measures. The company has already announced six colours for the launch edition but hasn't given any official price or quantity information. The first batch of the product will be produced based on customer needs and will be ordered on a first-come, first-served basis. The company sent out an early-access email announcing that pre-orders will begin on November 1. The company has not announced a shipping date yet, although it has stated that deliveries will be completed by the end of 2026. Temple wearable: How does it work? The temple is a small piece attached to the side of the head between the forehead and the ear. It measures changes in brain blood flow, known as BrainFlow, using its optical sensors. The wearable also measures a score from 1 to 250, known as 'entropy', to assess physiological strain. Goyal shared that factors such as rest, stress, exercise, and caffeine can affect the score. This device is for wellness and research and is not intended to diagnose medical conditions. Also Read | Deepinder Goyal’s Temple wearable could cost ₹1 lakh: What makes this unusual Temple features and how to wear them The single-use adhesive tapes that Temple uses, called Grips, attach to the skin. Each grip is expected to maintain its stretch for approximately 7 days, but the company suggests replacing it every 2 to 3 days, especially when sweating or exposed to dust. Goyal has revealed that the wearable will be used during physical activities, such as running and jumping. He states it can also be worn in the shower or while swimming. It is designed to fit under glasses in order to achieve a slim profile. Temple colours and expected price The launch edition will be released in 6 colours: True Gold, Rose Gold, Black Mirror, Real Jade, Deep Blue and Purple Funk. Limited edition options include Real Jade, Deep Blue, and Purple Funk. The official price is not yet announced. Goyal has reportedly indicated a price of around $1,000, equivalent to approximately Rs. 1 lakh, although an earlier estimate placed it closer to Rs. 72,000. Also Read | Apple’s October 28 event: What to expect What could Temple be used for? There are potential applications in sports and performance monitoring from the analysis of fatigue, recovery and physiological responses to training undertaken by Temple . Goyal has also spoken about its use in aviation and defence, such as evaluating an aviator's suitability for flying. At present, the wearable is a product geared toward health and research. The last details to watch are its final price, initial availability, and confirmed delivery timelines, as it comes with pre-orders on November 1, 2026.

content: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rocky Swift A rocky start for a South Korean startup cast a shadow over highly anticipated announcements by AI hyperscalers this week. title: Nvidia CEO urges German manufacturers to adopt AI, saying digital tech wont replace heavy industry
content: FRANKFURT, Germany (AP) — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang urged Germany's makers of cars and industrial machines to quickly adopt artificial intelligence to “re-engineer” the country's struggling business model by tapping its wealth of manufacturing data and expertise. Huang, whose company designs the powerful computer chips and software used by companies like Anthropic and OpenAI to develop AI applications, said that digital technology would never replace manufacturing and the engineering world of cars and robots where Germany has vast experience. Or, as he put it, “electrons will never replace atoms.” But he said industry would benefit by leaning into technology. “The next wave of AI is physical. This is where AI interacts with the physical world: robotics, manufacturing, cars, heavy industry,” Huang said Monday during a discussion with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz at an investment conference in Berlin. "And so AI can only augment your capability. It will not replace your capability. So take advantage of the technology." Huang said Germany's data and expertise on manufacturing “is your natural resource, it belongs to the nation" but it needs to take better advantage of AI. "This industrial revolution is so mighty, so powerful. You don't have another chance,” he said. European leaders like Merz are looking to AI as a potential source of growth but are also concerned about the extent of European dependence on U.S. tech companies in the field. Europe's wealth of high quality public-sector and machine-readable manufacturing data could serve as grist for AI, an opportunity cited by former European Central Bank head Mario Draghi as an area where Europe could compete with the U.S. and China in the AI field. Huang and Merz said AI was an opportunity for Germany's so-called “mittelstand,” the hundreds of small- and medium-sized companies in highly specialized industrial sectors. Merz is struggling to revive growth in Germany after years of near-stagnation after the pandemic. Among the economy's headwinds are high energy prices after losing cheap Russian natural gas due to the invasion of Ukraine , competition from China in sectors like autos where Germany once dominated, and excessive red tape and permissions that hold up projects for years. All that has put a damper on an economy heavily oriented toward building complicated machines for export, including cars, trains, aircraft and factory equipment. Europe lags the U.S. in building out the data centers that offer the massive computing capacity to train artificial intelligence applications, and faces concerns over the security of European companies' sensitive data against subpoenas and criminal warrants on servers owned by U.S. companies and thus exposed to the U.S. legal system even if they're in Europe. Huang appeared to address such concerns by urging Germany to import AI technology but adding that “you should not export your culture, export your values, export your knowledge." Huang said Germany should “take advantage of artificial intelligence. Let them codify, let them program, let them teach this artificial intelligence and keep it here in Germany, and let's re-engineer, the chancellor's words, Germany. This is your chance to do it.”

title: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of bugging conference room planned to fly to Saudi Arabia, prosecutors say
content: SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — A former OpenAI engineer charged with secretly installing a recording device in a conference room to glean company details had been “mere days” away from absconding to Saudi Arabia before his arrest, federal prosecutors said in new court filings. Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national, was also fired from his job at the ChatGPT maker , according to a government memo filed Sunday. His wife and young son left the country the day after his arrest on a one-way ticket booked and paid for by a Saudi military official, prosecutors said in the filing. “Ultimately, the defendant has little incentive to remain in the United States to see this case through,” federal prosecutors wrote. “He has ample resources —including his significant compensation from a decade of high-tech employment in the Bay Area and at least two bank accounts in Saudi Arabia — and what appears to be considerable support from a foreign government.” Prosecutors also noted Saudi Arabia has no extradition treaty with the U.S. as they seek to detain Alfozan until trial. A judge will consider the request Monday in federal court in San Francisco. Alfozan’s lawyers didn’t immediately respond to an email seeking comment ahead of Monday’s hearing. But in their own court filings, they argued that Alfozan, who had worked at OpenAI since July 2025, had purchased one-way tickets for his family to Saudi Arabia more than two weeks before prosecutors allege the recording devices were installed. The defense said the couple planned to spend Alfozan’s roughly two-month paternity leave in Saudi Arabia following the birth of their U.S.-citizen son. Prosecutors say after his arrest, Saudi officials purchased new plane tickets for the wife and son to leave the U.S. sooner than the Oct. 12 flight Alfozan initially booked. Alfozan’s lawyers also argued that he was on track to become a naturalized U.S. citizen with an interview with federal officials scheduled next month. They said he has been a legal permanent resident since 2020, has lived in the U.S. for 15 years and attended MIT and the University of California, Berkeley. “This was a long-held dream for the Alfozan family, as it is for so many immigrants,” his lawyers wrote. “His plan was always to return to the Bay Area, where his home, his career, and his community are.” Rather than remain in federal custody, Alfozan’s lawyers argue he should be confined to his family’s home in the San Francisco suburbs, with GPS monitoring, travel restrictions and a requirement to surrender his passport. Prosecutors have not said what Alfozan might have wanted to do with the recordings, but say he was in “frequent communication” with a member of the Saudi royal family. They said the royal family member repeatedly tried to recruit Alfozan to an artificial intelligence venture being launched in Saudi Arabia. Alfozan told the unnamed person in WhatsApp messages that he wouldn’t leave OpenAI until his stock was vested, even as he explored other career opportunities in the Middle Eastern kingdom, prosecutors wrote. Prosecutors say Alfozan concealed an audio recording device in toilet paper and plugged it into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room he wasn't authorized to access. They say security cameras captured him entering the room and checking behind the television after installing the device. It remained there for several days before being found Sept. 30. Prosecutors say the conference room was typically used for meetings involving company leaders, government officials and other executives and “discussions of highly confidential technical, commercial, and strategic information, including proprietary research, as well as nonpublic information.” OpenAI has said the recording device Alfozan used was sophisticated, designed to evade detection and featured advanced encryption and audio-monitoring capabilities. They also said they had evidence Alfozan planned to place other listening devices elsewhere in the office. Alfozan has been charged with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. If convicted, he faces a five-year prison sentence. __ Marcelo reported from New York.

title: iPhone 18 Pro vs Sony ZV-E10 II: Which should you buy for photography and content creation? All features explained
content: Looking for a camera and confused whether you should go for the best smartphone camera or just a camera with all the features a professional needs? We've got you covered as we bring to you a comparison between the Apple iPhone 18 Pro and Sony's ZV-E10 Mark II. Features Sensor : iPhone 18 Pro comes with multiple camera sensors and does computational image processing. The Sony ZV-E10 II has an approximately 26MP APS-C sensor. Camera system : The iPhone has three rear cameras while the Sony ZV-E10 II has one camera body with interchangeable E-mount lenses. Focal lengths : The iPhone comes with a 13mm ultra-wide, a 24mm main, and a 100mm telephoto focal length. On the other hand the focal length of the Sony ZV-E10 II depends on the lens you attach. Also Read | iPhone Duo preorders sell out in minutes: How it compares with iPhone 18 Pro Max Image quality : The iPhone provides computational processing that produces polished, ready-to-share images. The Sony has a large sensor that offers greater potential for detail and tonal control. Dynamic range : Apple Log 2 supports greater flexibility in video grading while Sony's larger sensor offers strong dynamic-range potential. Low-light performance : The iPhone's processing power can brighten scenes and produce attractive results. However, Sony's larger sensor can capture more light if paired with a suitable lens and settings. Video stabilisation : The iPhone is the best for video stabilisation, which is one of its major strengths. The Sony camera's active stabilisation is not as effective in certain situations. Ease of use : The iPhone is much easier to use when compared with the Sony ZV-E10 II. The iPhone can quickly capture and process the image, making it ready for sharing. However, the Sony camera has more settings and equipment choices that hve to be managed. Best use cases for both devices Everyday photography : The iPhone is convenient for every photographs like street photography, travel, family events, and social media. It beats the Sony ZV-E10 II in this regard. Professional work : The APS-C sensor and interchangeable lenses of the Sony ZV-E10 II give greater control over depth of field, lens character, exposure, and framing, thus making it the device to use when it comes to professional photographers. Vlogging and handheld video : The iPhone, with its impressive image stabilisation and ease of carrying around wins this round. The Sony can need a gimbal or other forms of stabilisation support for vlogging. Also Read | iPhone 18 Pro Max vs Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: Full specifications compared Which one should you pick? The device you end up buying depends on your requirements. If you need one easy-to-carry device that will constantly give you good quality images and also help in quick video recording without much hassle, opt for the iPhone 18 Pro. However, if you need a more dedicated camera for content creation, or are a professional photographer who needs more control over lenses, depth of field, and image character, the Sony ZV-E10 should be your device of choice.

title: AI agents can pose insider security risks even without being hacked: Microsoft
content: New Delhi [India], October 19 (ANI): Artificial intelligence (AI) agents deployed within companies could pose significant internal security risks even without being compromised by hackers, Microsoft has warned, calling for continuous monitoring of autonomous AI systems as their use across enterprises grows. In a blog post titled "Securing the agentic insider" published on Monday, Hayete Gallot, Executive Vice President, Microsoft Security, said organisations have traditionally focused on external cyber threats while placing implicit trust in AI agents deployed within their own systems. "Agents are unpredictable. They will adapt as the context changes, may not behave as intended and will collaborate and collude with other agents to reach their objectives, without needing to be compromised," Gallot stated. Microsoft warned that AI agents increasingly have access to sensitive corporate data, tools and systems, allowing them to make decisions and take actions in critical business processes. The company described these autonomous systems as "agentic insiders", highlighting the security risks arising from their growing role within organisations. "These agents are frequently overprivileged, have access to data, tools and systems and can take actions and make decisions in critical processes. They have become active participants in the enterprise," Gallot said. The warning comes as companies increasingly use AI agents to automate business operations and decision-making, raising concerns about how organisations can maintain oversight of systems capable of acting independently. Microsoft argued that securing these agents requires continuous supervision across identity, permissions, data, networks, cloud infrastructure and operating environments. "Monitoring and securing those agents must become continuous. We need to understand in real time what the agents are doing and what risks those actions create, and we need to adjust their ability to act accordingly," Gallot stated. To address these risks, Microsoft highlighted its Project Perception initiative, announced in July, which uses AI-driven security systems to help organisations detect and respond to cyber threats. The company said the same technology could be used to supervise internal AI agents through so-called Guardian Agents, which monitor their actions and intervene when risks increase. Microsoft also emphasised the need for greater transparency into how AI models make decisions, arguing that security systems must understand not only what agents are doing but also why they are taking particular actions. "Model transparency will not replace containment. It will make containment smarter and stronger," Gallot said. (ANI)

title: WhatsApp tests new Android navigation bar design: What is changing and how will it help users?
content: Meta Platforms-owned WhatsApp is testing another design change for its upcoming Android navigation bar, replacing the existing pill-shaped highlight with a circular indicator behind the selected tab. The update is part of the messaging platform’s ongoing efforts to refine its interface, reported Gizbot . The redesigned navigation bar remains under development and is not yet available to regular users or beta testers. The change was spotted in WhatsApp beta for Android version 2.26.41.7, where the circular selection indicator appears within the experimental floating bottom navigation bar. The latest adjustment suggests that WhatsApp is continuing to evaluate different visual styles before deciding on the final design for Android users. Also Read | Zoho targeting WhatsApp Business with Arattai for Business? Here’s what we know WhatsApp experiments with floating navigation bar WhatsApp has been testing a redesigned bottom navigation bar with rounded corners, replacing the traditional full-width layout. Earlier experimental versions introduced a floating bar intended to give the interface a cleaner appearance. The company also tested a version without text labels, leaving icons for key sections such as Chats, Updates, Communities and Calls. The latest change focuses on how the currently selected section is highlighted. In the earlier design, a pill-shaped background extended horizontally behind the active tab. In the newer version, a green circular indicator appears behind the selected icon, creating a more compact visual highlight. Although the adjustment is relatively small, it changes how users distinguish the active section from the other navigation options. Circular highlight could improve visual clarity The circular indicator keeps the selection highlight close to the icon, while the pill-shaped design spreads it across a wider area. The newer treatment could help reduce visual clutter and give the navigation bar a more streamlined appearance. The design also appears closer to the selection style used in WhatsApp’s iOS interface, potentially indicating an effort to create a more consistent experience across platforms. However, the company has not officially confirmed whether cross-platform consistency is the reason behind the change. The active-tab indicator could become more important if WhatsApp proceeds with removing text labels from the navigation bar. Without labels, users would rely more heavily on familiar icons and visual cues to identify their current section. A clearly visible selection marker could help users switch between chats, calls, updates and communities without confusion. Why the redesign matters for Android users WhatsApp is widely used in India, where users regularly move between conversations, voice and video calls, and status updates. Even minor interface changes can influence how easily people navigate the application. A floating navigation bar could make the interface appear lighter and potentially improve its visual organisation. Removing labels could also free up screen space, although users unfamiliar with the icons might initially need time to adjust. The circular indicator is therefore more than a cosmetic adjustment. It could play a greater role in helping users understand the navigation structure if the company adopts an icon-only design. Also Read | WhatsApp Business Platform charges from 1 October: 1,000 free service messages Release date remains unconfirmed WhatsApp has not announced an official release date for the redesigned Android navigation bar. The feature remains experimental, and its appearance or functionality could change before it reaches beta testers or users of the stable version. WhatsApp frequently tests multiple interface variations before deciding whether to introduce a feature more widely. The circular highlight should therefore not be treated as the final design. Users are advised to obtain updates through official channels, including Google Play, rather than downloading modified applications claiming to unlock unreleased features. Unofficial builds can pose privacy and security risks. For now, the latest test indicates that WhatsApp is continuing to fine-tune its Android interface. If the redesign is eventually rolled out, users could see a floating bottom bar with rounded edges, icon-based navigation and a green circular marker identifying the active tab.
