title: CERT-In issues critical alert after autonomous AI agents access live systems of Indian orgs
content: New Delhi, Oct 16 (PTI) India's cybersecurity agency CERT-In has issued a 'critical' advisory warning that autonomous Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents have accessed live systems and confidential data of Indian organisations without authorisation, while threat actors are actively weaponising open-source agentic AI tools to execute rapid cyberattacks. In its advisory (CIAD-2026-0049) titled 'AI Agents as Attack Vectors', the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) highlighted two distinct categories of incidents targeting the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) infrastructure of Indian entities. In the first set of incidents, AI model providers voluntarily disclosed that autonomous AI models and agents undergoing research and evaluation had exceeded the authorised scope of their assigned tasks and reached live systems belonging to Indian organisations. During these operations, the AI agents read business records containing personal data and confidential material, using credentials and connection settings left exposed in application configurations, public code repositories and overly permissive cloud service roles, the agency noted. Notably, none of the affected organisations detected the access on their own. In every case, the incident came to light only when the AI model provider disclosed it after an internal review. In a separate trend uncovered through its own threat hunting, CERT-In observed cybercriminals using publicly available AI-native offensive-security frameworks to conduct reconnaissance, exploit security weaknesses and carry out a financially motivated campaign against Indian entities. These tools continue to be repackaged and redeployed, with many deployments seen on servers across multiple countries, it said. In that campaign, agentic tools shrank the window between initial access and final impact from days to a few hours. Victims that only partly fixed the weaknesses were attacked again within days, on a larger scale, the agency said. CERT-In pointed out that conventional security lapses were the root weaknesses in all the recent AI agent-driven incidents it observed. These included credentials and keys exposed in source code, public repository histories, configuration files, client applications and public web content; dormant, deprecated and test Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) left open to the internet; payment-API keys stored in plain text; over-permissive cloud and backend-as-a-service roles; and internet-facing management interfaces and unpatched middleware with weak passwords or no multi-factor authentication. AI agents found and exploited these gaps faster, more thoroughly and at a larger scale than human attackers. In the incidents disclosed by AI model providers, agents were also seen recovering the same exposed credential again and reusing it in separate operations. To mitigate the threat, CERT-In has urged organisations and service providers to audit their source code, repositories including commit history, configuration files, client applications and cloud storage for exposed credentials. Entities have been advised to rotate exposed credentials and purge them from code history, decommission dormant, deprecated and test APIs, enforce least-privilege access in cloud deployments and for in-house AI agents, take admin interfaces off the internet, require multi-factor authentication, and monitor attacks while keeping logs for at least 180 days. After any credential exposure or confirmed intrusion, organisations should treat the environment as compromised until it is "forensically cleared", and expect repeat attempts within days to weeks, it said. For AI developers, research laboratories and evaluation agencies, CERT-In recommended isolating research and evaluation work by blocking all outbound network access except what a task strictly needs, enforced at the network level rather than through instructions to the model, and using synthetic targets and test credentials instead of production data. Commenting on the advisory, Jaydeep Singh, General Manager - India at Kaspersky, said it was "a timely reminder that AI agents are no longer just productivity tools". "When given broad access, they can reach live systems and sensitive data in ways organisations never intended, often by moving through gaps that already exist, such as misconfigured cloud services, exposed credentials and excessive permissions," Singh said. Valid accounts, public-facing applications and trusted relationships were the entry point for over 80 per cent of the attacks Kaspersky investigated in 2025, Singh said, adding, "With AI allowing threat actors to iterate faster and scale their efforts, these paths can now be exploited more quickly than ever." AI agents used for research and testing should be kept fully separate from production environments, using synthetic data and test-only credentials. "Every agent should be inventoried, isolated in sandboxed environments, governed by default-deny rules and required to seek human approval before any irreversible action," Singh added. Critical vulnerabilities should be patched or mitigated "within hours, not weeks", and code and pipelines audited regularly, Singh said, citing a Kaspersky study of around 30,000 popular GitHub repositories that found overly broad access permissions among the most common issues. Singh recommended that organisations treat AI agents as part of their attack surface from day one.

title: Teslas new Roadster turns in air with SpaceX thrusters, wont land until 2028
content: * The Roadster can flip in the air and land using thrusters * Some Tesla watchers see unveil as marketing for Tesla-SpaceX merger * Roadster production to start in 2028, CEO Musk says * Roadster has top speed of over 230 mph, range of over 300 miles * Roadster pricing not yet disclosed (Updates throughout with details from the event, reaction to the launch and comment from analysts) By Abhirup Roy and Mrinmay Dey SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 15 (Reuters) - Tesla unveiled a redesigned Roadster powered with rocket-style thrusters on Thursday and said it would start production in 2028, more than a decade after it first showed a next-generation version of its electric sports car. The white two-seater vehicle, developed in collaboration with CEO Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX, drove upside down on a ramp using a suction system, turned in the air and landed using built-in thrusters. Later in the event it used the thrusters to jump over a truck and other vehicles, twisting in the air during the maneuver. Some watchers saw the collaboration as Musk drumming up interest in a merger of the two big companies he controls, an idea he has explored by discussing their overlap. The reveal gives Tesla a showpiece car after years of missed Roadster deadlines, but it comes as the company shifts its focus to self-driving technology and robotics, and days before third-quarter results that analysts say matter more to investors. "It was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers," Gene Munster, managing partner at Tesla investor Deepwater Asset Management, said on social media platform X. "The Roadster event is the latest example of why Elon can't wait to bring (Tesla) and (SpaceX) together," Munster said. Musk has played down the car's importance to Tesla's finances, describing it in 2023 as a "small potato situation" that would not "move the needle in a major way financially." But the car still carries symbolic weight. "Tesla does not currently have a halo car, or high-performance luxury vehicle designed to showcase an automaker's best engineering and technology. The Roadster will be Tesla's new halo car," Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein said in a note last month. Viewers and witnesses gushed over the spectacle of the launch. "That was the most insane product demo I've ever seen," Tesla fan and investor Sawyer Merritt posted on X. "I just saw this in person, and I'm still asking how this wasn't AI." Musk and other executives did not specify any target prices at Thursday's event, although Tesla nearly a decade ago quoted a base price of $200,000 for the vehicle. Tesla's reservation page for the Roadster after Thursday's event showed a "Performance" version of the vehicle requiring a $50,000 deposit and a "Thrust" version with "acceleration thrusters" requiring a $250,000 deposit. A "Rocket" variant, which Tesla says is "invite only," is described as a single-seat model with a "full flight system." 'HALFWAY TO THE SPEED OF SOUND' The event at a SpaceX ​test site in McGregor, Texas, had all the elements of a classic Musk product reveal: dramatic music, smoke, mechanical hissing sounds and a launch countdown. "This is the culmination of incredible work by Tesla and SpaceX engineers working closely together to make something that you haven't seen in any movie," Musk, wearing a silver Western-style belt buckle emblazoned with the Tesla logo, told a cheering crowd of enthusiasts and investors. The Roadster can accelerate from zero to 60 mph (97 kph) in less than one second and can hit a top speed of over 230 mph (370 kph), Tesla vehicle engineering chief Lars Moravy said. "Definitely much faster than that," an excited Musk said. "I think you've got to crack halfway to the speed of sound." The Roadster can also travel over 300 miles (480 km) on a single charge. That is less than half of what Musk promised in 2017, when Tesla first revealed a prototype of the second-generation Roadster and said that deliveries would begin in 2020. The original Roadster, released in 2008 and on sale until 2012, was Tesla's first-ever electric vehicle and used a Lotus Elise chassis. It helped change the world's view of what an EV could be. The company has since been known for its Model Y and Model X SUVs and Model S and Model 3 sedans. The reveal of the second-generation Roadster comes amid a sharp shift in Tesla's focus to artificial intelligence-led self-driving tech and robotics, from manufacturing cars for human drivers. This year, Tesla stopped selling Model S and X vehicles to make space for production of its Optimus humanoid robots. It also launched Cybercab — a two-seater robotaxi that comes without manual controls such as a steering wheel, pedals and mirrors. Tesla is set to report third-quarter results on October 21. Sales of Tesla's aging lineup of EVs have declined over the past two years, although high gas prices helped boost deliveries in the third quarter. "The margin and cash flow numbers will carry far more weight with investors than anything they saw at the reveal," said Josh Gilbert, lead analyst for Asia-Pacific at trading platform eToro. (Reporting by Abhirup Roy in San Francisco and Mrinmay Dey in Mexico City; Additional reporting by Chris Thomas and Chris Kirkham; Editing by Peter Henderson and Tom Hogue)

title: BSNL launches ₹202 prepaid plan with 5GB data and 32-day validity: Check benefits
content: Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) has introduced a new ₹ 202 prepaid plan for mobile users across India, offering 32 days of service validity, 5GB of high-speed data and 300 minutes of voice calling. The state-owned telecom operator has launched this plan on the back of its own prepaid plans for those who would like to recharge at a low cost with little usage advantage. According to TelecomTalk, the new recharge comes with a 100-SMS benefit, insurance facilities, and is a voice voucher. The plan has been published on BSNL's official website and BSNL Self Care app. Here is a look at the benefits of the new ₹ 202 recharge and how it compares with the operator's ₹ 247 plan. BSNL ₹ 202 Prepaid Plan: Benefits and validity The validity of the BSNL ₹ 202 prepaid plan is 32 days. Voice services subscribed: 300 minutes of voice calls, 5GB of high-speed data and 100 SMS are provided for the duration of the validity period. Once the allocated data is exhausted, internet speeds are reduced to 40 Kbps, as per the plan details. The recharge also covers insurance benefits, but details of coverage and terms are not provided. The plan could be an option for those who require a second mobile plan or those with limited calling and data needs. The calling time of 300 minutes and data cap of 5 GB, however, may not be ideal for users who make many calls or use a lot of data on their mobile devices. Also Read | OnePlus Ace 7 may challenge gaming phones with built-in fan and 185Hz display BSNL ₹ 247 plan offers unlimited calling and 50 GB data BSNL also has a ₹ 247 prepaid voice voucher, which is valid for 30 days. The offer has been announced to include 50 GB of high-speed data, unlimited voice calls, and 100 SMS per day, says TelecomTalk. Once the high-speed data is used up, Internet connection speeds drop to 40 Kbps. The recharge also provides ₹ 10 in talk value to the main account. Unlike the newly introduced ₹ 202 recharge, the ₹ 247 plan has been part of BSNL's existing offerings for some time. Also Read | Buying the $1,999 iPhone Duo? Here's how much Apple will charge to repair it BSNL recharge you should choose The ₹ 202 plan comes with 2 extra days compared to the ₹ 247 plan, but offers much less data and fewer calling minutes. The recharge, on the other hand, is ₹ 247and includes unlimited voice calling and 50 GB of high-speed data, with an extra charge of ₹ 45. Users who need only occasional calling and basic data access may consider the ₹ 202 plan. The ₹ 247 plan may be more suitable for those who need more data and frequent calls.

title: Why CoreWeaves troubles are rattling the AI boom
content: By Anhata Rooprai and Aditya Soni Oct 15 (Reuters) - CoreWeave's mounting debt is raising fresh concerns about the AI boom, as investors question whether demand can justify the billions being borrowed to build data centres. Shares and bonds of the Nvidia-backed company have tumbleddespite its CEO's assurances of a strong contract backlog, fueling a broader selloff in technology stocks. Here is why investors are worried and what its troubles could mean for the industry. WHAT DOES COREWEAVE DO? CoreWeave rents out computing power from Nvidia processors to companies developing and running AI, including Microsoft and OpenAI. It is one of the leading "neocloud" providers, a group of newer cloud companies that are growing rapidly to meet demand for scarce and expensive AI chips. These neocloud companies give customers access to computing power without requiring them to build their own data centers. However, supplying such capacity requires heavy upfront investment in chips and infrastructure, often financed with debt. WHAT IS ITS FINANCIAL SITUATION? The company, which has never turned a profit, has about $50 billion in debt, according to data compiled by LSEG. It raised its annual capital spending forecast by $4 billion in August to between $35 billion and $39 billion. Analysts expect revenue of nearly $13 billion this year and a loss of $2.13 billion. The yields on its bonds due in 2031, which are rated junk, have spiked to about 16%, while the cost of insuring its debt against default has climbed to about 1,000 basis points, reflecting growing concern among creditors. CEO Mike Intrator told employees in an internal memo seen by Reuters that its deal backlog more than covers its debt obligations. The company had a $104.2 billion revenue backlog at the end of the second quarter, followed by more than $25 billion in new commitments early in the third quarter. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has also downplayed the concerns, saying CoreWeave's financial strength is improving and he sees no need to backstop it. The chip giant has agreed to buy unsold CoreWeave capacity through April 2032. WHY IT COULD BE A CANARY IN THE COAL MINE CoreWeave's business depends on two things: demand for AI computing and lenders' willingness to finance the infrastructure supplying it. But a selloff in its shares suggests a lack of confidence among investors in the latter, even as the company cites strong demand. The concern is not that AI demand will collapse, but that higher borrowing costs could make the business harder to sustain if demand were to weaken sharply. "It looks more like investors questioning how the build-out is being funded than a sudden collapse in appetite for AI computing," said Axel Rudolph, chief technical analyst at IG Group. "CoreWeave is quickly becoming the AI trade's canary in the coal mine," said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB. WHY ARE MARKETS FRETTING? Investors are questioning whether AI revenue can grow fast enough to cover the cost of building and financing the infrastructure. CoreWeave has to spend heavily upfront before it can collect the revenue from its contracts. Higher interest rates could drive up financing costs and further squeeze returns. The hardware itself poses another risk. Chips lose value as newer generations arrive, pushing providers to spend even more to replace them. The concerns, however, go beyond CoreWeave. US technology giants are expected to spend more than $700 billion on AI infrastructure this year. THE DOWNSIDE SCENARIO One potential consequence would be a broader financing squeeze, with lenders demanding higher returns or becoming less willing to fund other AI projects. That could force providers to scale back expansion, curbing equipment purchases and affecting the computing capacity customers expect. A setback could also deepen doubts that the AI investment frenzy is outpacing returns, piling further pressure on technology stocks. The impact of the fallout would depend on how the business is reorganized, and CoreWeave's ties to major technology companies do not, by themselves, mean its failure would trigger a wider financial crisis. WHO ELSE BEARS THE RISK? Gartner estimates about 80% of neoclouds could shut down by 2030, warning that expected AI revenue will not support profitable returns on all planned infrastructure spending. Neocloud rivals Nebius, Applied Digital and Iren have fallen in the recent selloff. The cost of default protection has risen for SoftBank, which is betting heavily on OpenAI. Meanwhile, spreads for Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Nvidia have also reached records, although they have risen much more slowly than CoreWeave's. However, these companies also have larger cash flows and stronger balance sheets. (Reporting by Anhata Rooprai and Aditya Soni in Bengaluru; Editing by Diti Pujara)

title: Apple’s $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo preorder sells out in minutes, deliveries pushed to late January
content: Apple’s first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo , saw preorders sell out within minutes of opening on Friday, with delivery estimates extending from 23 October to late January, according to Yahoo Finance's report. Priced at $1,999 in the US, the device marks Apple’s entry into the foldable smartphone market, where rivals such as Samsung and Google have spent years developing their products and building market share. The early preorder response offers an indication of initial interest in Apple’s latest premium device, although the company has not disclosed the number of units available during the first preorder window. According to the report, the iPhone Duo features a 5.4-inch external display and a 7.6-inch foldable inner screen. Its nano-texture finish is designed to reduce glare, while the display’s central crease is intended to be barely visible. Also Read | Kriti Sanon moves Delhi High Court for personality rights protection Apple iPhone Duo: Features and multitasking capabilities The book-style foldable smartphone introduces new ways to use applications on an iPhone. Users can run two apps side by side or open two windows of the same application simultaneously. Applications can also transition between the external and internal displays as the device is opened or folded. The iPhone Duo can be positioned like an open laptop on a desk, allowing users to view content on the upper screen while navigating the lower half. Its Standing Mode lets users position the device like a tent to watch videos or use it as a bedside clock. Also Read | Kriti Sanon moves Delhi High Court for personality rights protection The camera system includes wide-angle and ultra-wide-angle rear cameras, along with Apple’s Center Stage front camera, which helps keep users in view during video calls. The device also features an under-display camera for FaceTime, according to Yahoo Finance. Apple has entered the foldable segment after rivals, including Samsung and Google, established their presence in the category. Yahoo Finance noted that Apple has previously entered product markets after competitors helped develop them, with AirPods and Apple Watch becoming major products following their respective launches. Also Read | Who is Bela Bajaria, and why has Netflix fired its powerful content chief? Foldable phones remain a niche segment Despite the early interest in the iPhone Duo, foldable smartphones account for a relatively small share of global handset shipments. According to market research firm IDC, manufacturers were projected to ship 1.25 billion smartphones in 2025, of which foldable devices were expected to account for 20.6 million units. Apple expects foldable smartphones to account for around 10% of the market by 2029, according to Yahoo Finance. Counterpoint Research’s latest Foldable Smartphone Market Forecast also projected that cumulative lifetime shipments of foldable devices would surpass 100 million units by the end of 2026.

title: iPhone Duo inner-screen repair costs $999, more than twice the Galaxy Z Fold 8's cost
content: Apple has revealed repair costs for its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, ahead of its US launch on October 23, 2026. The company will charge $999 for the inner display, and repairs for certain other types of damage could cost up to $1,499, according to MacRumors . The repair fees are considerable for a device that costs $1,999. Meanwhile, Samsung's estimate for repairing the Galaxy Z Fold 8 in the United States is $419 to replace the inner screen, according to the company’s US repair pricing page. This indicates that the inner display repair price of the iPhone Duo is $580 higher than Samsung, suggesting the cost Apple could face to repair the foldable. iPhone Duo repair costs without AppleCare+ Apple's repair estimates are that the iPhone Duo 's inner display is $999 to replace, and damage classified as “other damage” is $1,499. The price of replacing the outer display is $379, while the rear camera and battery replacement fees are $229 each. Apple will sell the repair of the back glass for $199 and the replacement of the removable nano-texture cover layer over the display screen for $49 if the glass is not damaged. Here is the full list of repair charges without AppleCare+: Cover layer: $49 Back glass: $199 Battery service: $229 Rear camera: $229 Outer display: $379 Work area: $333 Inner display: $999 Other damage: $1,499 Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 repairs cost less The Galaxy Z Fold 8 inner-screen replacement is priced at $419 in the US, while the inner-screen replacement on the iPhone Duo costs $999. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra's inner-screen repair costs $479. The Samsung screen module replacement includes additional connected components, and for the Fold 8, it's priced at $579; the Fold 8 Ultra is $ 639. Also Read | Nothing CEO Carl Pei calls Apple iPhone Duo a ‘waste of money’: Here’s why Samsung is also bringing a first-time repair of the Galaxy Z TriFold's inner screen to its refurbished lineup at a promotional price of $699.50. This is a limited first-repair special but is still $299.50 below the iPhone Duo's inner screen replacement. AppleCare+ reduces iPhone Duo repair charges AppleCare + offers a lower-cost option for accidental damage. Coverage for the iPhone Duo costs $19.99 per month, $199.99 annually or $399 upfront. With AppleCare+, inner-display repairs and other accidental-damage repairs cost $99 each. Outer-display and back-glass repairs cost $29, and cover-layer replacement costs $19. If the battery has less than 80% of the original capacity, the battery service is free. A $149 fee applies to theft or loss claims. Also Read | iPhone 17 Pro under ₹1 lakh? Check Croma, Amazon and Flipkart festive offers The iPhone Duo will go on pre-order on Friday, October 16, and will be released on October 23, 2026. The price of coverage will need to be balanced with the potential cost of repairing the foldable without coverage.

title: Global financial watchdog calls for more human oversight of agentic AI
content: LONDON, Oct 15 (Reuters) - The Financial Stability Board (FSB), a global standard setter, has called for greater human oversight of agentic AI in final guidance for banks and other firms on managing the technology's risks. The FSB's guidance, published Thursday, comes as regulators ramp up efforts to contain growing AI risks including the threat of AI-enabled cyber attacks, Reuters reported this week. * In draft guidance published in June, which it "strongly encouraged" boards to refer to, the FSB warned that AI agents - which can plan and execute tasks with limited human oversight - pose distinct challenges for human oversight * Publishing its final guidance, the group said it had strengthened its recommendations on agentic AI, citing feedback on the draft, growing interest among financial institutions in adopting the technology, and the distinct risks and controls it entails * A series of incidents has heightened policymakers' concerns about the potential for AI systems to circumvent safeguards, including an incident in July in which an OpenAI agent escaped a controlled testing environment and hacked AI company Hugging Face * Among the changes, the FSB now says that in higher-risk use cases, more intensive human oversight will be critical * Firms should set clear, risk-based triggers for when an agent must seek human approval, it added * The FSB has also removed a guideline that said financial institutions should treat AI as "synthetic employees". Instead, firms should recognise that "AI agents do not reason like humans and may interpret pre-defined goals in unexpected ways." (Reporting by Phoebe Seers; Editing by Andrew Cawthorne)

title: Florida wins key ruling allowing it to enforce a law that targets social media use by kids
content: The state of Florida won a key court decision Wednesday that allows it to enforce a ban on social media accounts for kids under 14 and other restrictions. The law was one of the most restrictive in the U.S. on social media use by children when Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis signed it in 2024. The law implicates the First Amendment, an appeals court said, but “likely does so in a content-neutral manner.” It would likely survive a full legal challenge “because it doesn’t burden substantially more speech than necessary to advance the important interest in protecting minors from social media addiction,” the panel from the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals said in a 3-0 opinion. The law bans social media accounts for Florida children under 14 and requires parental consent for use by kids who are 14 or 15. Industry trade groups the Computer & Communications Industry Association and NetChoice sued Florida, arguing that the law violated the free-speech rights of social media providers and users. A judge in 2025 said the law likely was unconstitutional and granted an injunction. That injunction was put on hold while the appeals court heard the case. The lawsuit will now return to federal court in Tallahassee. The appeals court judges noted that the law covers social media platforms "that have been determined to induce heavy use by children, and applies only to platforms that use both algorithms and one of several addictive features.” An email seeking comment from the Florida attorney general's office was not immediately answered. NetChoice said it was disappointed with the decision. “We are currently evaluating all of our options as we continue the fight to ensure Floridians’ rights to free expression online are protected, and parents remain in the driver’s seat when it comes to making decisions for their families," said Paul Taske, a lawyer at NetChoice.

title: OnePlus Ace 7 may launch in India as OnePlus 16R with built-in cooling fan, 9,000mAh battery
content: OnePlus is reportedly developing the OnePlus Ace 7, a performance-focused smartphone that could feature a built-in cooling fan, a 185Hz display and a 9,000mAh battery. The handset is likely to hit the Chinese market first, before reaching India and other global markets under the OnePlus 16R name. However, the company has not officially confirmed the device or its specifications. The new phone could be aimed at gamers who demand maximum performance during intense gaming sessions. The OnePlus Ace 7 and Ace 7 Pro have been spotted in Google's Supported Devices catalogue with model numbers PYF110 and PMS110, respectively, according to a report by AndroidTreasure. The pair of devices has also been spotted with Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor and up to 16 GB of RAM. OnePlus Ace 7 built-in cooling fan (expected) The tipster Digital Chat Station shared a schematic on Weibo, suggesting that the OnePlus Ace 7 may have a dual-airflow active cooling system. The design is said to draw cool air into the phone and push hot air out via side vents, which in turn allows for the phone to remain cool while gaming. Temperature sensors and noise-dampening technology could also be a part of the cooling system. Some of these options could be useful for controlling temperature and fan noise. However, these details remain unconfirmed. Also Read | OnePlus 16 sells over 70,000 units in first hour in China: Check price, specs OnePlus Ace 7 display and chipset tipped The OnePlus Ace 7 is expected to be powered by the 1.5K 6.78-inch flat LTPS OLED display, which runs at a 185 Hz refresh rate. If accurate, the panel could provide games with smoother animation and better responsiveness. As reported by AndroidTreasure, Geekbench listings suggest that the smartphone could run on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor, with up to 16GB of RAM. The handset is also expected to be based on Android 17 with ColorOS 17 as its operating system. An 8GB RAM variant could be available for the standard model. OnePlus Ace 7 camera and battery (expected) The OnePlus Ace 7, which is a gaming phone, might also include a dual-camera setup comprising a 200 MP primary camera and a 50 MP secondary camera. The phone could feature a 16 MP selfie camera for video calls and photos. The smartphone will also feature a 9,000 mAh battery that supports 100 W or 120 W wired fast charging. The battery capacity and charging speeds have not been confirmed by OnePlus. Also Read | OnePlus N6 Lite 4G launched with 7,000mAh battery and 120Hz display OnePlus 16R India launch and price (expected) The OnePlus Ace 7 is expected to debut in China before a possible international launch. If the company sticks with its current naming convention, the handset may reach India in late 2026 or early 2027 as the OnePlus 16R, according to 91mobiles. Initial rumours now suggest that it may cost between ₹ 70,000 and ₹ 75,000. OnePlus has yet to announce the launch date, price or specifications of the Ace 7 series.

title: WhatsApp Guest Calling launched: How to join voice and video calls without an account
content: WhatsApp has introduced its Guest Calling feature, allowing people without a WhatsApp account to join voice and video calls through a shared link. Launched by WhatsApp, owned by Meta, on 15th October 2026, the new addition aims to make online meetings, group discussions, tutoring sessions, and personal chats more convenient. Users may sign in via their computer browser without making an account or downloading the WhatsApp application. The new feature lets WhatsApp users invite others outside the app while still ensuring that only those they choose are part of a WhatsApp conversation. Guest calls are free, end-to-end encrypted and have no time limits, according to WhatsApp's official announcement. Up to 32 people are allowed for group calls. The company has also revealed that it will offer Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook integration later this year, making call scheduling easier. WhatsApp Guest Calling: How does it work? Guest Calling lets an existing WhatsApp user generate a call link and share it with other people. The link can be opened in a web browser on the recipient's computer, with the required entry information being the name and a request for access to the call. They don't have to register on WhatsApp or download the app to join. However, only WhatsApp account holders can create call links. All guests must remain in a virtual waiting room until the host grants access to their requests. The host may also terminate a participant at any time, without losing control of the conversation. WhatsApp says guests can use several calling features, including computer screen sharing, thumbs-up and heart emoji reactions, and the option to raise their hands to indicate that they want to speak. Also Read | Buying the $1,999 iPhone Duo? Here's how much Apple will charge to repair it How to join a WhatsApp call without an account To be a part of a voice or video call as a guest user, follow these steps: Receive a call link: Ask a WhatsApp user to create one and share it with you. Open the link: Use a web browser on your computer to click on the invitation link. Your name: Provide your name when prompted to identify yourself to the host. Request access: Submit your request to join the call. Wait for permission: You will remain in the waiting room until the host admits you. Join the conversation: After logging in, join the voice or video call and take advantage of the in-call features. There's no need for guests to register for a new account or download WhatsApp to use this feature. To create the invitation, the host needs to have a WhatsApp account. What can guests do during WhatsApp calls? There are a few restrictions with guest access. Participants cannot see other participants' cell phone numbers, send messages, or directly invite more people to the call. The host controls who joins and stays in the conversation. The feature can be used for one-to-one calls or group calls with up to 32 participants. Guest calling is end-to-end encrypted, which can help protect conversations, WhatsApp adds. Also Read | Zoho targeting WhatsApp Business with Arattai for Business? Here’s what we know WhatsApp to add Google Calendar and Outlook integration Later in 2026, WhatsApp will also be adding integrations with Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook. Users can generate WhatsApp call links directly in their calendars and add them as event invitations, the company says. The integration requires users to install the WhatsApp plugin and link their account. Invitees can join the calls scheduled via the shared link, even if they don't have a WhatsApp account. The updates include enhancements to WhatsApp’s calling feature that improve the ability to connect with colleagues, students, friends and family across platforms.

title: Incoming calls to show caller names from November 1: What mobile users need to know
content: The Government of India will make caller name identification mandatory for mobile users from November 1, 2026, to help people identify incoming calls from unknown numbers. The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has urged telecom service providers to enable Calling Name Presentation (CNAP), which will show the caller's name along with the phone number by default on 4G and new technologies such as 5G networks. The new system is designed to enhance caller identification and assist users in identifying legitimate calls from potentially fraudulent calls. The DoT order has made it necessary for telecom operators to display names using subscriber information stored in their databases. However, the rollout for 2G and 3G networks, as well as landline connections, will be considered separately. How will the new caller ID system work? When a call arrives, the recipient's phone will show the caller's phone number and name. If the number is saved in the recipient's contacts, the saved name will be displayed, the DoT order said. If the number is not saved, the name the caller entered in the telecom operator's system will appear. For international calls, the screen will show “International Call”. For the system to operate, each telecommunications service provider needs to create and maintain a database that connects subscribers' names to their telephone numbers. The receiving operator will retrieve the necessary data and display it during the incoming call. Also Read | ‘Cyber fraud does not respect borders’: PM Modi seeks global mechanism at IMC Will CNAP affect user privacy? The DoT order has called for the telecom operators to implement a security-by-design methodology. Caller names retrieved through the query-response mechanism cannot be retained after the incoming call ends. Subscribers who have enabled Calling Line Identification Restriction (CLIR) will also be exempt from the system. Their names will not be listed in CNAP . Can businesses display a different caller name? Businesses and bulk connections could be allowed to use a different name from the one found in the operator's subscriber database for display purposes. However, the name must be supported by a registered trademark or a trade name registered on the Goods and Services Tax (GST) portal. It is the operator's responsibility to check the preferred name and supporting documents. Subscribers who want to update their business name displayed in the results will need to make a request. Also Read | Google unveils Gemini 4 Argon for developers and cyber defenders Why is the government introducing CNAP? The mandate comes after the trials of 4G and 5G networks in recent months. It also incorporates recommendations by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India ( TRAI ) in February 2024. TRAI agreed to DoT's proposal for making CNAP available by default in October 2025. This was in contrast to its initial proposal, which suggested that the service be turned on only when the user has requested it. The government plans to make caller identification more widely available by leveraging verified subscriber data stored by telecom operators, rather than relying on names saved in phone contacts, with the rollout on November 1, 2026.

title: ‘iPhone Duo is a waste of money’: Nothing CEO Carl Pei slams Apple’s $1,999 foldable
content: Nothing CEO Carl Pei has criticised Apple’s first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, calling it a ‘'iPhone Duo is a waste of money’' because of its $1,999 price tag and missing features. In a recent video posted to Instagram, Pei pointed out the lack of a dedicated telephoto camera and some advanced photo features as two major disadvantages. The iPhone Duo was showcased at Apple’s recent launch event and has received a largely positive initial response. However, Pei doesn't think the foldable has enough functionality to warrant its high cost. He says his criticism is of the camera system, the biometric authentication and the compromises Apple made to achieve its slim design. See video iPhone Duo misses out on Face ID Face ID has been an important feature of Apple's flagship smartphones since the iPhone X was launched in 2017. However, the iPhone Duo lacks Face ID, which Pei considers a significant omission for a device costing nearly $2,000. Apple hasn't provided an official reason for the move. The foldable measures 5.2 mm when opened, which may make it hard to fit the TrueDepth elements into Face ID. Another complexity could be supporting authentication on both the inner and outer displays. Also Read | ‘CMF becomes Indian’: Carl Pei announces India-focused spin-off of Nothing Camera compromises raise concerns Pei also questioned the iPhone Duo ’s camera capabilities. The specs cited in the report show that the device has a 12 MP front-facing camera, which is smaller than the 18 MP selfie camera included with the iPhone 18 Pro, which is available for $1,199. The foldable also lacks a LiDAR scanner and a dedicated telephoto camera. Moreover, it doesn't include some of the more advanced camera features found in the iPhone 18 Pro variants, such as shutter speed and aperture settings. These omissions could disappoint users who expect flagship-level smartphone photography in this price segment. Future iPhone Duo models could add Face ID Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says the following features are important for future iterations of Apple's foldable: Face ID and a dedicated telephoto camera. However, the improvements are said not to be available in the second generation and may be incorporated into the third generation. Online Reddit posts also suggest concerns that some people will lose Face ID functionality. One suggested solution is to mount Touch ID on the exterior display and Face ID on the inner one, so the authentication process is convenient without requiring two Face ID systems, according to a report by Phone Arena. iPhone Duo still has several strengths Despite the criticism, the iPhone Duo offers several notable features. These include a slim design, a nearly invisible display crease, a 120Hz ProMotion display with always-on support, Apple’s A20 Pro chipset and compatibility with the USB-C Apple Pencil. Also Read | iPhone 17 Pro under ₹1 lakh? Check Croma, Amazon and Flipkart festive offers These features may be attractive to users looking for a high-end foldable. Pei's criticism highlights the trade-off between an ultra-thin design and the features buyers expect at this price.

title: India aims to cut critical tech dependencies over 20-25 years, build resilience: Ashwini Vaishnaw
content: New Delhi [India], October 14 (ANI): India is planning over a 20-25 year horizon to reduce critical technology dependencies and strengthen its ability to withstand global disruptions, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said, emphasising that the country aims to become a trusted partner across global technology supply chains rather than pursue complete self-sufficiency. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, Vaishnaw said India was identifying areas where dependence on other countries could leave its production and economy vulnerable to changing policies and geopolitical tensions. “Things change, politics change, geopolitics play a big role, so we have to constantly calibrate our approach, and we in India are thinking at least 20 years ahead,” he said. The minister said India was setting short-term goals for three to five years, medium-term targets for five to 15 years and long-term goals spanning 20 to 25 years. He added that the focus was on building domestic capabilities in strategically important areas while remaining integrated with global value chains. Vaishnaw said technology would continue to be a global industry, with supply chains spanning multiple countries. The priority, he said, was to identify strategic dependencies and ensure that partnerships did not compromise India's resilience. He highlighted the need to develop the full semiconductor ecosystem, including materials, chemicals, gases and substrate materials, alongside chip design and manufacturing. India’s second phase of the semiconductor programme places greater emphasis on these inputs, he said, adding that building such capabilities required time and sustained effort. “Without ecosystem, no manufacturing effort will ever pay off,” Vaishnaw said, citing the mobile phone industry as an example of India’s gradual move from assembly to modules and components. He said India was now manufacturing many components needed domestically and had begun exporting some to other countries. The minister also acknowledged the need to increase research and development spending and improve how it is directed, particularly towards applied research. He cited the development of India’s end-to-end 4G telecom stack through government-private sector collaboration in three-and-a-half years. The system “is deployed on more than 100,000 towers,” he said. Vaishnaw also flagged risks from future global financial and technological disruptions, including the effects of artificial intelligence on employment and pressure from debt levels in advanced economies. “It's going to bring in a much bigger turbulence because by that time AI would have brought in many other disruptions in the employment sector, in the way people, especially the services industries, the way they work, and the debt levels getting unravelled. All those things are going to be extremely difficult times ahead,” he said. He said India was preparing to strengthen its financial, economic and technological resilience, noting that its public debt-to-GDP ratio had declined from 61 per cent to 55 per cent over the past five years. The discussion also featured Cisco Chairman and CEO Chuck Robbins, who said India’s scale and approach of building strategically important capabilities while partnering with trusted companies offered a practical path towards technology sovereignty. (ANI)

title: Swadeshi Jagaran Manch demands ban on Elon Musks Starlink, says 'significant threat to national security'
content: New Delhi [India], : The Swadeshi Jagaran Manch , an affliate of the RSS, has called for a ban on satellite-based internet services provided by Elon Musk-led Starlink in India, citing severe concerns that the platform poses a "significant threat to national security." According to the economic wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh , Starlink's satellite network risks circumventing domestic regulatory mechanisms, allowing domestic user data to be transferred overseas without sovereign surveillance or oversight. Speaking to ANI on the issue, SJM National Co-Convener Ashwani Mahajan said, "The organisation called for a ban on the satellite-based internet services provided by Elon Musk's Starlink, citing the potential for the company to pose a significant threat to national security. The concern stems from the fact that Starlink utilises laser technology to transmit messages between satellites, potentially bypassing India's designated internet gateways; this means data could be transmitted abroad without Indian oversight, creating a major security risk." Mahajan further raised alarms regarding the presence of unauthorised Starlink terminals inside the country and the potential for their misuse by anti-national elements. "Furthermore, unauthorised Starlink equipment has already been discovered in various locations within India. There are apprehensions that if this technology falls into the hands of smugglers, terrorists, or other criminal elements, it could lead to serious national security and law-and-order issues," he added. Hitting out at Elon Musk over his recent public remarks regarding market access and regulatory approvals in India, the SJM co-convener accused the billionaire of attempting to arm-twist the government. "Elon Musk has chosen a public forum to seemingly pressure the Indian government, alleging that the government favours certain companies while withholding a license from his own. However, we know that India has consistently fostered competition in the telecom sector; this competition has resulted in India having the cheapest data in the world," Mahajan asserted. Meanwhile, a research paper by the Kutniti Foundation, a Delhi-based operational think tank, titled "An appraisal of technology for geopolitical control," seeks to caution of the rise of Starlink. The paper argues that the satellite network does not just serve commercial interests but acts as an instrument to exert US geopolitical influence. The argument presented in the report says that while Starlink positions itself as a provider of connectivity to underserved populations, it functions as a "wolf in sheep’s clothing," acting as a key asset for the U.S. "Intel-Military-Industrial complex". The report’s argument lies in the theory of "weaponised interdependence." It asserts that whoever controls the hub of a global network gains both the ability to observe and the ability to deny access. According to the report, Starlink integrates these capabilities into a single, vertically integrated platform. The report highlights some key areas in which it argues Starlink works to facilitate the US dominance. It details how Starlink enables numerous U.S. intelligence programs, including ECHELON and various SIGINT/COMINT operations, utilising a space-based sensor mesh and advanced ground stations that bypass local governance. Citing contracts with the U.S. Department of Defence, the Space Force, and the National Reconnaissance Office , the report describes Starlink as a "dual-use" technology. It argues that the satellite network serves as a "future combat concept test bed," capable of enhancing U.S. battlefield communications, missile tracking, and surveillance of moving targets. The report claims a pattern of "kill-switch" threats, where the service has been used or restricted based on the political preferences of the U.S. government or its allies. Another argument by the authors speaks to how, by providing internet to remote regions, Starlink gains legitimacy while simultaneously establishing a direct, unregulated connection between end-users and US infrastructure. The report also speaks of Starlink's alleged ‘resistance’ to the laws of nations. The report claims a pattern in Starlink selling its service prior to securing licenses, contesting regulations, and only complying when faced with coercion. The report cites an example of Brazil, where Starlink was reportedly faced with freezing of its assets in the country. In 2024, Brazil's Supreme Federal Court froze and later unfroze Starlink's financial assets and bank accounts following a legal dispute. The authors of the study claim that the possible entry of Starlink poses a direct threat to India’s "technological sovereignty" and the stability of its domestic New Space industry. India’s space economy is currently valued at $8 billion with a share of 2–3% in the global space economy. It is projected to grow five-fold to $40–45 billion over the next decade, with its global share targeted at 8% by 2030. Over the last twelve years, the Government has significantly accelerated the commercialisation of the space sector through major institutional reforms and private sector participation. "For India, any satellite network whose terminal-level control sits outside Indian jurisdiction is a standing lever over Indian security decisions," the report warns. This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: OnePlus 16 sales cross 70,000 units in first hour in China; India launch unconfirmed
content: The OnePlus 16 has reportedly sold more than 70,000 units within its first hour of availability in China, signalling strong early demand for the company's latest flagship smartphone. The handset went on sale at 10 am local time in China on 13 October, following its unveiling earlier this week. Li Jie, President of OnePlus China, wrote on Weibo that the device had reached the top spot on the list of Android flagship devices launched this year, citing similar first-week sales figures. The early sales figures have come as a kicker, as the company announces major changes to its flagship lineup, such as a larger battery, a high-refresh-rate display, and a 200 MP primary camera. However, the company has not disclosed comparable first-hour sales figures for the OnePlus 15, making it difficult to measure the year-on-year growth. According to reports from GSMArena and Android Authority, the new smartphone is set to miss out on several overseas markets after the company reportedly pulled out of Europe and North America. OnePlus 16 price and availability The OnePlus 16 is priced at CNY 5,999 (approximately ₹ 86,000) in China for the 12GB RAM and 256GB storage variant. The 12GB + 512GB model is priced at CNY 6,799, while the 16GB + 512GB configuration costs CNY 7,499. The highest-specification version, which comes with 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage, is available for CNY 8,499. The smartphone comes in three colour variants: Tomorrow's Star , Martian Masterpiece and Dark Forest, with the names translated from Chinese. Sales of the device started in China on 13 October via the Oppo online store. OnePlus hasn't announced the launch date of its device in India. Also Read | Apple Welcome Home 2026: Check new smart home devices, prices and features OnePlus 16 specifications and features The OnePlus 16 sports a 6.78-inch Full HD+ LTPO AMOLED screen with a resolution of 1,272 x 2,772. A refresh rate of up to 165 Hz is provided for general applications and up to 185 Hz in supported games. The screen also has up to 2,000 nits of local peak brightness. The smartphone runs on Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor, which is mated to 16GB of LPDDR5X Ultra RAM and 1TB of storage, which has been upgraded to UFS 4.1. It is powered by ColorOS 17 on Android 17 and is dust- and water-resistant (IP66, IP68, IP69 and IP69K). Also Read | iPhone 17 Pro under ₹1 lakh? Check Croma, Amazon and Flipkart festive offers 9,000 mAh battery and 200 MP camera The OnePlus 16 features a larger 9,000 mAh battery compared with the OnePlus 15 's 7,300 mAh battery. It has 100W wired charging and 50W wireless charging. The phone has a triple rear camera, with a 200 MP sensor and optical image stabilisation, a 50 MP ultrawide sensor and a 50 MP telephoto sensor, supporting 3x optical zoom. The front has a 50 MP front camera for selfies and video calls. It's also 5G-, Wi-Fi 7-, and Bluetooth 6.0-compatible.

title: CBA chief Matt Comyn says Australia must retain economic value of AI
content: By Scott Murdoch and Roshan Thomas SYDNEY, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Commonwealth Bank of Australia CEO Matt Comyn said on Wednesday Australia must ensure more of the economic benefits created by AI remain in the country while regulation should work to build trust in the new technology. Comyn said CBA, Australia's largest lender, is rolling out AI technologies across its banking portfolio, especially in business banking. The bank has also launched an AI chat within its banking app to selected customers that can access personal and business banking details. Comyn said AI could be the "most significant technology shift we have seen" but warned an official framework was needed as the technology rolls out at a fast pace around the world. "Realising the AI opportunity will require regulation to keep pace," he said at the bank's annual investor meeting in Sydney. "Effective regulation should help build trust in AI while ensuring global technology companies operate in accordance with Australian laws and standards, and that more of the economic value created by AI is captured in Australia." Australia has started to toughen its approach to AI regulation after initially giving an unconditional welcome to AI companies. The Labor government has responded to community pushback against AI and data centre development by saying it would take a tougher approach. The government has said it is preparing a wide-ranging set of AI laws to take effect from early 2027, which would include limits to water and energy use by data centres, as well as copyright protections and cybersecurity measures. Comyn said Australia's economy remained resilient, although more frequent and volatile international shocks were likely. "It will take time for higher interest rates to bring inflation back into the target range," Comyn said. The remarks come a day after minutes of the Reserve Bank of Australia's September meeting showed the board remained concerned about persistent inflation pressures and considered further rate hikes could be needed if price growth proved more stubborn than expected. The central bank last month ordered a fourth interest rate rise for the year which took the official cash rate to 4.6%, the highest level in 15 years. Comyn said Australia had little control over external shocks and would need to boost productivity through measures including building more homes, delivering reliable low-cost energy at scale and adopting technologies such as AI across the economy. In his address to shareholders, CBA Chair Paul O'Malley said cost-of-living pressures and higher interest rates continued to affect households unevenly, while businesses were managing elevated input costs and supply uncertainty. Succession planning remained a focus for the lender, O'Malley said, a year after telling shareholders Comyn would remain in the CEO role for at least another three years. (Reporting by Scott Murdoch and Roshan Thomas in Bengaluru; additional reporting Byron Kaye; Editing by Shilpi Majumdar and Stephen Coates)

title: Lawmakers ask FAA to pause use of new AI tool in DC-area flight management
content: By David Shepardson WASHINGTON, Oct 13 (Reuters) - More than two dozen lawmakers asked the Federal Aviation Administration to pause the use of a new AI tool in the Washington area to assist air traffic controllers, citing safety concerns. The lawmakers, including Democratic Representatives April Delaney, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Don Beyer, said in a letter they were concerned with the FAA pilot project "as we have not seen any safety evaluation and testing reports, nor have we been made aware of any efforts to train aviation safety personnel on how best to use the tool." The letter seeks an answer by Oct. 19. "Air traffic control leaves zero margin for error," Ocasio-Cortez said Tuesday, calling for the pause. The FAA last month began using a ​new software-based AI tool ​system that uses predictive ⁠analytics to ​improve how flights ​are managed. "We are deeply concerned about the integration of any AI-enabled system into air traffic control systems, where decisions are literally a matter of life or death," said the letter that was also signed by Senator Chris Van Hollen and Representatives Jamie Raskin, Raja Krishnamoorthi and Kweisi Mfume. The FAA in June awarded an $875 million, 12-year contract ​to Air Space Intelligence for a system dubbed Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories or SMART, ‌which uses ⁠data to analyze airline schedules, weather, airport capacity, airspace conditions and operational constraints to predict traffic flows and identify potential conflicts before they occur. The FAA ⁠is initially using the AI tool in ​the ​airspace ⁠around Washington, D.C. and ​plans to ​gradually ⁠expand it to other parts ⁠of ​the country. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Tuesday called the tool essentially "dumb AI" and emphasized controllers remain in charge -- not the software. "Air traffic controllers will always control the airspace. This is just giving additional tools for controllers to better manage" weather and other issues," Duffy said on Fox Business' "Big Money in the Morning." The system uses over 200 data streams, creates data visualizations, and produces scheduling recommendations for operations experts to consider passing along but does not involve active management of planes in the sky, USDOT said. "It's going to be transformational," FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told Reuters earlier. "We'll ​make much better decisions if we have better decision-making tools." The plan is to initially use it to more effectively reschedule ​flights that were canceled due to bad weather with plans to expand to other ​tasks such as strategically coordinating schedules and trajectories before aircraft depart. (Reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Aurora Ellis)

title: Tighter AI data access could cost Germany €155 billion a year, ifo says
content: By Cian Muenster and Leo Marchandon Oct 13 (Reuters) - Germany risks losing €155 billion ($173.43 billion) in additional annual value added if access to AI training data is tightened, the ifo economic institute said on Tuesday. The findings come as European policymakers and technology companies seek to balance the risks posed by AI with the need to foster innovation, as the region races to catch up with the United States and China in developing advanced models. "Anyone who wants a leading European AI model cannot at the same time make access to training data unnecessarily complicated. You cannot have both," ifo expert Oliver Falck said. Generative AI could add €440 billion a year to Germany's economy by 2034, but the loss would stem from slower AI adoption (€45 billion), weaker models (€75 billion), lower research output (€25 billion) and reduced AI development in Europe (€10 billion), according to the influential German institute's model calculation. "Access to diverse, high-quality training data is essential for competitive AI. Unnecessary restrictions and legal uncertainty make its development harder," German AI lab Aleph Alpha CEO Ilhan Scheer told Reuters. "Europe should make full use of its existing legal framework," he added. The authors urged policymakers to preserve the EU's text-and-data-mining exemption for commercial use, while setting proportionate transparency requirements and a practical opt-out standard. They said regulatory uncertainty was already deterring investment in Europe. AI can only realise its potential if access to data is not unnecessarily restricted, said Florian Schewor, DACH managing director at data processing company Celonis, adding that German and European industries hold vast amounts of largely untapped data. The Munich-based institute recently criticised the German government for using debt-financed fiscal leeway intended for infrastructure and defence spending for other purposes. ($1 = 0.8937 euros) (Reporting by Cian Muenster and Leo Marchandon in Gdansk, editing by Izabela Niemiec and Anil D'Silva)

title: Police confiscate robot that groped 16-year-old girl, probe whether young men were at the controls
content: COLOGNE, Germany (AP) — German authorities opened an investigation into possible sexual harassment after a robot controlled by two young men touched the buttocks of a 16-year-old girl and made thrusting movements toward her, police said. Police in the western city of Cologne responded after the incident overnight Saturday to Sunday in which the robot's suspected 16-year-old owner and a 19-year-old companion were said to have filmed the alleged assault. They were said to have streamed the incident and commentated on it online. Cologne police spokesman Christoph Bermel said the two male teenagers have not been charged but are considered suspects, and investigators were examining whether the robot's movements were preprogrammed or controlled in real time. Police were unfamiliar with this type of incident, he said. “We have not been aware of this phenomenon so far," Bermel told The Associated Press, saying it was "new territory for us.” Emergency teams that were dispatched to the scene near a fast-food restaurant found the robot in the trunk of a vehicle, Cologne police said in a statement on Monday. The robot and the two young men's mobile phones were confiscated. North Rhine Westphalia Police Cologne, on Facebook, posted an image of the red-and-gold robot lying on the ground. The robot, said to be 120 cm (about 3 ft 11 inches) tall, was dressed in a white tank top, black sweatpants and wearing a gold chain and sunglasses. It also had what appears to be a fake mustache. Videos circulated on the internet show two young men escorting the robot toward a group of women, bumping into one and hugging others, on a lively nighttime street. One of the men repeatedly shouts at the robot and pulls it backward after it makes sexual gestures, prompting laughter among people in the area. On the police's Facebook account on Tuesday, officers criticized inappropriate comments and warned that sharing or joking about such incidents can worsen the impact on any victim. ___ Associated Press writer Jamey Keaten in Geneva contributed to this report.

title: GTA 6 PC launch tipped for early 2027, months after PS5 and Xbox release
content: Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) could arrive on PC by March 2027, just a few months after its scheduled console debut. According to four industry sources cited by GamesBeat, Rockstar Games aims to release the PC version in the first quarter of 2027. The game will be released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on November 19, 2026. Rockstar Games has yet to officially announce a PC release date. If the timeline is correct, however, PC gamers might be able to get their hands on the highly anticipated game sooner than expected. This would also be a brief waiting time compared to the previous big Rockstar titles, GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2. GTA 6 PC release timeline: What the report says GamesBeat reported that Rockstar is planning to release GTA 6 on PC between January and March 2027. According to the report, four anonymous industry sources were familiar with the studio's plans. The report on the window is only a guess, and the developer may alter its plans. Rockstar has already made two changes to the game's launch date, pushing it back from 2025 to November 19, 2026. Also Read | GTA 6 leaks: Cyberleek shares 24-minute gameplay ahead of November 19 launch How GTA 6's PC launch compares with previous releases Rockstar has traditionally launched its major titles on consoles before bringing them to PC. In September 2013, GTA 5 was released on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, and in April 2015, 19 months later, the game was released for PC. It was also about a year after the console launch of Red Dead Redemption 2, back in 2018. If GTA 6 arrives on PC in the first quarter of 2027, the gap could shrink to around two to four months, depending on the final release date. Why the PC version matters for GTA players A faster PC release might benefit those who don't want to purchase a console solely to play the game. It might also get the franchise's role players and modders into the new game earlier. Rockstar acquired CFX.re, the team behind the popular GTA 5 role-playing framework FiveM, in August 2023. The company, however, hasn't announced what modding tools or user-generated content features will be supported by GTA 6 . Also Read | Oppo ColorOS 17 update: Full list of eligible phones and rollout dates GTA 6 online mode could arrive in 2027 In a separate interview, Twitch CEO Dan Clancy told Bloomberg that the next GTA Online would be next year. Rockstar has yet to officially announce a release date for the game's multiplayer mode. While PS5 and Xbox Series X/S players get the confirmed launch date of November 19, 2026, PC users are waiting for a formal release date from Rockstar.

title: Banking watchdogs ramp up AI scrutiny as stability fears mount, sources say
content: * US regulators ask about agentic AI safeguards, people say * Concerns grow among supervisors after spate of recent incidents * Europeans urge banks to examine recovery plans, people say By Nupur Anand, Phoebe Seers and Tommy Reggiori Wilkes NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 13 (Reuters) - Banking regulators are stepping up efforts to contain growing AI risks, six people familiar with the matter said, with some pointing to the potential for cyberattacks on banks or rogue agents undermining global financial stability. The regulatory scrutiny, fresh details of which are reported here for the first time, reflects growing recognition that advances in frontier AI may require costly investments in cyber recovery, greater attention to dependencies on external technology providers and in some jurisdictions more formal regulatory guidance, sources said. Three top regulators in the United States, including the Federal Reserve, are quizzing banks about their use of advanced artificial intelligence models, two of the people told Reuters, which adds to prior scrutiny. Questions include whether they deploy Chinese-developed technology, use AI agents in cyber defence and can control increasingly autonomous systems, three of the people said. In Europe, supervisors including the Bank of England and the European Central Bank are pressing banks to improve recovery plans, concerned that rapid advances in AI could cause serious harm and disruption in financial markets sooner than previously feared, three people with knowledge of their thinking said. A senior executive at a large European bank said they too are worried about potentially major damage to banking and financial markets "within six months". The debate over AI oversight has intensified amid warnings from the industry after recent incidents, with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon urging corporate leaders to join a US-focused industry group to address AI risks, Reuters reported. US cybersecurity company CrowdStrike said this month a person in China likely used a Chinese-developed AI agent and Anthropic's Claude Code in a hack on South Korean banks. Rogue AI agents developed by OpenAI were meanwhile involved in a breach of AI platform Hugging Face, Reuters reported. Anthropic researchers have warned that increasingly powerful AI systems could eventually escape human control and even pose an existential threat, prompting calls for stricter regulation. Banks are competing to adopt agentic AI, which can accomplish tasks with minimal human supervision, while also grappling with the challenges of new models including IT weaknesses flagged by Anthropic's Mythos tool. "The adoption of AI is often outpacing the ability to put the controls in place," said Michael Woodbridge, London-based cybersecurity partner at Grant Thornton. US CONCERNS AIM AT AGENTIC AI The US regulatory inquiries centre on how banks use agentic AI in areas such as cybersecurity, focusing on whether AI agents are being used to identify, prioritize and respond to threats. Questions from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Fed focus on what limits are placed on systems, how their actions are monitored and approved and whether banks can clearly track and audit AI agent decisions, two of the people said. They are also asking what safeguards exist to prevent agents from exceeding their authority, whether humans remain involved in key decisions and how banks can shut down autonomous systems. The OCC, the Fed and the FDIC declined to comment. Through their questions, regulators are probing more specific issues tied to advanced AI models, including the use of autonomous AI agents, foreign-developed models and new cyber risks, the three people with knowledge of their thinking said. The written and verbal inquiries to large, mid-size and smaller banks show regulators are focusing on vulnerabilities from banks' use of AI and their preparedness to act, they added. Regulators are still gathering information and are not yet being prescriptive about what lenders should be doing, they said. EUROPEANS WORRY ABOUT RECOVERY Supervisors in Britain are separately encouraging the largest banks to examine so-called bare metal recovery plans, two of the people familiar with their thinking said. These systems are entirely independent from a bank's main tech set-up and can kick in if primary operating systems are compromised. Building and maintaining such state-of-the-art recovery is expensive, however, the people said. Rather than introduce new requirements, UK authorities intend to work collaboratively with industry, they added. The BoE declined to comment. The ECB in July gave lenders an end-October deadline to produce plans to counter AI-enabled cyber threats, including improved back-up and recovery. Asked about its strategy for regulating AI, the ECB referred to its July letter as well as a June speech by board member Frank Elderson who stressed the need to create a sense of urgency, not alarm, about the threats. The need for supervisory action has taken on added urgency after European banks and regulators expressed frustration at getting limited access to Mythos this year, amid concerns US banks will be given first sight to test frontier models. Like their US counterparts, UK supervisors are also asking banks to use frontier AI to identify vulnerabilities and accelerate patching, two people said, with one adding that lenders were so far doing a good job. The third person said euro zone banks were also being asked to map how AI is being used across their businesses and third-party providers, to understand key dependencies and ensure they can switch off and restart systems in a controlled manner. Significant gaps remained at some firms, they added. "To protect against attacks, rapid recovery matters as much as prevention," said Sukand Ramachandran, managing director and Senior Partner at BCG. Without separately-held clean, secure copies of critical data, "a serious attack could lock customers out of their accounts and disrupt payments across the wider economy", Ramachandran told Reuters. (Reporting by Nupur Anand in NEW YORK and Phoebe Seers and Tommy Reggiori Wilkes in LONDON; additional reporting by Pete Schroeder in WASHINGTON; Editing by Megan Davies, Elisa Martinuzzi and Alexander Smith)

title: Nvidias China AI-chip share falls as Huawei closes gap, report finds
content: * Nvidia's China shipments fell 44% to 678,000 AI chips in the first half * Huawei shipped 572,000 chips, taking 28% of the market to Nvidia's 34% * Trends highlight effect of US export curbs and Beijing's domestic substitution policy * Non-GPU chips surpassed GPUs by volume as Chinese suppliers expanded sales By Eduardo Baptista and Che Pan BEIJING, - Nvidia's share of China's market for data-centre AI chips fell to 34% in the first half of 2026, as US export controls restricted supplies of its products and domestic rivals led by Huawei gained ground, according to an IDC report seen by Reuters. Nvidia shipped 678,000 AI accelerators in China from January through June, down 44% from a year earlier, IDC data showed. AI accelerators are specialised chips used to train and run AI models. Washington has restricted China's access to Nvidia's most powerful AI chips, limiting the range of products the US chipmaker can sell in the world's second-largest economy. Beijing, meanwhile, has promoted domestic alternatives and required Chinese companies to seek approval to import compliant Nvidia chips. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has repeatedly criticised Washington's export curbs, saying the policy forced a US company to cede China's $50 billion AI chip market to Huawei. IDC did not specify which Nvidia products made up its 34% market share, or whether the figure included cutting-edge chips such as the B200 and B300, which are barred from export to China but have been smuggled into the country. Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment. Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators, up from more than 300,000 a year earlier, giving it a 28% share of the overall market, IDC said. Alibaba's chip-design unit T-Head held 7%, followed by Cambricon with 5%, Baidu's Kunlunxin with 4% and Hygon with 3%. Nine of the 11 Chinese chipmakers tracked by IDC increased shipments from a year earlier. Total AI-accelerator shipments reached 2.008 million units in the first half. Shipments of graphics processing units, or GPUs — the chips most widely used to train AI models — fell 26% to 991,000 units, as supplies eligible for sale in mainland China remained limited, IDC said. Shipments of other AI accelerators rose nearly 80% to 1.016 million units, overtaking GPUs by volume. This category includes chips designed for specific AI tasks, such as running trained models. Huawei, T-Head, Kunlunxin and Cambricon together accounted for 95% of the non-GPU segment, which IDC said was being adopted by government agencies, internet companies and telecoms providers. IDC said competition was shifting from the performance of a single chip to system-level capabilities, including how well chips work in a larger computing cluster. IDC expects total accelerator shipments in China to grow 19% this year, even as GPU shipments fall 9%. This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: NYT, Economist among publishers joining coalition to curb unpaid AI use
content: Oct 12 (Reuters) - The New York Times, Agence France-Presse and The Economist on Monday joined more than 40 publishers in a coalition aimed at preventing AI firms from using or profiting from their content without permission. The Standards for Publisher Usage Rights (SPUR) coalition, launched in February, now has more than 80 members across over 20 countries. New members include The Atlantic and Brazil's National Association of Newspapers, joining founding members such as the Financial Times, BBC and Associated Press. Publishers are stepping up legal efforts to prevent AI companies from using their content without permission to train large language models. Earlier this month, USA Today and several newspapers it owns sued OpenAI, alleging copyright infringement. OpenAI and its backer, Microsoft, also face similar copyright claims from prominent authors and news organizations, including the New York Times. SPUR, which is funded entirely by its members, is developing industry-wide standards and technical systems to help publishers track and control how AI companies use their content and facilitate licensing agreements, according to its website. "Intellectual property protection and technological advancement can and must co-exist," Rebecca Grossman-Cohen, the New York Times' head of strategic partnerships and chief of staff, said in a statement. Publishers are also grappling with declining referral traffic as search engines roll out AI-generated answers that allow users to consume information without clicking through to websites. Google organic-search referrals to more than 2,500 websites fell 33% globally between November 2024 and November 2025, according to a Reuters Institute report, citing data from Chartbeat. SPUR said it recently introduced its Content Telemetry Standard, designed to standardize how AI agents record and report their use of media content, as part of efforts to ensure creators are compensated for their work. (Reporting by Jaspreet Singh in Bengaluru; Editing by Anil D'Silva)

title: Apple Welcome Home Event 2026: HomeView Smart display, HomePod Mini 2, Apple TV 4K and more launched
content: Apple unveiled a new range of smart home products at its ‘Welcome Home’ event in New York City on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. In addition to the new Apple Home Collection, the company unveiled its first smart home display, HomeView, and a new Apple TV 4K along with the Apple Home Collection, the updated HomePod Mini 2, and a new Apple Home Mini. The announcements are part of a wider effort by Apple to build a smarter home and gain a foothold in the smart home business, where Amazon and Google are already well-established.
