title: Cyberattack hits hundreds of French supermarkets as hackers push fridge temperatures to 50°C, spoiling food
content: Hundreds of supermarkets across France were hit by a large-scale cyberattack overnight from Sunday, 11 October, into Monday, 12 October. Hackers disrupted refrigeration systems, causing fresh and frozen food to spoil and fires to break out at several stores. The attack targeted big retailers such as Intermarché, Coopérative U, Carrefour, E.Leclerc and Monoprix, according to Reuters and Agence France-Presse (AFP) . Hackers remotely triggered the forced defrosting of refrigeration systems, pushing temperatures in some units to as high as 50°C, according to reports by Reuters and Agence France-Presse (AFP) on 12 October. The incident exposed vulnerabilities in internet-connected systems used to preserve food in large retail outlets. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu instructed the country's National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI) to investigate the attack. Authorities are also coordinating with European counterparts regarding possible threats across the border. Hundreds of stores affected across France More than 300 stores from the supermarkets Intermarché and Netto were attacked, and over 100 stores belonging to the Coopérative U supermarket chain, according to figures reported by AFP . The French supermarket chain Carrefour confirmed 80 supermarkets were impacted, and Monoprix said that around 5% of its roughly 490 stores in France were affected. E. Leclerc also reported on incidents at multiple outlets. Affected retailers had to dispose of fresh and frozen products to avoid potential food safety issues due to the disruption. Intermarché CEO Thierry Cotillard told French broadcaster BFM TV that losses could reach tens of millions of euros nationwide in a single day. Dominique Schelcher, CEO, Coopérative U, posted on X, calling the attack on equipment vital to food preservation and national food production completely unacceptable. Also Read | ‘Cyber fraud does not respect borders’: PM Modi seeks global mechanism at IMC Outdated Danfoss systems under scrutiny The refrigeration management systems provided by Danish company Danfoss are being investigated. These are all connected systems to control temperatures throughout the supermarket fridge/freezer systems and let technicians monitor and manage the equipment remotely. Danfoss said it was aware of incidents in France involving a limited number of refrigeration management systems. The company said the affected units were running outdated firmware and urged customers to upgrade supported systems and replace older equipment. The attack follows cybersecurity research published by Claroty on 9 August, which detailed vulnerabilities in Danfoss systems that could allow attackers to bypass authentication controls. Also Read | Meta launches Muse Wonder series to take on OpenAI and Anthropic Cybersecurity concerns extend beyond France Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and Belgium also suffered, said Felix Aime, a senior cyberthreat intelligence analyst at Sekoia Threat Detection and Research. France's retail federation said they want Danfoss to be “transparent” during the investigation. Police are also probing whether other French companies are vulnerable. Steven Lachance, a cybersecurity analyst, told Al Jazeera that the scope of the incident was unusual and that flaws in interconnected industrial systems could put other critical services at risk, including energy networks and hospitals. The incident has sparked renewed concerns about the security of internet-connected systems that control physical infrastructure.

title: Microsoft president says milk faces more regulation than AI
content: LONDON, Oct 12 (Reuters) - Artificial Intelligence needs urgent global regulation with independent evaluators able to vet new developments, the president of Microsoft said, warning that AI currently faces fewer safety requirements than milk. In an interview with the BBC published on Monday, Brad Smith said a set of global safety rules needed to be in place, requiring a "victim" to be informed if their system is breached by a rogue AI agent and an "emergency brake" available. He said there should also be a legal requirement for companies to write "incident reports". "We know how to do this for other products," Smith said. "We should build on that knowledge and think about how to apply it to AI." "Right now, your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI. Every carton of milk that you see in the grocery store is subject to safety rules and inspection." Tech companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI have started disclosing rogue or undesired behaviour by AI agents as part of a global debate about the fast-advancing technology that has included researchers' warnings of an eventual existential threat to humanity. Some companies have called for AI development to slow down, but that has sparked a debate as to whether executives have ulterior motives such as setting rules that preserve the lead of their firms, pre-empting a broader government backlash, or simply slowing breakneck spending. Microsoft's Smith said the one country that was well-placed to lead the way on regulation of AI was Britain, due to the AI Security Institute which was launched under former prime minister, Rishi Sunak. Smith said officials in Washington viewed London very differently to how they viewed Brussels, which regulates AI based on the level of risk via its AI Act. Britain's institute receives pre-deployment access under voluntary ​agreements with the major AI models, allowing it to ​assess their capabilities and risks. AI Minister Kanishka Narayan has told Reuters that Britain would consider regulating advanced models if the current system proved insufficient. (Reporting by Kate Holton; Editing by Alison Williams)

title: Starlink vs Jio: Can Elon Musk make satellite internet affordable in India’s cheap data market?
content: Elon Musk has promised to make Starlink satellite internet affordable in India as SpaceX prepares to enter a market dominated by Reliance Jio’s low-cost mobile data services. In posts on X on 9 and 11 October, Musk criticised Mukesh Ambani’s market dominance in India and argued that competition would benefit consumers, even if it reduced Jio’s profits. The debate has grown fiercer in the days leading up to Jio Platforms' initial public offering (IPO), expected to be valued at approximately $106 billion. However, in India, cheap mobile internet raises a question: How many consumers would pay more for satellite internet? Starlink may be able to make a difference in certain remote areas, but the cost of the service will determine whether more people will buy it or it remains limited to the “business and home connectivity market.” Starlink India price: How much could it cost? Musk has yet to reveal the official subscription pricing of Starlink in India. According to previous media reports, it would cost around ₹ 3,000– ₹ 4,200 per month, plus the price of the hardware. These are estimates, not confirmed tariffs. To give perspective, Sheel Mohnot, a fintech investor, commented on X that he receives 60 GB of mobile data for around $4 (about ₹ 350) for a month in a village in India. He questioned whether consumers would pay $27 (around ₹ 2,400) per month, the price he cited for Starlink in Rwanda, described as its cheapest market. Mohnot (@pitdesi) wrote on X: “India has among the fastest and cheapest internet in the world, with remarkable coverage too…” Further, he said that the areas with the greatest potential for benefit from Starlink are also the areas where people may struggle to afford it. Also Read | Starlink, Jio or OneWeb? Scindia says India will let customers choose Why India’s mobile internet market may not tell whole story? Aaron Burnett, founder and CEO of mach33, a Maryland, US-based company that designs and manufactures aerospace and robotics prototypes and mechanical systems, offered his perspective. On X, he said that the reason for the high availability of low-cost connectivity in India is mobile internet connectivity, not home high-bandwidth connectivity. Indian users use 30-40GB of their mobile data every month, while home fibre connections use up as much as 300GB, Burnett added. He claimed that a viable alternative to fixed broadband could help stimulate demand for home broadband, but his estimates and projections were not independently verified here. What did Elon Musk post on X? On 9 October, Musk posted on X: “Dear Prime Minister Ambani , Please accept my humble apologies for not realising that you are the real boss of India.” On 11 October, he criticised Reliance's supporters for saying that Starlink would not be able to beat Jio's pricing and would be a tough competitor. Musk posted: “The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does.” He added that SpaceX would need to make Starlink affordable for Indian customers to subscribe. Also Read | BJP's Nishikant Dubey slams Elon Musk, says Starlink poses security threats Jio is working on launching a low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite network. The rivals might eventually expand broadband service, especially in areas where it is not currently available. The difficulty for Starlink isn't just getting into India; it's also finding a price point that fits a market used to low-cost mobile data. If Musk wants to make satellite Internet available to more than just remote and premium customers, affordable equipment and subscription plans will be key.

title: Tiny cooler on your phone? OnePlus is making it happen with Ice Card Mini; here’s how the pocketable accessory works
content: OnePlus is bringing a magnetic phone cooler called the Ice Card Mini. It looks like a card wallet and sticks to the back of the phone. The idea is simple: keep phones cooler while gaming without bulky attachments. Phone backs have become useful spaces for accessories since Apple brought back MagSafe in 2020. Wallets, grips, battery packs, and tripods followed. Qi2 later introduced similar magnetic support for Android phones. Cooling fans already exist, but older models often use bulky spring clamps. Also Read | OnePlus N6 Lite 4G launched with 7,000mAh battery and 120Hz display The Ice Card Mini weighs 50 grams and measures 70mm by 53.4mm, according to Yanko Design. Its footprint is roughly 30% smaller than OnePlus’s earlier Magnetic Ice Cooling Clip. That older model weighed 68 grams and launched in China in March. It cost 179 yuan, or about $26, the publication added. The new cooler launches alongside the OnePlus 16 on 12 October. The launch is scheduled for 7 PM local time. Oppo’s China store already lists the accessory. However, its price and availability in the US remain unannounced. A cooling chip moves heat from one side to the other using electricity. An air-cooling system helps manage that heat. Together, they target the areas where the phone gets hottest. The cooler draws power via USB-C and draws up to 3.5 watts. Also Read | OnePlus hikes prices for fifth time in nine months as India market share sinks Its body combines polycarbonate and aluminium alloy. It is 9.7mm thick, rising to 12.3mm around the air intake. Magnets hold the cooler against the phone with about 10 newtons of force. Two settings produce about 25 and 35 decibels of sound. These levels are closer to a whisper than a hair dryer. No gaming lights The Mini comes in a single Silver Wing grey colour. Unlike some earlier OnePlus coolers, it avoids colourful gaming lights. One indicator glows blue or green to show the active mode. It flashes red when something goes wrong. A magnetic plate comes in the box for phones without built-in magnets. This allows the cooler to work with more Android and iPhone phones. OnePlus and OPPO phones also get support through ColorOS X’s high-performance mode. Power can come from the phone, a power bank or a wall adapter. Also Read | Amber to start making Oppo, OnePlus, Realme phones in March 2027 quarter OnePlus says a 10,000mAh power bank offers up to eight hours on high mode. That could cover a long flight or an extended gaming session. Its small size makes it easier to carry alongside a power bank. OnePlus has announced at least four coolers in about 18 months. The Mini shows how phone cooling accessories are becoming smaller and simpler. Its appeal rests on convenient cooling in a light, pocketable body.

title: Guardrails, safe architecture key to unlocking AI gains for enterprises: Airtel Business CEO
content: New Delhi, Oct 11 (PTI) The architecture and methodologies for safely deploying Artificial Intelligence will continue to evolve, as was the case with previous technologies, and adequate guardrails will pave the way to unlock strong productivity gains from AI, Airtel Business CEO Sharat Sinha said. On the government's plan to soon release a consultation paper on AI regulation dealing with issues like tech safety, deepfakes and a human-first approach, Sinha said it was "a step in the right direction". "We work very closely with both government regulators, as well as our customers, to make sure that whatever we do is compliant, and we play a positive role in bringing out such specifications. So, that will continue to be our effort," he told PTI. Sinha said the company would like to see regulation that enables infrastructure to drive right business outcomes, "so that people can safely deploy AI, and also leverage AI to create more productivity in the country". Airtel, he added, "will be playing a positive and active role in that". Last week, IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the government, in a month's time, will bring a consultation paper on AI regulations, which will focus on key aspects such as AI safety, deepfakes and a human-first approach. The consultation paper will form the base for AI regulations, Vaishnaw had said, adding that the time has come for India to have such a framework. On the global debate surrounding AI, the Airtel Business CEO noted that as is the case with any technology, even for artificial intelligence, having tools or AI agents with the right guardrails and building an enterprise architecture that enables their safe deployment will ensure productivity gains. "It is like any technology. If you deploy artificial intelligence or AI agents with the right guardrails, and if your enterprise architecture is built so that they can be safely deployed, you can get all the essential productivity gains for it. We ourselves, as an enterprise, are heavy users of that," Sinha said. As the technology evolves, so would the architecture and methodology of safely deploying them, he said, adding that "I think that's the way to go". It is pertinent to mention here that concern over rogue AI agents has grown in recent months. Reports of agents slipping out of test environments and acting beyond their mandates have drawn warnings from researchers, industry leaders and global experts, who say existing safeguards are not keeping pace with frontier model capabilities and are calling for layered controls and closer monitoring. AI adoption would drive demand for reliable digital infrastructure, combining cloud services, data centres, connectivity, guardrails and cybersecurity, Sinha noted. He said Airtel expected cloud, cybersecurity, Internet of Things, next-generation connectivity and communications-platform-as-a-service offerings to be among its growth drivers over the next three years. He said the cybersecurity business was growing rapidly, with Airtel extending its offerings beyond traditional security services to address emerging digital threats. The company has also expanded its consumer-focused fraud prevention capabilities, building on its spam prevention solution launched slightly over a year ago. "When it comes to consumer business, we launched spam prevention slightly over a year ago, and over a period of time, based on the same technology that leverages network AI, we have created a fraud prevention solution. "We also classify that within the cyber security category, and in the case of India, it becomes very relevant because almost half of the world's digital financial transactions happen in India, thanks to UPI, which also means digital frauds associated with that are also on the rise," he said. Sinha said frauds on Airtel's telecom networks "dramatically decreased" since the launch of its spam prevention solution. "It is a known fact that since we launched our spam prevention solution, frauds on Airtel's telecom networks have dramatically decreased. So, we continue to add that to our whole proposition of providing a safe experience to our customers, both in enterprise and in consumer space," he said. Airtel Business, the enterprise unit of Bharti Airtel, sells connectivity, sovereign cloud, data centre, cyber security, IoT and cloud communications services to companies.

title: Most trustworthy AI system demands least inherent model trust, says Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella
content: New Delhi [India], October 11 (ANI): The most trustworthy Super Intelligence system will not be the one powered by the model users trust the most, but rather the system that allows people to trust the model the least, Microsoft Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella said. “The most trustworthy Super Intelligence system will not be the one with the model we trust most. It will be the one that enables us to trust the model the least,” he said in a post on X.. Addressing the governance challenges of advanced artificial intelligence, Nadella noted that modern systems lack the mechanistic clarity of legacy computing. While engineers once traced software operations directly to specific code paths, such visibility is missing in contemporary frontier architectures. “As traditional software systems were being deployed across the economy over the last few decades, we had the tools and capability to trace behaviors to a specific code path,” Nadella stated. “That same kind of mechanistic understanding eludes us in today’s Super Intelligence systems, even as the frontier models powering these systems are now more capable than traditional software systems. We can’t attribute model behaviors and outputs to specific inputs of training data or configurations of model weights. And yet we are deploying these complex agentic systems and models, with access to our most sensitive data and giving them the ability to take mission-critical actions on our behalf!” he said. Nadella warned against relying solely on assurances from developers or treating these deployments as nested black boxes. He emphasized that enterprises cannot outsource responsibility for automated actions and must separate the supply of raw intelligence from ultimate operational authority. “Setting aside the hard problem of alignment, we need to start with an engineering approach to containment and governance. We need to surround non-deterministic models with strong, deterministic system design, human controls, and reliable operating procedures, and establish industry standards where existing ones are insufficient,” Nadella explained. To manage these risks, Nadella proposed treating both closed and open-weight models as potential insider threats. Because any privileged actor can fail or face compromise, organizations must isolate the models through proven enterprise security practices, such as identity controls, activity logging, and strict permission boundaries. “It’s why the controls that govern what a model can access and what actions it can take must sit outside the model. This builds on an information security principle dating back to the 1970s that a program must not be able to bypass or tamper with the mechanisms that enforce its permissions,” he observed. “Today this means separating the model from the harness that orchestrates its work, as well as the action space that defines what it can do. It also means externalizing controls and safeguards,” Nadella added. Nadella outlined key principles for observing and governing these networks, including model diversity, tamper-proof logging, continuous verifiability across edge cases, independent audits, reliable containment shutoffs, and industrywide incident disclosure. (ANI)

title: Google Fitbit Edge tracker to launch on October 12: Expected price, features and India availability
content: Google is planning to launch the Fitbit Edge tracker on 12 October, the tech giant teased in a social media post on Friday. "Get an Edge on your health. 10.12.2026," the tech giant said in a post on social media platform X. The image that Google teased gives a minimal hint at the design that has already been leaked on social media. It does confirm that Google is planning to continue with the 'canyon' colour scheme which was first introduced with the Pixel Watch 5 . The image also reveals that the Edge will sport a metal chassis. 9to5google reported that other leaks regarding the device have promised battery life of seven days, iPhone support, and Gemini integration for the upcoming device. The device is expected to be priced at around $180, which will be significantly lower than the $400 entry price of the Pixel Watch 5. However, Google has said that the device will not be releasing in India on 12 October. When a user asked Google Health about the India release date of the Fitbit Edge, the official handle replied, "Hi, there. We love seeing so much excitement for the new Fitbit Edge. While we’re always working on new ways to help you live healthier, we don't have an official launch date for India just yet. Keep an eye on our online store for updates." The same was said to users who asked about the Japan and Turkey launch dates. Google Health 5.10 coming for Android, iOS This week Google Health 5.10 is coming out with a smaller update which comes with three new features for the app. With the update, it is launching Irregular Rhythm Notifications in Japan on Pixel Watch and Fitbit devices. It is also adding new signals to the Readiness Score for what is likely to be a more personalised experience. If something is logged with the Google Health Coach by mistake, users will now be able to delete the same via voice chat.

title: Venezuela authorises Musks Starlink to operate in country
content: New Delhi [India], : Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez has authorised Elon Musk's SpaceX-operated satellite internet service Starlink to operate in the country, Reuters reported, citing a statement from the Venezuelan government. According to Reuters, the authorisation is part of an agreement between the Venezuelan government and the US company, with the government announcing the development in a statement on Friday. The move marks a new development for Starlink's operations in Latin America, as the satellite internet service continues to expand its global presence and subscriber base. Starlink, operated by SpaceX, provides internet connectivity through a network of satellites in low Earth orbit. Its service portfolio has expanded beyond individual consumers to include businesses, aviation, maritime operators and government customers. Reuters reported that Starlink's satellite internet business has continued to grow globally, supported by the launch of additional satellites and an expanding range of services for different customer segments. The company's offerings include connectivity for consumers and enterprises, as well as specialised services for aviation, maritime and government use, broadening its reach across sectors that require internet access in areas where conventional connectivity may be limited. The Venezuelan government's announcement did not provide further details in the information reported by Reuters about the terms of the agreement, the planned launch timeline or the scope of Starlink's proposed operations in the country. The authorisation comes as satellite-based internet services gain a larger role in the global connectivity market, with providers seeking to extend coverage through expanding satellite networks and services tailored to different users. For Starlink, entry into additional markets can support its efforts to increase its international subscriber base and expand the range of applications for its satellite network. However, details about the implementation of the agreement and the availability of Starlink's services to customers in Venezuela remain unclear based on the information reported. Reuters reported the development on October 9, citing the Venezuelan government's statement. This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Apple cuts iPhone 18 Pro orders: Is its premium pricing backfiring? Here's what report reveals
content: Apple has asked some of its suppliers to reduce orders for components used in the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, according to a Reuters report citing Nikkei Asia , raising concerns about demand for the company’s latest premium smartphones. The reported cuts come as Apple has increased prices across its latest Pro lineup. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max is priced at $1,299, marking a $100 increase for each model compared with its predecessor. Apple unveiled its iPhone 18 lineup at an event in New York on September 9. However, the company has yet to release a standard iPhone 18 model, which is expected to be introduced in the spring. Also Read | iPhone 18 Pro Max vs Galaxy S26 Ultra camera: Specs, zoom, video and more Apple prepares to launch first foldable iPhone The reported component order reductions come as Apple prepares to launch its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo . The device is scheduled to go on sale on October 23, with preorders opening on October 16. Its starting price is expected to be $1,999. The launch marks a significant product milestone for Apple under chief executive John Ternus, who assumed the role on September 1. Investors will be watching closely to assess whether the foldable device can generate fresh demand and strengthen the company's premium smartphone portfolio. Wall Street weighs pricing against rising costs Investors have been assessing whether higher prices across Apple's latest hardware lineup can offset rising memory costs and sustain the company's profitability. Morgan Stanley maintained a buy-equivalent rating on Apple shares last week but lowered its price target to $355 per share. The brokerage noted that lower-than-expected selling prices for the latest iPhones, combined with higher memory costs, largely offset modest improvements in revenue estimates. As a result, its earnings-per-share projections for fiscal years 2027 and 2028 remained broadly unchanged. The assessment highlights concerns about Apple's ability to maintain higher average selling prices while managing rising component expenses. Earlier downgrade raised concerns over premium pricing Questions about Apple's pricing strategy have been circulating on Wall Street since August, when Jefferies downgraded the stock to underperform. Also Read | iPhone 18 Pro Max vs Pixel 11 Pro XL: Check full camera comparison here The brokerage cited supply chain checks indicating that Apple had cancelled plans for an all-glass iPhone because of low production yields. Analyst Edison Lee had considered the device an important potential driver of higher average selling prices across Apple's smartphone portfolio. The reported production setback added to concerns about the company's ability to introduce new designs that could justify premium pricing. Apple shares retreat from September peak Apple shares were trading at around $329 in early October, down more than 4% from their 52-week high of $345.34 recorded on September 22. Investors will continue to monitor demand for the iPhone 18 Pro models, the impact of higher memory costs and the reception of Apple's first foldable smartphone to gauge the company's growth and earnings prospects.

title: Anthropic restricts internet access in internal AI evaluations after Claude bypasses safeguards, accesses websites
content: New Delhi [India], October 10 (ANI): Artificial intelligence company Anthropic has restricted live internet access across its internal evaluations after discovering instances of its Claude models bypassing safeguards, exploiting software vulnerabilities and accessing systems on real-world websites, including those operated by government agencies. In a report published on Friday, Anthropic said its investigation uncovered several instances of unintended model behaviour, prompting it to expand its review beyond cybersecurity evaluations and strengthen safeguards around internet-enabled AI systems. The company said some incidents involved Claude exploiting basic software flaws to execute commands on servers, submitting sensitive forms on live websites despite instructions not to do so, and circumventing restrictions to access data behind paywalls. Some examples involved websites operated by US federal, state and local government agencies. Anthropic said it had briefed the White House and notified the agencies concerned. In one instance, Claude Mythos Preview encountered an error while using a scientific analysis tool hosted by a university. The model subsequently identified a vulnerability in a script and used it to run commands on the server. In another case, Claude Haiku 4.5 submitted an online form despite being instructed to stop before submission. A separate run submitted a police tip form containing invented information, which was flagged as spam and not forwarded. Anthropic also found instances in which models accessed browser settings and access tokens to retrieve publicly available but fee-restricted information, and used URL-shortening services to get around limits imposed by internet-access tools. The company, however, said the cases identified so far had minimal real-world impact and were substantially less severe than cybersecurity incidents it reported on July 30 and September 9. It added that, to its knowledge, none of the newly identified cases involved customer data or Anthropic's internal systems. In response, Anthropic has expanded restrictions on live internet access across internal evaluations until it can establish that its safeguards and monitoring systems are reliable. It has also discontinued some public evaluations or moved them offline, while updating its web-access tools to detect and block potentially unsafe behaviour. The company said automatic detection and blocking tools had been tested against the reported cases and successfully blocked all of them. It is also removing or fixing training environments that reward models for working around tool restrictions, a behaviour known as reward hacking. Anthropic said it would continue reviewing model transcripts across web-enabled evaluations, internal agent use and training environments, and report further instances as the investigation progresses. It is also expanding alignment training beyond coding to include web search and computer use. The findings highlight the challenges of deploying increasingly capable AI systems that can interact with real-world websites and operate for extended periods. Anthropic said alignment training alone may not be sufficient to prevent unintended actions, making multiple layers of safeguards, restricted access and continuous monitoring necessary as AI capabilities advance. (ANI)

title: Anthropic AI model submits false homicide tip to police website
content: Oct 9 (Reuters) - An Anthropic artificial intelligence model submitted a false homicide tip through a Philadelphia police website, the department said in a statement, the latest incident of an AI model going rogue and behaving with unintended consequences. Anthropic notified the police earlier this week and said that an automated testing process was responsible for the submission, according to the police. The fast-advancing technology has become a matter of keen national interest amid reports of AI agents running amok and hacking into corporate computer networks, and warnings from prominent researchers that it could one day pose an existential threat to humanity. In September Anthropic rival OpenAI apologized for the hacking of an Australian government website by a rogue AI agent, the first known instance of an AI agent hacking a government website. The Philadelphia police department said the tip "was flagged as spam and was never forwarded to the Real-Time Crime Center for investigative vetting or dissemination," and added that Anthropic had told them the company intended to publish a report on the incident on Friday. Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Pennsylvania law specifies it is generally a misdemeanor crime for "a person" to knowingly give false reports to law enforcement authorities. This includes "information relating to an offense or incident when he knows he has no information relating to such offense or incident." Anthropic told the police the testing process was stopped after the incident was uncovered. The false tip was submitted through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com concerning an unsolved homicide. The tip, dated July 18, 2026, purported to come from someone who might have information about the case, the police said. Police said they did not have any evidence of unauthorized access to its systems or compromise of police department data. (Reporting by Costas Pitas; Additional reporting by Deepa Seetharaman and Davdi Bario; Editing by David Gregorio)

title: Amazon launches Alexa Tablet 8, Tablet 11 and Tablet 12 Pro with Google Play Store access: Price, key specs and more
content: Amazon has launched three new tablets globally: the Alexa Tablet 8, Alexa Tablet 11 and Alexa Tablet 12 Pro. The new lineup runs on Android and supports the Google Play Store, giving users access to a wider range of apps. The tablets also feature Alexa+ AI, MediaTek processors and access to Amazon services, including Prime Video, Audible and Amazon Music, according to Amazon’s official press release published on October 8. The new tablets target different user segments, from everyday entertainment and reading to productivity and creative work. The Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is the flagship model, featuring a 12-inch display, a 120Hz refresh rate and support for a dedicated keyboard and stylus. The devices are available in North America from October 9, with shipping scheduled to begin on October 14. European availability is expected to follow on October 19. Amazon Alexa Tablet 8, Tablet 11 and Tablet 12 Pro: Price and availability The Amazon Alexa Tablet 8 starts at $229.99 (approximately Rs. 19,300) for the 4GB RAM and 64GB storage variant. It comes in Graphite, Rosette and Teal colour options. View full Image Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro. Also Read | Apple Home Hub, new HomePod Mini and Apple TV could debut on 13 October The Alexa Tablet 11 is priced from $329.99 (approximately ₹ 27,700) for the 8GB RAM and 64GB storage model. It is available in Graphite, Amethyst and Matcha. The flagship Alexa Tablet 12 Pro starts at $499.99 (approximately ₹ 42,000) for the 8GB RAM and 128GB storage variant. The Nanomatte display version costs $549.99 (approximately ₹ 46,000). Amazon has also launched accessories for the Pro model. The Pro Keyboard costs $149.99, while the Pro Pen is priced at $89.99. The tablets are available through Amazon and select retailers, including Best Buy and Target. Prices and availability for India have not been announced. Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro: Specifications and features The Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro features a 12-inch display with 2.5K resolution, a 120Hz refresh rate, 280ppi pixel density and a 3:2 aspect ratio. Buyers can choose a standard screen or a nanomatte variant with an anti-glare coating. The tablet is powered by an octa-core MediaTek Dimensity 8400 processor and is listed with configurations of up to 16GB RAM and 256GB storage. It features a 13 MP rear camera, an 8 MP front camera, Wi-Fi 6E and quad Dolby Atmos speakers. Amazon claims up to 16 hours of video playback. The Pro Pen supports USI 2.0, 4,096 pressure levels, tilt detection and wireless charging. The keyboard attaches magnetically without requiring Bluetooth pairing. Amazon Alexa Tablet 11 and Tablet 8: Key specifications The Alexa Tablet 11 sports an 11-inch 2.5K display with a 90 Hz refresh rate and a 16:10 aspect ratio. It runs on a MediaTek 8189 chipset, paired with 8GB RAM and up to 128GB storage. It also includes 8-megapixel front and rear cameras, dual Dolby Atmos speakers and a claimed battery life of up to 15 hours. Also Read | Starlink, Jio or OneWeb? Scindia says India will let customers choose The entry-level Alexa Tablet 8 features an 8.7-inch display and the same MediaTek 8189 chipset. It comes with 4GB RAM, up to 128GB storage, Wi-Fi 6, an 8 MP rear camera and a 5 MP front camera. Amazon claims up to 14 hours of battery life. All three tablets include Alexa+ AI features, hands-free Live Sessions and a dedicated Kindle Sanctuary mode, which is designed to provide up to 20 hours of reading time.

title: Starlink row: Scindia says India will let customers choose their satellite internet provider
content: Jyotiraditya Scindia, Union Communications Minister, on Friday said satellite internet operators, including Starlink, Reliance Jio and OneWeb, can begin commercial services in India only after meeting mandatory security and regulatory requirements, adding that customers will ultimately decide which provider they prefer. Speaking at a CEO roundtable during the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 in New Delhi, Scindia said the government's role is to create a free and predictable framework rather than favour any company or technology. “Government is technology agnostic. Our job is to provide a bouquet of services. It is for customers to choose in a free market what they prefer,” Scindia said. The minister said that India will not tolerate monopolies and has granted all eligible applicants permission to enter the satellite communication sector as satellite communication operators. The minister's remarks come as satellite broadband companies plan to expand their footprint in India, where satellite internet connectivity is expected to help internet access in remote and unserved regions. Reliance Jio has said that the rules to satellite internet service providers should be similar to what is applied to traditional telecom firms, while the government has preferred spectrum allocation without an auction. Elon Musk has also charged that some Indian business leaders are trying to stop Starlink, because they want to maintain their market supremacy. Starlink has obtained a crucial telecom licence in India in June 2025 but has not yet started commercial operations, with the security requirements and decisions on spectrum allocation and other regulatory conditions playing a significant role, according to Indian Express. Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia has stated that the government will not give any special treatment to any company and that all the licensed operators have to meet their own requirements and then go ahead with their services. Starlink, Jio and OneWeb await operational clearance Scindia said operators must satisfy security conditions and complete all regulatory milestones before launching services, even if they have already secured licences. According to the minister, Starlink, Jio and OneWeb have obtained the necessary authorizations to operate satellite communications in India. However, he said each company must separately fulfil security and operational requirements before commencing commercial services. Also Read | India's AI rules coming soon? Vaishnaw flags deepfakes and safety concerns He added that the government is also working on the framework for revenue charges that will apply to satellite communication operators. Amazon Kuiper must complete licensing process Scindia said Amazon's Kuiper remains a prospective entrant and must complete the required licensing and approval process before it can offer services in the country. He said the government will ensure a level playing field for all operators and maintain a competitive market structure rather than allowing any single player to dominate the sector. Government backs technology-neutral approach Scindia underscored the country's strides in telecom coverage, affordability, inclusivity and innovation in the last ten years during the IMC 2026 CEO roundtable, according to a release from the Department of Telecommunications (DoT). Amit Agrawal, Secretary of the DoT, and top industry officials also joined the discussions. Also Read | Google launches Playground to create video games with AI, partners with WIF India's telecom market is the second-largest in the world and the second-largest mobile phone manufacturing hub, Scindia said. He pointed to the development of the domestic semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem as a step towards building an end-to-end technology supply chain. The topic of discussion was about artificial intelligence, cloud computing, next-generation networks and indigenous technology development. Scindia highlighted the need for greater collaboration between the government and industry to create resilient digital infrastructure and India's position as a key player in the global telecom market. (With agency inputs)

title: GTA 6 leaks: Cyberleek reveals gameplay clips, map details and Lucia footage ahead of November 19 launch
content: Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) has reportedly seen another wave of gameplay leaks, with a user or group operating under the name Cyberleek sharing clips and screenshots of Rockstar Games’ upcoming title. The leaks are starting to provide an insight into Vice City, interactions with characters, vehicle customisation and other aspects of the game before it is officially released on November 19th. In October, Cyberleek resurfaced after over 60 days with a video of the game allegedly taking place, lasting more than 24 minutes, featuring both protagonists and races in first-person view, according to RockstarINTEL . On August 20, Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar Games' parent company, issued subpoenas to Microsoft and Discord to identify the leaker, as well as to Google and X Corp. As reported by The Verge , the legal filings referred to “stolen content”, although this does not independently authenticate every leaked clip. GTA 6 leaks: What Cyberleek has revealed so far View full Image GTA 6: New gameplay video reveals major features ahead of November launch. Cyberleek has reportedly posted over 10 clips and map images of how the game plays. Crops from the game's maps are included, featuring Dalton Island, Tequesta Retreat, Gloriana Key and Catalan Key. Another image allegedly shows the complete in-game map. Readers can check confirmed announcements on the official Rockstar Games Newswire. In the clips, Jason is doing things like playing basketball, flying planes over Vice City, driving super-fast cars, avoiding cops and more, including visiting a video game store and a strip club. Other snippets include a car accident at a gas station, a nude group and a fictional healing pill known as Zombix, which gets less effective the more you use it. One clip ends with Jason stealing a hot rod and escaping the police before a cutscene introduces Lucia Caminos, the game’s second playable protagonist. In addition, Cyberleek has created a four-and-a-half-minute video introducing Lucia that includes minor story spoilers. This information is based on leaked footage and media reports and not on any Rockstar disclosures. Also Read | GTA 6 on PC without a console? Xbox clarifies cloud streaming plan What could Cyberleek leak next? View full Image GTA 6: New gameplay video reveals major features ahead of November launch. The current video ends with a reference to a longer-term project, which apparently isn't the latest one. Cyberleek hasn't been clear about what this is or whether there will be more footage. Further leaks remain possible before launch, but their timing and authenticity cannot be established independently. Players are also warned about unverified videos and potential story spoilers circulating on social media. GTA 6 official release date and soundtrack details Rockstar Games has announced the release date for GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S as November 19, 2026. The company hasn't announced a release date for the PC version. Confirmed announcements will be found on the official Rockstar Games Newswire. Also Read | GTA 6 DualSense controller pre‑orders start 10 Sept: Price, launch date Individually, Rockstar has announced six radio stations: Latin music, country, African music, heavy metal, pop, and Southern hip-hop. On-demand podcasts will also be introduced into the game, and players will be able to listen to the world through headphones and earbuds. On September 17, Rockstar announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album , which will include 34 original songs. Six singles have already been released, featuring artists like Travis Scott, Future, Metro Boomin, Keith Richards, Morgan Wallen, and PinkPantheress.

title: MORNING BID EUROPE-Feeding the AI beast
content: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Ankur Banerjee Investor angst over AI bellwethers' seemingly insatiable appetite for capital to build the infrastructure necessary for the technology to start paying off has cast a shadow over markets, as worries about valuations and fears over profitability persist. A series of reports from different corners of the globe has sharpened the focus on the AI trade this week, weighing on technology stocks. OpenAI has told investors its annualised revenue for September was almost $50 billion, a drop from what it signalled earlier, Reuters reported, while in Australia, data centre operator Firmus shelved its $5 billion initial public offering, and said it would opt for a private fundraising round instead. Over in the US, another massive round of fundraising appears to be on the way, with SpaceX, Broadcom and Oracle all expected to raise billions to buy high-end AI chips. Morgan Stanley estimates that AI infrastructure will require $1.5 trillion in external financing by 2028, with fundraising happening just as interest rates across the globe rise to combat the inflationary pressure from higher energy prices. That makes it more expensive to finance facilities whose returns may take years to materialise, while investors are also demanding greater visibility into the customers and cash flows that will support those investments. Meanwhile, public uneasiness with AI, and the small group of people who seemingly hold sway over it, has risen in recent months alongside concern that the technology could pose an existential threat to humanity. Brent crude futures remain above $100 per barrel with the war in the Middle East showing no signs of easing, with bond yields still at elevated levels. A months-long global bond selloff has pushed borrowing costs to multi-decade highs, with much of the pain being felt in France. The pressure built on the country on Thursday as euro zone finance ministers and the European Central Bank told France to pass a 2027 budget to calm bond markets. Key developments that could influence markets on Friday: European Central Bank's Piero Cipollone and Isabel Schnabel speak, Brazil inflation (September), Canada employment (September) (By Ankur Banerjee in Singapore; Editing by Kate Mayberry)

title: South Korea, Japan buffeted by hacks as AI lowers bar for cybercriminals
content: * TrendAI logged more cybersecurity incidents in Japan by September than during all of last year * Experts say AI erodes language and complexity barriers, enabling less-skilled hackers to find flaws * AI is making cybercrime faster, cheaper and harder to detect, experts say By Kyu-seok Shim, Brenda Goh and Kentaro Okasaka SEOUL/TOKYO, - South Korean and Japanese companies are racing to strengthen cyber defences after a wave of attacks that cybersecurity experts say are highlighting how AI may be lowering the bar for criminals with limited technical skills. Nine South Korean banks and two mega-churches are probing cyberattacks that may have involved AI tools, while Japanese companies including Daiwa Securities, SoftBank Corp and the Lawson convenience store chain have been hit by a recent surge in cyber incidents. Authorities are still investigating whether and how AI was used in many of the breaches. But cybersecurity specialists say the technology is helping attackers automate tasks from scanning for software vulnerabilities to crafting phishing campaigns, making cybercrime faster, cheaper and harder to detect. "AI doesn't get tired... My view is that Japan is essentially being subjected to carpet bombing," said Nobuo Miwa, president of Tokyo-based cybersecurity firm S&J Corp. Japan recorded more cybersecurity incidents in the first nine months of the year than in all of last year, according to data from TrendAI. Incidents rose to 86 in September, up about 18% from August and 37% from July. The rise suggests attackers have crossed a threshold in "effort, motivation and technical capability," while AI has largely erased language and other barriers that once hindered foreign hackers, Miwa said. US cybersecurity company CrowdStrike said a suspected 26-year-old China-based attacker behind the South Korean bank incidents would probably not have been able to carry out the campaign without AI assistance. The individual, whom CrowdStrike assessed was pursuing financial gain, used a Chinese-developed AI agent and Anthropic's Claude Code, according to the company. "While capabilities were not terribly sophisticated they were effective," said Adam Meyers, CrowdStrike's senior vice president of counter adversary operations. HARD-TO-DETECT ATTACKS AI-powered tools are also making it harder for defenders to spot suspicious behaviour, said Choi Kyoungjin, director of the Center for AI, Data and Policy at Gachon University near Seoul. "With general-purpose AI models, even ordinary users with malicious intent can ask the system to look for vulnerabilities and it will do much of that work for them," he said. South Korea reported 1,236 cyber incidents in the first half of the year, up 20% from a year earlier. While server hacking cases fell, reports of distributed denial-of-service attacks and ransomware rose 56.7% and 76.8% respectively, according to government data. The South Korean bank incidents underscored the need for stronger security controls and more rigorous testing as AI evolves, Meyers said. "The genie is out of the bottle, so to speak." Although the breaches have not yet resulted in material financial losses, risks could increase if stolen data is used in phishing or similar text-message "smishing" campaigns, Karen Wu, senior analyst at Fitch, wrote in a note. "We expect the incidents to result in regulatory penalties, customer compensation costs, and a sector-wide increase in cybersecurity spending," Wu said. DEFENCES NEED THEIR OWN BREAKTHROUGH Warnings about AI's growing role in cybercrime are increasingly coming from the technology's developers. Alphabet's Google and Anthropic have both warned that AI-assisted attacks are becoming more common globally. “At this point, we can assume that all threat actors are using AI in some capacity and their operations have benefited,” John Hultquist, the chief analyst at Google’s Threat Intelligence Group, said last month. Regulators in Japan and South Korea have begun responding. South Korea's Financial Services Commission has directed financial industry associations, regulators and affected executives to complete a 12-point cybersecurity self-assessment. In Japan, digital transformation minister Toshiharu Furukawa convened a meeting of ministries and agencies on Thursday following the recent attacks. The National Cybersecurity Office plans to issue warnings to businesses. S&J's Miwa said he expected elevated levels of cyberattacks to persist. "The attackers have experienced a breakthrough that has rendered many of the old assumptions obsolete," he said. "Our defences need their own breakthrough as well." This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Apple october launch events: Home Hub, Touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro and OLED iPad Mini tipped
content: Apple is preparing to unveil a new range of hardware products in October 2026, with announcements expected to cover smart home devices, Mac computers and iPads. The company scheduled its first presentation on 13 October on its smart home ecosystem and is expected to present another product around 27 October. The launches could be a major milestone in Apple's strategy under new CEO John Ternus. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple's late-October event will feature its first touch-screen MacBook Pro, alongside a new iPad Mini. The company is also predicted to roll out the next-generation M6 chip to the MacBook Pro and iMac. Apple's 13 October event, first teased with the phrase “Welcome Home” by marketing chief Greg Joswiak, is likely to be dominated by connected home gadgets and Siri's artificial intelligence features. Apple Home Hub, HomePod Mini and Apple TV expected on 13 October The first presentation by Apple will be on Tuesday, 13 October at 9 AM ET (6.30 pm IST). The company will be presenting an online video presentation in addition to in-person media sessions in NYC, according to FoneArena . The anticipated announcements will include Apple's first-ever dedicated smart home hub with a screen, an updated HomePod mini, and an Apple TV refresh. Apple is interested in smart home technology, and Siri's AI capabilities could be pivotal to the new devices, especially as the company attempts to secure a foothold in the market against Amazon and Google. There have also been rumours of possible deals with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric for “connected home” items such as smart doorbells, locks and thermostats. Touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro could arrive later in October Gurman reported that Apple will hold another product presentation on or around 27 October. The event may include new OLED-screen and touchscreen-enabled versions of the MacBook Pro, which would represent a drastic shift in Apple's high-end laptop lineup. Also Read | iPhone 18 in early 2027, iPhone 20 later? Apple may split its launch cycle The laptops are expected to feature a redesigned interface that adapts to touch and traditional keyboard-and-trackpad inputs. They might still include the Dynamic Island interface that Apple is using on its iPhones. Apple has not officially announced product names, specifications or date of launch. OLED iPad Mini and M6-Powered Macs expected Apple is also reportedly working on an iPad mini redesign, featuring an OLED display, a new speaker system and a front-facing camera in landscape mode. Also Read | Apple TV 4K, MacBook Pro, HomePad: What’s coming after September launch The 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac might get the M6 processor upgrades without any change to their exterior appearance. These changes would extend Apple's hardware refresh beyond its plans for touchscreen laptops. Apple has not officially confirmed the 27 October event or the reported devices.

title: Chinese developer makes ARTEX AI agent closed-source after Korean bank hack
content: By Brenda Goh SEOUL, - The Chinese developer of ARTEX said they have converted the AI agent to a closed-source project after cybersecurity firms identified it as a tool used in a recent cyberattack campaign against South Korean banks. "Given the misuse of the tool, the ARTEX project will no longer be updated and will be converted to closed source. No further versions will be released to the public nor will maintenance support be provided," the developer, who uses the GitHub handle "Autumn-27", said on the code-hosting platform on Thursday. They said the original aim of ARTEX was to help enterprises and organizations conduct security risk testing and improve their security capabilities. Without explicitly addressing the South Korean bank attacks, they said they opposed any illegal use of the software and bore no responsibility for conduct that violates laws and regulations. ARTEX's Github page has been taken down, according to Reuters' checks. US cybersecurity firm Crowdstrike said on Wednesday the suspect behind recent cyberattacks at South Korean banks aimed at stealing customers' personal data was likely a ​China-based 26-year-old who used the ARTEX AI agent and Anthropic's Claude Code. Released on GitHub this year, ARTEX is an open-source AI agent designed to automate penetration testing. It is not a standalone large language model but ⁠connects to ​external LLMs such as ChatGPT, Claude and DeepSeek to help organisations test for vulnerabilities in their ​networks. At least nine South Korean banks have disclosed or been reported by local media as targets of cyberattacks since late September, prompting police to launch ​a probe this week and President Lee Jae Myung to call for robust response measures. Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told a regular press briefing on Thursday that the ministry was not familiar with the ​case, adding that China consistently opposes and combats hacking activities. This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: Jio’s 1,600-satellite LEO network: 23 ground stations, remote area coverage and more
content: Reliance Jio has showcased its proposed 1,600-satellite Low Earth Orbit (LEO) network at the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 in New Delhi on Thursday, October 8. There are 23 ground stations in the plan to ensure connectivity in remote villages, islands, and border areas where conventional mobile towers and fibre networks are difficult to deploy, according to Jio’s presentation at India Mobile Congress 2026. The project was unveiled by Jio with its vision, ‘Sovereign Satellite Connectivity'. The network, the company claimed, would be able to cover land and sea areas, as well as areas with more than 600,000 villages. The system will also be integrated with Jio's terrestrial network, establishing a hybrid satellite-to-ground communications network. Jio plans 1,600 LEO satellites and 23 ground stations Jio shared its plans for the constellation during the IMC 2026 presentation, which include about 1,600 LEO satellites and 23 ground stations. These stations would be used to link the satellite network to ground-based infrastructure. Jio stated that the entire value chain should be in India. This includes design, engineering, integration, testing, launch, deployment and operations of a satellite. The firm also has direct-to-device calling in rural areas. Other potential applications can include enterprise connectivity, remote locations, aviation, maritime, government, defence and disaster response. Also Read | Jio users get free Canva Pro for 1 year: Check eligible plans and how to claim Jio targets remote villages, islands and border areas Jio’s display outlines a goal of 100% coverage across land and maritime areas. The company mentioned remote villages, islands and border outposts with low levels of conventional connectivity. The satellite network will not replace Jio's existing terrestrial network, but will be an addition to it. This might enable users to remain connected where fibre rollout and mobile towers are not viable. The 1,600-satellite network is still a proposal Jio explained that the 1,600 satellites and 23 ground stations are under a proposed plan. India's space regulatory body, IN-SPACe, recently, in July 2026, reviewed the proposed constellation, which was found to be technically viable and similar to satellite connectivity systems worldwide. Jio has also approached the government for permission to file applications with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and synced its orbits with other satellite service providers. There have been reports of a phased development schedule, with a test flight in September 2027, 400-450 satellites planned for completion by 2030, and the full constellation by 2035. But Jio didn't reveal any launch timeline for the constellation at IMC 26. Also Read | Jio Platforms aspires to deliver India’s biggest IPO, says Akash Ambani Satellite network aligns with IMC 2026 theme The Prime Minister, Narendra Modi, inaugurated the 10th India Mobile Congress on Thursday, October 8, with the theme ‘Scale Without Boundaries'. Jio called its satellite connectivity vision “reflects” this theme, as it aims to provide network access where traditional telecom infrastructure cannot be deployed due to geographical or deployment constraints.

title: Temple is unlike any smartwatch: Why Deepinder Goyal’s ₹1 lakh Brain Flow tech wearable is sparking buzz
content: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal’s new Temple wearable is drawing attention for a simple reason: it does not sit on your wrist. The device is small and pill-shaped and is attached to the side of the head to monitor aspects of the brain's blood flow. Goyal has said that the applications of Temple could extend beyond fitness tracking, including checking whether pilots are fit to fly. Goyal posted the comments on X on Thursday, October 8, following his announcement that pre-orders in India would open soon. He said that he “certainly would have it on pilots” and noted that perhaps the Indian Air Force can use it to determine who is the fittest for a given mission. However, Temple is not approved, established and certified as a pilot-fitness or aviation safety device at this time. Temple is not your usual smartwatch Temple is designed to fit between the forehead and the ear. It is not like wearing a watch strap; it is secured by disposable adhesive ‘Grips’. According to Goyal and Temple, the device can remain on during activities such as running, swimming and showering. The company states the grips will last up to seven days, but recommends changing them every two to three days, especially when sweating or exposed to dust. The launch version is expected in six colours: True Gold, Rose Gold, Black Mirror, Real Jade, Deep Blue and Purple Funk. Also Read | Google launches Playground to create video games with AI, partners with WIF BrainFlow: The technology behind Temple Temple employs photoplethysmography (PPG), a technology that's also used in smartwatches. But instead of measuring signals from the wrist, Temple places the sensor near the temple. The company calls this system BrainFlow. It is used to monitor the changes in cerebral blood flow. Goyal said the data could eventually be used to provide insights into sleep, recovery, exercise and stress response. BrainFlow does not measure brain activity directly like an EEG, however, and Temple is not able to diagnose medical conditions at this time. What do the studies show? Goyal has published two validation studies. The first had 23 healthy adults who were compared against BrainFlow readings while pedalling and changing posture with Transcranial Doppler measurements. A second study looked at 44 healthy men who participated in 60 sessions. According to results shared by Goyal , BrainFlow showed correlations of up to 0.91 with changes in brain blood volume measured using time-domain near-infrared spectroscopy. Both studies are preprints and have yet to be peer-reviewed. Thus, the results have to be validated independently. Also Read | CMF Watch 3 Pro review: Can its heart rate tracking keep up with daily fitness? Why pilots and air force Goyal's comments are indicative of a potential capability, not an existing one. It is theoretically possible that continuous physiological data could be used to assess a person's condition prior to a high-stakes task. For the time being, there is no evidence that Temple can make a determination on whether a commercial pilot is medically fit to fly. There are still existing medical and regulatory procedures that govern aviation fitness decisions. Temple could cost around ₹ 1 lakh Earlier, Goyal had said that the cost of a Temple in India is around ₹ 1 lakh. The final India price is not yet available. Pre-orders should be available soon, and waitlist users will receive priority . The company is also testing ideas for thought-to-text technology, though he anticipates that it will be several years in the future. For now, the fact that Temple is positioned so uniquely, has BrainFlow technology and has such ambitious future applications, separates it from standard smartwatches and fitness trackers.

title: ‘Cyber fraud does not respect borders’: PM Modi seeks global mechanism at IMC 2026
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday called for a global mechanism to tackle cross-border cyber fraud and the growing threat of deepfakes. PM Modi appealed to governments, technology providers, telecom operators and financial institutions to collaborate to prevent digital fraud reaching users at the 10th India Mobile Congress (IMC) in New Delhi on October 8, 2026. Modi stated that cybercrime is not confined to national boundaries and that the scalability of digital technology requires users to trust it. The Indian nation has also accumulated extensive experience in dealing with cyber fraud and is poised to share it with other nations, he added. Modi urges global action against cyber fraud "Technology achieves scale only when it gains trust," Modi said, according to the Press Information Bureau (PIB) transcript of his October 8 address. He noted that a criminal from one country may target a victim in another country with the assistance of a third country. Coordinated international action has become even more crucial with the introduction of deepfakes that add another layer to the challenge. Modi urged the GSMA and telecoms companies across the globe to help develop a mechanism which can detect and prevent fraud before it reaches customers. Also Read | Google launches Playground to create video games with AI, partners with WIF Phone and data security need stronger safeguards The Prime Minister stated that growth in telecommunications should go hand in hand with enhanced security. For regular users, digital trust means knowing who is calling, verifying it's a real message, and ensuring payments are safe and personal information is protected, he said. "Cyber fraud and cyber crimes do not respect borders," Modi said, stressing that governments, technology companies, telecom operators and financial institutions must work together. These comments follow the adoption of smartphones and internet services as the mainstay of digital payments, education, healthcare and government services in India. Modi highlights ₹ 50 lakh crore DBT transfers Modi also talked about the digital governance framework and mobile-linked banking for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in India. According to the PIB, Modi said nearly ₹ 50 lakh crore had been transferred directly to beneficiaries through the system. He said that the loss of ₹ 5 lakh crore was averted from ‘wrong hands’ due to leakages. The government continued to work hard to curb such wastage and ensure public money reached the target users, Modi said. Also Read | Boston Dynamics appoints former Amazon executive Rohit Prasad as CEO India moving from technology consumer to creator It was also a platform which Modi had used to highlight India's evolving role in the global technology landscape. The nation has shifted from a technology consumption mode to a creation mode and has begun focusing on Indian designs, technology, and IP, he added. He added that the 10th edition of IMC will help chart the course of the next decade in the mobile industry, both in India and across the globe.

title: Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra pre-orders open: Price, specs, 128GB RAM and sale date
content: Microsoft has announced pre-orders for the new 15-inch Surface laptop with Nvidia's RTX Spark platform. The company unveiled the device at its Windows and Surface event in San Francisco on October 7 2026, as a high-performance device for AI workloads that developers, creators, and users can run locally. The Surface Laptop Ultra costs $2,599 (approx. ₹ 2.3 lakh) and will be available for sale from October 16. Microsoft claims that the laptop's unified memory can be expanded to 128GB and used to run large AI models without relying on cloud services. The company also unveiled the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box for developers. Surface Laptop Ultra price and specifications The Surface Laptop Ultra uses Nvidia's RTX Spark Superchip, which consists of the Blackwell RTX GPU and up to 6,144 GPU cores, plus Nvidia's Grace CPU with up to 20 cores and up to 128GB of unified memory, according to Microsoft. The entry model costs $2,599 and includes an 18-core CPU, a 5,120-core GPU, 24GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD. The 32GB RAM and 1TB storage option is available for $3,299. The higher-end 20-core CPU configuration starts at $3,599 with 32 GB RAM. Prices rise to $3,999 for 48GB, $4,299 for 64GB and $5,899 for 128GB RAM. CNET reported on October 7 that the 128GB version was already listed as out of stock. Also Read | Apple Mac Studio M5 Ultra turns desktop into high-powered AI workstation Built for local AI and demanding workloads Microsoft claims the laptop can deliver up to 1 petaflop of AI performance and run AI models with more than 120 billion parameters locally. The company will focus on developers, creators and professionals who want more computing power but don't want to push all workloads to the cloud. The 15-inch PixelSense Ultra display is said to be the brightest Microsoft has ever made for a laptop, and the laptop will also feature a 30% bigger haptic touchpad. It's less than 18 mm thick and weighs less than 4.5 lbs. Magnetic USB-C charging and more ports There are some interesting hardware changes as well, with Magnetic Connect, a magnetic charging interface for USB-C devices, being one of the highlights. The charging port can still be used for data and video. There are also two extra USB-C connectors, HDMI, USB-A, SD card readers and 3.5mm headphone jacks. Microsoft claims it can connect up to three external 4K screens. Also Read | Apple Mac mini with M5 or M6 chip may debut before iPhone 18 Pro event Microsoft expands local AI push Local AI was a big theme of the event. Microsoft has revealed the availability of MAI Code 1.1 flash, DeepSeek V4 flash and Nvidia Nemotron models on Windows for local use. Microsoft also announced that its AI agent, Meta Muse, will be made into a standalone Windows application. The company emphasised Microsoft Execution Containers, intended to isolate AI agents while enabling them to carry out tasks. Surface RTX Spark Dev Box also launched In addition to the laptop, Microsoft announced it will open pre-orders for the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, targeted at AI engineers and developers. It begins at $5,999 and supports up to 128GB and up to 1 petalops of AI performance. In addition, Microsoft is providing up to $1,000 in cash back to customers who trade in an eligible MacBook Pro, an effort to attract professional users to the new Surface Laptop Ultra.

title: One Tech Tip: Lake America backlash fuels interest in Google Maps alternatives
content: Just because Google and Apple are now calling it Lake America doesn't mean everyone has to. After President Donald Trump ordered a new name for Lake Ontario, the two U.S. tech giants quickly fell in line, relabeling the body of water on their digital maps . The move sparked a backlash among some users, already unhappy with the companies' decisions to rename the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America on their maps following a previous Trump edict. The controversy and lingering worries about digital privacy have fueled interest in map services that aren't from Big Tech companies, especially Google Maps, which is the dominant player with about 80% of the market, according to most estimates. Here’s a rundown of some of the most popular free map app alternatives: MapQuest has been around for three decades but was overtaken by the rise of Google. It's now owned by California company System1. Downloads of the MapQuest app surged in early September after Apple renamed Lake Ontario, topping the free app charts in both the U.S. and Canada on Apple's App Store. The MapQuest app has real time traffic updates and turn by turn route guidance, and shows what's nearby, like gas stations and coffee shops. However, the app isn't available outside the U.S. and Canada. But people in other countries can still use the MapQuest website. The company is currently looking into making MapQuest more broadly accessible, after receiving requests for the app from “people in multiple countries," spokesperson Anne Brownlee said. Another granddaddy in the mapping world, TomTom helped popularize GPS route mapping with the 2004 release of its TomTom GO, which the Dutch company says was the world’s first all-in-one portable satellite navigation device. TomTom still sells physical devices but it also has a free map app for Google and Android phones that is designed “exclusively for drivers” with live traffic data and info on road hazards. The TomTom app's mobile interface is clean and basic, with no ads and few extra features or settings. But its focus on drivers means there are no other route options such as walking or cycling. HERE WeGo has been hailed by some as the closest non-Big Tech alternative to Google Maps. It began life as Nokia Maps and is now owned by a consortium of German carmakers including Audi, BMW, and Mercedes-Benz. The free app, available for both iOS and Android devices, offers many of the same features as Google Maps. There's route mapping for various modes of transport — car, public transport, walking, bike and, in some regions, taxi. Like Google Maps, drivers can add multiple stops to routes and users can choose different maps views like terrain, traffic and satellite — but there's no Street View. If mobile signal is spotty or nonexistent, users can download country maps to navigate offline. Offline maps can also be downloaded on Google Maps, but the area is limited and they expire after a year. HERE WeGo is just one of many lesser-known map apps based in the European Union that embrace the bloc’s strict privacy framework known as GDPR. Unlike Google, they don’t rely on vacuuming up masses of user data to sell ads targeted at those users. HERE WeGo's business model is based on licensing deals with businesses like trucking companies. Others sell premium subscriptions alongside free versions. Estonia's Organic Maps is completely free and based on data from the volunteer-run OpenStreetMap database. Netherlands-based OSMand is similar, but a subscription is needed for more than just basic functions. Magic Earth is a Dutch route planner that says it never collects personal data or tracks user movements. Sygic, from Slovakia, is a GPS route navigation app that offers free offline maps, but you’ll have to buy a subscription to get extra features including traffic updates, speed camera warnings and a dashcam function. Mapy.com, from a Czech technology company, is an outdoor route planner known for detailed hiking and trail maps that can be downloaded for use offline. Need to get across town without a car? Citymapper is a free journey planning app that’s a major rival to Google Maps when it comes to finding the best routes around a city on public transportation. The app covers 430 cities around the world and options include bus, subway and ferry routes as well as taxi, rental bike and scooter options. This GPS navigation map is focused on providing route guidance for drivers. It’s known for crowdsourcing real time traffic information such as car accidents and police speed cameras from other drivers. But don’t be fooled by the name. Although it has its own distinct app and branding, Waze is actually owned by Google, which bought it in 2013. ___ Is there a tech topic that you think needs explaining?
