title: Samsung flags $80 billion profit on AI boom, highest quarterly for any tech company
content: By Heekyong Yang and Hyunjoo Jin SEOUL, Oct 8 (Reuters) - Samsung Electronics on Thursday projected its quarterly profit would top 100 trillion won, a world first for a technology company, estimating a nearly nine-fold jump in third-quarter earnings as booming demand for AI chips drove strong memory sales. The world's largest memory chipmaker estimated an operating profit of 107.4 trillion won ($80.17 billion) for the July-September period, slightly ahead of an LSEG SmartEstimate of 106.1 trillion won. The forecast marks Samsung's fourth straight quarter of record operating profit, underscoring a deepening global memory chip shortage as AI infrastructure investment outpaces supply growth, which has driven chip prices up sharply. Samsung and Micron expect the imbalance to persist into 2028, although Chinese competition and a potential slowdown in AI spending pose risks to the longer-term earnings outlook. Samsung's shares moved sideways despite flagging another record profit, slipping 0.2% in early trade versus a 0.5% fall in the benchmark KOSPI. Its share price has slumped more than 25% from a record high in June amid concerns about the durability of the AI boom. Analysts have also recently trimmed their forecasts due to the sharp appreciation of the South Korean currency, which reduces the value of dollar-denominated overseas sales when converted into local currency. "The market's focus has shifted to whether the sharp earnings growth that started a year ago would be sustainable," market analyst Kim Seok-hwan at Mirae Asset Securities said. Analysts expect profit in the fourth quarter to grow 8.2% from the previous quarter, slowing from 20% sequential quarterly growth in the third quarter, with chip price growth abating. Market research firm TrendForce expects conventional DRAM contract prices to rise 10% to 15% in the fourth quarter from the preceding quarter, much slower than a second-quarter surge of ​roughly 60%. The moderation in memory prices is being closely watched by investors after a more than year-long rally that propelled profit margins to record highs for the world's largest memory producers Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron. Third-quarter revenue would likely rise 127% to 195 trillion won from a year earlier, Samsung said. The company will release detailed results, including a breakdown of earnings by business division, on October 29. BIGGER-THAN-EXPECTED MOBILE LOSS Memory chips are expected to account for the bulk of the earnings improvement. Prices have soared due to the tight supply of conventional DRAM and NAND chips as well as growing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), essential for processing vast amounts of data for AI applications. Douglas Kim of Douglas Research Advisory estimated that Samsung's HBM bit shipments expanded by close to 50% quarter-over-quarter in the third quarter, with Samsung trying to narrow the gap with SK Hynix in the HBM market. But the memory chip boom presents a challenge for Samsung's other businesses, particularly its smartphone and consumer electronics divisions, which face mounting pressure from higher component costs. Samsung's mobile business posted a larger-than-expected loss of more than $1 billion in the third quarter, analysts said. Meanwhile, Samsung's contract chipmaking, or foundry, business is expected to remain loss-making because of the burden of fixed costs and still-low utilisation rates, analysts said. However, utilisation is expected to improve over the next several quarters, supported by stronger demand for advanced manufacturing processes. Samsung has been seeking to narrow the gap with industry leader TSMC in advanced contract chip manufacturing. Investors said they would also be closely watching for details of Samsung's shareholder return policy during its earnings call later this month. ($1 = 1,339.5700 won) (Reporting by Heekyong Yang, Joyce Lee and Hyunjoo Jin; Editing by Sonali Paul)

title: Can you play GTA 6 on PC this November? Xbox clarifies cloud streaming plans ahead of launch
content: Grand Theft Auto 6 was reportedly set to become playable on PC through Xbox Cloud Gaming when it launched on 19 November. According to a report in The Verge on 7 October, Microsoft holds the exclusive streaming rights to Rockstar Games' long-anticipated next game, GTA 6, and could be offering a playable version of the title to PC players that doesn't require them to own an Xbox or wait for a native PC version. However, Xbox has disputed the report. Matthew Ball, Xbox Chief Strategy Officer, posted on X that GTA 6 will come to the console on 19 November and will not be available to stream on Xbox or on PC. Xbox Cloud Gaming is not likely to be available to PC gamers when GTA 6 launches, he said. Xbox denies GTA 6 PC cloud streaming The report by The Verge claimed that Microsoft signed a deal with Rockstar Games for exclusive rights to stream GTA 6 . It quoted sources close to Microsoft saying the arrangement could enable the game to be streamed live via Xbox Cloud Gaming when it launches. The report indicated that Xbox chief Asha Sharma had termed the deal as “one thing no other platform owner is doing”. However, Ball rejected the report and posted, “We're excited to bring GTAVI to XBOX on November 19, with a note that GTAVI will NOT be streaming on PC[sic].” Also Read | GTA 6 DualSense controller pre‑orders start 10 Sept: Price, launch date GTA 6 still has no announced PC version Rockstar Games officially announced that GTA 6 will be coming for both Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation 5, and it will release on 19 November. The cloud option would have presented a choice to those who played on PCs rather than consoles. However, there is currently no confirmed way to play GTA 6 on PC at launch. Xbox Cloud Gaming is changing in November The confusion stems from Microsoft's plans for major updates to Xbox Cloud Gaming. More specifically, according to the report by The Verge , a pay-as-you-go option is in the works that would allow users to buy blocks of cloud-streaming hours without signing up for Game Pass. Also Read | GTA 6 new gameplay video released: Jason, Lucia and Vice City revealed Xbox has also revealed the cloud gaming limits for Xbox Game Pass members, which will kick in in November. The amount of cloud gaming time will be higher for Ultimate customers and lower for those who have other subscription tiers, according to Pure Xbox. GTA 6's launch on Xbox Series X|S and PS5 is scheduled for 19 November.

title: Smart glasses privacy concerns grow: Norway, Australia, UK and US curb Meta Ray-Ban use
content: Smart glasses are moving from a futuristic gadget to a growing privacy concern as governments, courts, regulators, and businesses rethink where camera-equipped wearables are allowed. The most prominent feature is Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses, which can capture photos, videos and audio and use AI capabilities, yet appear to be just regular glasses. The concern is that people nearby may not know when they are being recorded. The debate has intensified after Norway proposed a temporary ban on AI glasses in certain public areas. Australia is looking at limitations in the government sector, and courts in the UK and the US have already done so in their jurisdictions. Recent cases in France and the Dutch firms have placed pressure on Meta and other smart glasses makers, Reuters reported. Norway moves towards a temporary ban Norway is making the strongest regulatory move. The Norwegian government, on 5 October, announced its intention to propose a temporary ban on AI glasses in specific public locations, such as parks, beaches, museums, shopping centres and public events. Schools, childcare centres, health care facilities, gyms and places with changing rooms could also be included in the proposal. Torgeir Micaelsen, Minister of Digitalisation and Public Governance of Norway, expressed concern that some people might be photographed, filmed or recorded without their awareness. Norway also intends to establish an expert group to recommend lasting rules. Also Read | How HRMS cuts management costs by 90% and AI helps routine queries by up to 80% Australia explores work restrictions Australia is also reviewing the technology. The federal government in September announced it was considering limiting the use of smart glasses with cameras in government workplaces due to privacy and security concerns, Reuters reported. The move comes as Australian authorities separately work on broader privacy reforms covering emerging technologies. On 31 August, Attorney-General Michelle Rowland announced that one of the technologies of concern was smart glasses that used AI as more people gain access to such devices. UK and US courts restrict smart glasses In the UK, courts have banned the use of Meta smart glasses due to existing restrictions on recordings in court. On 20 August, the UK Cinema Association also announced that some cinema operators were rolling out measures to limit or ban the use of camera-enabled smart glasses due to privacy and film piracy concerns, Reuters reported. Starting 20 July, the Unified Court System in New York, USA, banned smart glasses in courthouses. The rule applies to all eyewear that has a camera, microphone or other technology that can record audio or video. Also Read | Should AI agents have the power to act without asking us first? Privacy backlash spreads across Europe The problem is also spreading to France and the Netherlands. The investigations by Paris prosecutors were initiated in September after complaints of women being filmed without their consent through connected glasses. Meanwhile, Dutch retailer Hans Anders suspended sales of Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses in the Netherlands and Belgium on 2 October, citing growing public and political concerns. Meta claims that the glasses include an LED light to indicate when they're recording and anti-tampering features. However, regulators and governments are increasingly wondering if that protection is sufficient. The larger issue for the industry is now whether smart glasses can record people. The question is whether society is comfortable with always-available cameras on people's faces in everyday public spaces, according to the Reuters report.

title: McDonalds sued over AI tool that recommends prices to US franchisees
content: McDonald’s is facing a federal lawsuit that alleges its AI-enhanced pricing tool violates antitrust laws because it shares nonpublic data with franchisees who might be competing in the same market. The lawsuit, which was filed Friday in Illinois, said McDonald’s pricing tool uses artificial intelligence to collect data that competing franchises wouldn’t normally share, like store-level sales. The Chicago-based burger giant has said it makes the tool available to U.S. franchisees to help them set prices at their individual restaurants. The lawsuit also blames the pricing system for raising McDonald’s U.S. prices. “McDonald’s has built and for years deployed its own information-sharing pricing platform, which draws on data from its millions of daily transactions to set menu prices across thousands of U.S. restaurants,” the lawsuit states. “The result is algorithmic price-fixing aimed at customers who are already stretched thin.” McDonald’s said Tuesday that the lawsuit is “filled with inaccuracies” and it would vigorously defend itself. “AI does not set menu prices at McDonald’s restaurants – McDonald’s franchisees do,” the company said in a statement. “Optional tools are available to franchisees to help them make the best decisions for their businesses and customers, but these tools do not automate, coordinate or fix pricing in any way.” The lawsuit was filed on behalf of a consumer, Michael Thomas, of DeKalb, Illinois. According to the lawsuit, Thomas frequently visits McDonald’s and orders a Quarter Pounder with cheese, french fries and a Coke. The lawsuit said Thomas noticed price differences between McDonald’s stores near his home. McDonald's said it has used an AI-enhanced pricing tool for more than a decade. The program determines the optimal price for menu items based on a store’s sales, location and other factors, including competitors’ prices. McDonald's said that long before adopting the AI-enhanced tool, it collected data and recommended prices to its franchisees, who own and operate 95% of McDonald’s 14,000 U.S. stores. “All we do is provide the context of what’s going on,” a McDonald’s spokesman told The Associated Press. “We don’t have any way to affect the menu pricing in a restaurant.” But the lawsuit said McDonald's has “significant leverage over its franchisees” and can pressure them to follow its pricing recommendations. The Associated Press left a message Tuesday with the National Owners Association, which represents McDonald’s franchisees. McDonald’s has been experimenting with various value strategies in the U.S. and other markets for several years as it tries to win back lower-income consumers, whose visits to fast-food chains have dropped. But franchisees don’t always follow its guidance. During a conference call with investors in August, McDonald’s Chairman and CEO Chris Kempczinski said only 60% of its U.S. restaurants were offering McDonald’s proposed menu of 10 items for under $3. “As you know, in our system, that’s not something that we just flip the switch on,” Kempczinski said. “It requires conversations with franchisees.” The lawsuit asks the judge to certify the case as a class action and to require McDonald's to pay damages to the class. It also seeks to prevent McDonald's from enforcing agreements that restrict competition. This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: World Bank says India should scale small AI applications instead of betting heavily on frontier models
content: New Delhi [India], October 6 (ANI): India should focus on expanding the use of existing artificial intelligence applications across the economy and selectively invest in frontier AI capabilities instead of making broad investments in developing advanced models from scratch, Vincent Belinga, Senior Economist at the World Bank, told ANI in an exclusive conversation. Belinga said India should follow a three-stage approach to AI development: adoption, adaptation and frontier development. "One is adoption, meaning using existing application. The second is adaptation, meaning taking open source AI and adapting them to local conditions. And then the third stage is frontier model, meaning developing the next capability from scratch," Belinga said. He said India's immediate priority should be to deepen AI adoption among firms and workers, as adoption is increasing but remains limited across the economy. "What we recommend for India is doing the two. Meaning, deepening adoption so that many firms, millions of firms, millions of workers use AI more productively because so far we see that adoption is increasing but not broad based," he said. Belinga said India already has promising AI applications in areas such as education and healthcare, but many of these initiatives are either limited to specific states or remain at the project stage. The focus, he said, should be on taking such applications to a larger population. "Some promising small AI in education, in health that are either state specific or that are still at project level. So, what we need is to scale up these initiatives so that they are broadly shared across all the states or enriching the broader population," he said. The World Bank report highlights local AI applications in India, including Bhashini and AI4Bharat for multilingual access to services, DIKSHA for personalised learning, KATHIR and the PM-KISAN chatbot for agriculture, and AI-assisted tuberculosis screening from chest X-rays. Belinga said broad-based deployment across sectors would be more important for India than relying on productivity gains from only a few industries. "AI is going to raise productivity," he said, adding that India needs to ensure that AI is adopted across sectors and by workers. The World Bank estimates that 14 per cent of Indian workers are in jobs where AI can complement their work and raise productivity. It also estimates that AI could add 0.1-0.8 percentage points to annual labour productivity growth over the next decade, depending on the pace of AI deployment and complementary investments. Belinga said India should also be selective in developing frontier AI capabilities because such development requires significant resources. "Frontier development is very resourceful. I mean, you see what happening in the US, you have billions of dollar to be invested in frontier development. And given that India has competing development needs, what we suggest is to invest selectively in frontier capabilities where India has a comparative advantage," he said. He said the broader objective should be to deploy smaller AI applications across sectors such as education, healthcare, agriculture, finance and IT so that productivity gains are spread across the economy rather than concentrated in individual sectors. "So you have to make sure that broadly, AI is being adopted and you deploy these small applications across all the economy so that we can have larger productivity gain instead of having productivity gain at sectoral level," Belinga said. (ANI)

title: India among top 10 emerging markets in AI readiness; private AI investment triples: World Bank
content: New Delhi, Oct 6 (PTI) India is among the top 10 leading emerging-market performers in artificial intelligence (AI) readiness and is well positioned to harness the technology, helped by its large technical workforce, globally integrated IT sector and digital public infrastructure, the World Bank said on Tuesday. In its latest report titled 'India and Artificial Intelligence: Seizing the Development Opportunity', the World Bank said private investment in AI in India more than tripled to USD 4.1 billion in 2025 from USD 1.2 billion in 2024. At the same time, the number of professionals employed by Global Capability Centres (GCCs) rose to 2.36 million in 2025 from 1.9 million a year ago, it said. The report, however, noted that the long-term economic and labour market impact of AI remains uncertain. It called for cross-cutting policy measures to deepen AI-enabling infrastructure, improve the business environment, broaden access to AI and enhance labour capacity so that the benefits of the technology are widely shared. "India is one of the top 10 leading emerging-market performers on AI readiness," said Paul Procee, World Bank Acting Country Director for India. "Harnessing AI as a development tool – not just a technology – could be one of the most powerful levers India has to boost productivity and improve public services," he said. The World Bank Group is also investing through AgriConnect in 'small AI' targeted and locally adapted tools aimed at ensuring that the benefits of AI reach a wider section of the population while supporting workers through the transition, he said. The India Development Update is a companion to the World Bank Group's South Asia Economic Update, which examines economic developments and prospects in the region. The latest South Asia Economic Update projects that South Asia will grow 6.9 per cent in 2026, retaining its position as the world's fastest-growing region, the report said. For most of South Asia, the biggest gains from AI are likely to come from adopting and adapting the technology to local conditions, including through small AI applications suited to low-resource settings, it said. The report said complementary measures would also be needed to reduce barriers to AI adoption by small firms, promote local AI innovation and establish a clear regulatory framework that reduces uncertainty while safeguarding data security and privacy. "The adoption of AI has the potential to transform South Asia's development trajectory by boosting labour productivity, expanding export opportunities, and improving public service delivery," said Franziska Ohnsorge, World Bank Group Chief Economist for Asia. "But to reap these benefits, governments need to address the foundational gaps that hold back adoption," she said. The Update recommended strengthening workforce skills, creating a more business-enabling environment and improving physical as well as digital infrastructure.

title: UK watchdog opens first Online Safety Act probe into Meta
content: By Paul Sandle LONDON, Oct 6 (Reuters) - Britain's communications regulator opened its first formal investigation into Meta under the Online Safety Act on Tuesday, questioning whether it properly assessed risks posed by its Instagram Instants feature before launching it in May. Instants allows content shared by users on Instagram to disappear after being viewed. Ofcom said its investigation would establish whether Meta carried out a "suitable and sufficient" assessment of the risks of illegal content on the feature and any risks posed to children before its launch. George Lusty, director of enforcement at Ofcom, said: "Our online safety laws are clear — significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched." Safety by design had to be built in and not bolted on, he said. "Today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," he said. Meta said it took its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously. "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," a spokesperson said. "Instants has in-built protections, including blocking screenshots, reshares and forwarding, no public feed, and Teen Account protections on automatically." "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation," the spokesperson said. Ofcom's first investigation under the Online Safety Act was into an online suicide discussion forum last year, followed by probes into pornography sites, file-sharing services used to distribute child sexual abuse material, and platforms such as 4chan. Britain's online safety regime sets obligations for social media platforms, search engines and adult content providers to tackle illegal content and to protect children's safety. Ofcom requires companies to conduct risk assessments and implement safety measures, such as age verification. If a company fails to comply, Ofcom can impose fines of up to £18 million or 10% of qualifying worldwide revenue, whichever is greater. Meta has launched legal challenges against Ofcom over its implementation of the act, including the scale and scope of information it has to provide to the regulator and the level of fees Ofcom charges. In January, Ofcom launched an investigation into Meta over the provision of information about its WhatsApp Business product under a separate Communications Act. (Reporting by Raechel Thankam Job in Bengaluru and Paul Sandle in London; Editing by Mrigank Dhaniwala, Sarah Young and Tomasz Janowski)

title: Vivo V80 launched in India with Zeiss cameras, 7,200mAh battery: Check specs, price and sale date
content: Vivo has launched the V80 and S2 FE in India on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, expanding its smartphone portfolio ahead of the festive season. The V80 is designed for those who want a smartphone with camera capabilities, while the S2 FE is designed for users who prefer a large battery and mid-range performance. The Vivo V80's price in India starts at ₹ 62,999 and is powered by a Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 chipset, a 7,200 mAh battery, and Zeiss-branded cameras. The S2 FE is priced at ₹ 38,999 and powered by a 10,000 mAh battery, a MediaTek Dimensity 7300e processor and a 120 Hz AMOLED display. Vivo has already announced the October 6 launch date in India. Vivo V80: Design and display Vivo V80 has a glass back, an aerospace aluminium frame and a large rear camera module. According to Vivo's official specifications, the phone measures 7.69 mm thick and weighs 203 grams. It is also dustproof (IP68) and waterproof (IP69). It gets a 6.59-inch 1.5K AMOLED display with a refresh rate of up to 144 Hz. Vivo claims a peak brightness of 5,000 nits and 1.07 billion colours. The phone comes in the Sunrise Anthem, Horizon Blue and Stellar Black colours. Also Read | Vivo V80 India launch date, camera, battery and display details confirmed Vivo V80 cameras and performance The V80 features a triple camera system of a 50 MP ZEISS OIS main camera, a 50 MP ZEISS telephoto camera with 3x optical zoom and an 8 MP ZEISS ultra-wide camera. There's also a 50MP ZEISS autofocus selfie camera. For video, Vivo says the phone supports 4K recording at 60fps and includes cinematic LUT options. The Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 chipset powers the handset, while LPDDR4X RAM and UFS 3.1 storage provide memory and storage. It is based on Android 17 and OriginOS 7 OS. The V80 features 7,200 mAh of battery with 90W fast charging support. According to Vivo , this is the largest battery in Vivo V-Series smartphones released in India to date, as of 6th October 2026. Also Read | Vivo V80 Lite 5G launches with 120Hz AMOLED display, 7,050mAh battery Vivo S2 FE: Display, camera and battery Vivo S2 FE is equipped with a 6.83-inch 1.5K AMOLED display and a 120 Hz refresh rate, and supports up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness. It is powered by the MediaTek Dimensity 7300e chipset. The phone features a 50 MP Sony IMX852 primary rear camera and a 2 MP secondary camera. A 32 MP camera handles selfies. Its most notable feature is the 10,000 mAh battery that comes with 44 W charging. The mobile has OriginOS 6, which is based on Android 16. Vivo V80 and S2 FE price and sale date The Vivo V80 is priced at ₹ 62,999 for 8GB RAM and 128GB storage. The 8GB/256GB and 8GB/512GB variants cost ₹ 69,999 and ₹ 79,999, respectively. The Vivo S2 FE costs ₹ 38,999 for the 6GB/128GB variant and ₹ 42,999 for the 8GB/128 GB variant. These prices are preliminary and are now included in the launch details. The Vivo V80 will launch on October 13, and the Vivo S2 FE on October 20. Both smartphones will be available for purchase on Vivo's official website, on Flipkart, or at retail stores.

title: Is era of affordable smartphones ending? HMD India CEO warns prices may stay high till 2027
content: The era of ultra-affordable smartphones could be coming under pressure as rising costs of memory and other components push device prices higher, said Ravi Kunwar, VP & CEO, HMD India-APAC, in an exclusive interview with LiveMint during the HMD Vibe 2 Pro 5G launch in India. He added that cost pressures may persist in the industry until the end of 2027. Kunwar said that HMD is focusing on features that will be useful in practice, battery life, and those specifically helpful in the Indian market, rather than going into an aggressive price war. The company has officially introduced the Vibe 2 Pro 5G at discounted prices, starting from ₹ 14,999 for the 6GB RAM configuration and ₹ 16,999 for the 8GB RAM configuration, and it will be available for sale from 8 October during Flipkart's Big Billion Days sale. Rising component costs could keep phones expensive In the interview, Kunwar said smartphone component prices have risen considerably over the last six months, especially those of memory prices. Growing demand for memory due to artificial intelligence (AI) is part of that pressure, he said. Manufacturers will continue to seek to optimize their supply chains and costs, but that pressure is not expected to last long, Kunwar said. “The challenge is going to remain till probably the good end of 2027,” he added. As the high input costs become universal, “consumers will have to get used to the higher prices of smartphones,” he shared. Also Read | HMD Vibe2 Pro 5G launched: First impressions of the new smartphone HMD targets value-conscious buyers The pressure might be greater in the sub- ₹ 20,000 smartphone price band, which accounts for about 40% of the Indian smartphone market, Kunwar said. He added that consumers facing higher prices could delay upgrades. With this, HMD is shifting the Vibe 2 Pro 5G's focus toward features targeted at heavy users. The smartphone gets a 6,000mAh battery, 33W fast charging, dual speakers, dual microphones and a MediaTek Dimensity 6300 processor. It also comes with a 120Hz display. Kunwar said the upgrades were driven by customer feedback following the Vibe 2 5G, which continues to have a 4.5-star rating on Flipkart, according to HMD. Sarvam AI brings local language focus HMD also hopes AI will help it differentiate its phones in India. Vibe 2 Pro 5G has been enhanced with Sarvam AI, which will support 22 Indian languages and take into account regional and cultural contexts. Kunwar said the goal is to make AI a regular part of consumers' lives, particularly beyond India's major metropolitan areas. Also Read | Vivo V80 India launch date, camera, battery and display details confirmed HMD plans to expand beyond entry-level phones Kunwar said that HMD is not planning to stick with the affordable smart devices. The company is slowly climbing the price ladder, having introduced its products at ₹ 10,000 and later in the ₹ 14,000- ₹ 17,000 range. Eventually, he said, the company wants to be a full-line player in each smartphone price segment. “Our motto is not about being the loudest in the marketplace; it is about being the most trusted,” Kunwar said.

title: South Koreas Lee says AI appears to have been used in bank hacks
content: SEOUL, - South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Tuesday that AI models are believed to have been used in some recent hacking incidents against banks and called for the country to develop cybersecurity methods suited to the AI era. • "In some hacking incidents, signs have emerged of AI being used, causing considerable public concern and anxiety," Lee said during a cabinet meeting. "Please establish the circumstances swiftly and clearly, and concentrate personnel and resources on minimising the damage." • South Korea's police have launched a full-scale investigation into the hacking attacks against commercial banks that led to a breach of customers' personal information, the Yonhap news agency reported on Tuesday. • Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and others had reported cyberattacks, the Financial Services Commission said on Friday, while Yonhap reported that Hana Bank and Woori Bank had also suffered breaches. • Authorities have not yet disclosed details on what kind of AI tools were used in the hacking incidents or the full scale of the breaches. • On Sunday, FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon convened an emergency meeting with financial industry associations, regulators and executives from affected institutions, warning that the sector must respond with the highest level of vigilance. • In September, Australia said an OpenAI agent breached a government health data portal in June, gaining unauthorised access to files, in what could be the ‌first known instance of an AI agent hacking a government website. • An artificial intelligence research firm said last week that AI agents tried to hack into a Canadian government website, casting the effort as a failed hacking attempt, while Canada said there were ​no indications its systems were compromised. This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: UP govt aims to establish Lucknow among Indias leading AI innovation cities: Yogi Adityanath
content: Lucknow, Oct 6 (PTI) Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday said the state government aims to establish Lucknow among India's leading AI innovation cities and will support at least 50 AI-focussed startups in the city over the next five years. Addressing an event marking the 10th anniversary of HCLTech's Lucknow campus, Adityanath called on the IT major to partner with the government in developing a strong AI innovation ecosystem in the state capital. The chief minister said the government would provide full support to establish, strengthen and help the startups access global markets. "We have to make Lucknow not just a centre for IT services but a major hub for AI, semiconductors, cyber security, computing technology and deep tech," he said, stressing the need for the government and industry to work together. Adityanath said HCL's journey in Lucknow was a matter of pride for Uttar Pradesh, noting that founder Shiv Nadar had started his journey from the state nearly five decades ago. "HCL chose Lucknow and Lucknow adopted HCL," he said, adding that the company's campus, established 10 years ago, had given a new dimension to the partnership. He said the success of the campus was not merely about business or employment, but was also linked to the aspirations of families whose children had found career opportunities in the city. Referring to the state's workforce, Adityanath said Uttar Pradesh's young and talented population was its biggest strength. "Today, I proudly say that I have India's youngest workforce, and its talent is my greatest strength," he said. Adityanath further said that a decade ago, young people from Uttar Pradesh often had to move to Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad for better career opportunities, but the situation had changed and young people were now choosing Lucknow for their careers. The chief minister said Uttar Pradesh's infrastructure and connectivity had also expanded significantly. The roughly 1,200-km journey from Ballia to Bijnor could now be completed in about 10 hours, compared with several days a decade ago, he said. On the state's IT and electronics sector, Adityanath claimed Uttar Pradesh accounted for around 55 per cent of India's mobile manufacturing and nearly 60 per cent of the electronic components manufactured in the country. He said the state's IT and IT-enabled services exports, which stood at around ₹ 12,000-15,000 crore a decade ago, had crossed ₹ 1 lakh crore and the government was targeting ₹ 2.5 lakh crore over the next four years. Electronics exports have also risen from around ₹ 3,800 crore a decade ago to ₹ 45,000 crore, with a target of ₹ 2 lakh crore by 2030, he said. Adityanath said the IT sector was no longer limited to Noida, with IT parks operating in Lucknow, Kanpur, Prayagraj, Meerut and Agra. Seven Software Technology Parks are operational in the state, while new IT parks are being developed in Varanasi, Bareilly, Kanpur and Gorakhpur, he said. He said Noida and Lucknow were being developed as deep-tech hubs under the new startup policy and work was progressing on developing an AI city and a broader AI ecosystem in Lucknow. The CM also highlighted HCL's social initiatives in Uttar Pradesh, saying its programmes had reached more than 50 lakh people and over 3,000 villages during the past 10-11 years. He said HCL had contributed to education, rural livelihoods and community development through its initiatives in districts including Sitapur and Bulandshahr. "Development does not mean merely building large campuses in big cities. Real development is when a farmer in a village gets access to better technology, women get new livelihood opportunities, children get better education and healthcare, and rural youth become part of the new economy," Adityanath said. HCLTech Chairperson Roshni Nadar Malhotra said Uttar Pradesh was the "karmabhoomi" and home of the HCL Group and that the company had an "unwavering belief" in the state's talent and opportunities.

title: Tablet shipments decline 3.8 pc YoY, hit by memory price inflation: Report
content: New Delhi, Oct 6 (PTI) Tablet PC shipments in India declined by 3.8 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026 due to a rise in memory chip prices, market research firm Counterpoint Research said on Tuesday. The tablet PC segment priced below ₹ 20,000 was most impacted by the memory price hike, with a 43 per cent dip in supplies during the reported quarter. "Tablet shipments in India declined 3.8 per cent YoY in Q2 2026. The decline was driven by brands starting to pass higher input costs on to consumers, increasing overall selling prices. India's tablet market has begun to face pressure from memory price inflation, more prominently from Q2 2026 onwards," the research firm said. Counterpoint Research said that the brands have increased prices across their portfolios and streamlined memory variants. "The sub- ₹ 20,000 segment, which has traditionally formed the backbone of India's tablet market, was most impacted by the memory price hike, declining 43 per cent YoY in Q2. The above ₹ 20,000 segment emerged as a key battleground, growing 27 per cent and capturing 74 per cent of the market. This was driven by brands increasing prices and streamlining their portfolios, with consumers moving towards premium products," Counterpoint Research Principal Analyst Anshika Jain said. According to the firm, the shift towards the higher-price segment resulted in a 15 per cent increase in average selling price, she said. "There has been a notable movement in the market towards larger screen sizes, especially for screens larger than 12 inches, at a price point greater than ₹ 20,000, as consumers increasingly view the tablets as a secondary screen," Jain said. The ₹ 20,000 to ₹ 30,000 price band saw strong growth of 45 per cent YoY, supported by brands such as OnePlus and Lenovo. Despite a dip in supplies, domestic manufacturing grew 30 per cent YoY in Q2, as established players, such as Samsung and Lenovo, continued to expand their local production. "Brands including OnePlus and OPPO are also deepening their manufacturing presence in India. On the demand side, the impact of elevated memory prices is expected to continue in festive seasons, though the promotions might provide some support to demand," Jain said.

title: Frances Mistral announces new AI model
content: By Elizabeth Howcroft and Leo Marchandon PARIS, Oct 6 (Reuters) - French AI company Mistral on Tuesday announced a new AI model, which the company said outperforms some Chinese open-weight models. The 3-year-old startup is seen as Europe's best hope of fielding a home-grown competitor to US and lower-cost Chinese rivals. Mistral had not released a new model since May, and in August started making third-party models available to its customers, starting with Beijing-based Z.ai's GLM 5.3. Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch told a conference in Abu Dhabi that the new product beat Chinese models on some aspects, "including cyber", without giving details. Pierre Stock, Mistral's vice president of science, told Reuters that it ranked among the best open-weight options. Mistral said Le Chonk - officially named Mistral Large 4 - will be made fully public on October 27. In a preview period, some cybersecurity experts and state authorities will have access to a version with fewer safety barriers to test its capabilities, Mistral said. SAFETY FEARS Stock told Reuters the new model had tried to go beyond its testing environment, but attempts had been contained using software. OpenAI and Anthropic, whose models escaped their testing environments, have restricted access to their most cyber-capable systems. Mistral will release its model open-weight, meaning anyone can download and run it on their own servers. When US executives last month said AI could pose an existential threat to humanity, Mensch said the incumbents' comments were self-serving. Mistral, which raised €3 billion in its latest funding round, positions itself as a safer, European alternative. DESIGNING CHIPS Mistral said Large 4 is "closing the gap with frontier models" on coding, finance, geospatial analysis, manufacturing and product design. Mistral has trained the model on its own infrastructure. Stock said its goal is to partner "very deeply" with backers including ASML and new-investor Samsung "across the entire value chain". Stock said that Large 4 is capable of designing computer chips, but declined to comment on whether Mistral is currently developing chips with Samsung. (Reporting by Elizabeth Howcroft in Paris and Leo Marchandon in Gdansk. Additional reporting by Federico Maccioni in Abu Dhabi. Editing by Louise Heavens)

title: Poco X8 Power review: Great battery life and striking design, but does it justify ₹35,999 price tag?
content: POCO has recently launched the X8 Power in India, marking the company’s first smartphone in the country to cross the massive 10,000mAh battery threshold. The phone is priced at ₹ 35,999 and is designed for people looking for long battery life but don't wish to switch to a rugged or oversized phone. The X8 Power is also equipped with a 6.83-inch AMOLED screen, a Snapdragon 6 Gen 5 processor and a 50MP camera with IP69K waterproofing. The big question is whether the massive battery is enough to make the X8 Power stand out in the crowded mid-range segment. For users, particularly those with long workdays or lots of travelling, the answer is mostly yes. The mobile phone can extend beyond a day and, on moderate use, has a two-day battery life. However, its cameras and performance leave some room for improvement. View full Image Poco X8 Power box content. ( Pragya Singha Roy ) Battery The biggest attraction is obvious. The X8 Power sports a 10,000 mAh battery, eliminating most of the battery worries. I discovered that the handset was able to hold approximately 40-45% of its battery charge after an average workday. With moderate use, it lasted about two days. It might be possible to extend it to three days for lighter users. View full Image Poco X8 Power battery test. The phone scored 26 hours and 44 minutes in the PCMark battery test. It is also capable of 100W charging, but charging such a large battery is not necessarily fast. During testing, a full charge of the battery can be done in approximately 30-50 minutes. There is also 27W reverse charging. That makes the X8 Power a handy power source for another phone in an emergency. Also Read | CMF Watch 3 Pro review: Can its heart rate tracking keep up with daily fitness? Design Poco has taken a different design pattern for the X8 Power. The yellow variant gets a vegan leather back, a contrasting black frame and a camera module. It looks more unique than standard mid-range phones made up of glass and metal . View full Image Poco X8 Power. ( Pragya Singha Roy ) At 8.65 mm thick and 223 grams, the X8 Power is not light. This is partially due to the large battery. However, it's not so heavy that it feels excessively bulky, especially for a phone that has such a large battery. It is also dust and water-resistant with an IP69K rating. This is an extra security feature for people who spend a lot of time outside. Display The X8 Power is equipped with a 6.83-inch 120Hz refresh 1.5K AMOLED screen. The bezels are thin and uniform, and the Gorilla Glass Victus 2 is protected. Poco is claiming up to 3,500 nits of peak brightness. The outdoor visibility was good, as were the punchy colours, making it well-suited for video streaming. The panel is capable of displaying the entire DCI-P3 colour gamut, HDR performance on Netflix and HDR on YouTube. There are stereo speakers with Dolby Atmos for enhanced entertainment. Performance Qualcomm's Snapdragon 6 Gen 5 chipset is used in the X8 Power. The POCO X8 Power is the first smartphone in India to feature this new processor. Performance is quite good for normal use. Apps launch in a timely fashion, and application switching is usually easy. However, occasional stutters can appear during heavier multitasking. View full Image Poco X8 Power. This isn't a performance-first smartphone, though you can still play games. The game is able to support a max of 90 fps but can drop to lower frame rates during extended gameplay. Geekbench 7 scored 915 points in single-core and 2,851 points in multi-core tests. The variants have an important storage difference. The 256GB version receives faster UFS 4.1 storage, in addition to LPDDR5X RAM. The 128GB variant's storage is based on UFS 2.2. Cameras View full Image Poco X8 Power wide shot. View full Image Poco X8 Power. View full Image .. View full Image .. View full Image Poco has given the X8 Power a 50MP Sony IMX882 primary camera and an 8MP ultrawide camera. Poco has given the X8 Power a 50MP Sony IMX882 primary camera and an 8MP ultrawide camera. Selfies are taken with a 16MP camera. Good light performance with the main camera. Colouring is fairly reliable , but may be over-coloured at times. Portrait shots also include some smoothing of the skin. The ultrawide camera is adequate for occasional use but is not a major strength of the phone. Video recording is more impressive on paper. The rear camera is able to shoot 4K video at 30 frames per second (fps) and is equipped with optical image stabilisation. The selfie camera also has 4K at 30 fps, and the ultrawide camera is capped at 1080p at 30 fps. View full Image . ( Pragya Singha Roy ) HyperOS features The X8 Power is powered by HyperOS 3 running on Android 16. Users who have used Xiaomi or Poco phones will find the user interface familiar, as there are a few options to customise the launcher and lock screen. There is some pre-installed software, although most of it can be removed. The Indus Appstore is a system app and cannot be uninstalled. By default, Glance is turned off. Poco has guaranteed four years of OS updates and six years of security updates. This means the X8 Power has a longer software runway than other phones in the segment. Verdict: Battery first, everything else second The Poco X8 Power is an unusual phone because its biggest selling point changes the way you use it. A 10,000 mAh battery makes checking the battery percentage less significant. The display, durability and design are a plus, and the cameras and Snapdragon 6 Gen 5 chipset are sufficient for the average user. However, those seeking the primary purpose of gaming or camera features could pursue better options. The X8 Power is the clear choice for those who travel frequently, heavy chargers and those who just don't want to carry a charger around. The 256GB model, at ₹ 38,999, is the more sensible choice, especially as it upgrades the storage from UFS 2.2 to UFS 4.1. Also Read | iPhone Duo yield near 60%: Why Apple's foldable faces supply woes In short, the Poco X8 Power is not trying to be the fastest camera phone or the strongest gaming device in its price range. It is doing something simpler: making battery anxiety almost irrelevant. I rate the Poco X8 Power 7.3/10.

title: Can Temple check if pilots are fit to fly? Deepinder Goyal suggests Air Force could use it too
content: Deepinder Goyal ’s Temple wearable is expected to roll out soon in India. Ahead of opening its pre-orders, Goyal claimed that Temple will be able to check the fitness of pilots before flights. His revelation came days after the FlyDubai incident, where a co-pilot attacked Captain Smit Machchhar during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv in an alleged attempt to crash the flight carrying more than 170 passengers. Temple can be used by pilots and air force Taking to X, Deepinder Goyal said that Temple can also be used by the air force authorities. He said that the wearable would be able to determine the fitness of pilots before taking on a mission. After Goyal announced that Temple would be available in six different colour options, someone wrote to him on X, “One interesting use case for @temple could be giving it to restaurant managers & head chefs. It would be fun to see the data on a dry day vs weekend vs weekday. Would be even more interesting to see shifts till around 7pm and then from 7pm to say 1am. Can this be eventually hooked to an API and detect if a chef is going thru stressful time, cause the supply chain is running late and they risk shortage of raw-materials? I gotta get my hands on this soon (sic).” Responding to the suggestion, Goyal revealed, “I would certainly have it on pilots to check if they are fit to fly. And on the air force to check who is the fittest to fly a mission today.” What is Temple? Temple is a wearable designed to sit on the side of the head, somewhere near the temple area, between the forehead and ear. Unlike other wearables such as smartwatches, Temple is intended to collect information linked to blood flow to the brain. The technology behind it is called BrainFlow. Also Read | Deepinder Goyal reveals six colours for Temple ahead of pre-orders Deepinder Goyal reveals ahead of launch The Zomato founder previously said that Temple will be able to read people's intent. He said that currently research is underway on a thoughts-to-text tech. However, he said that such development would take a few more years. It is expected to be available in the third or fourth version of Temple. Also Read | Does Temple 'stick to your skin'? Can you bathe with it? Deepinder Goyal answers Talking about Temple, Goyal also briefly commented on whether Temple would come with any age restrictions. “We use a PPG sensor. Same as Apple Watch, and other wearables. Nothing in there which can hurt a developing brain. Having said that, I don’t see why anybody less than 18 years would need a Temple, unless they are aiming to go to the Olympics,” he said.

title: OPPO F35 Pro and F35 launched in India with 8,000mAh battery: Price, specs and sale date
content: OPPO has launched its new F35 series in India, the F35 Pro 5G and F35 5G, as the company marks 10 years of its F Series in the country. The smartphones highlight higher battery capacity, a wide-angle front camera, and durability, all at an entry-level price of ₹ 38,999. The OPPO F35 series was unveiled in India on 5th October 2026 and will be available on sale from 11th October 2026 through offline retail stores, the OPPO India e-store, Flipkart, and Amazon. The phones are powered by an 8,000 mAh battery, with 80W SUPERVOOC charging support in both models, while the Pro gets a 144 Hz 1.5K AMOLED display and the MediaTek Dimensity 7360 MAX chipset. OPPO F35 series display The OPPO F35 Pro 5G has a 6.78-inch 1.5K AMOLED screen with a 144 Hz refresh rate. It has up to 3,600-nit peak brightness and 2,160 Hz PWM dimming. It is equipped with a 4 nm MediaTek Dimensity 7360 MAX chipset. According to OPPO, its CPU multi-core performance is 30% higher than the previous generation, while its GPU performance is 35% higher. It's also equipped with a 5,000 mm² SuperCool vapour chamber for thermal management. Also Read | CMF Watch 3 Pro review: Can its heart rate tracking keep up with daily fitness? The display is a 6.57-inch AMOLED with FHD+ resolution, 1,400-nit max brightness, and a 120 Hz refresh rate for the standard OPPO F35 5G. It is powered by a 6 nm MediaTek Dimensity 6360 MAX processor. OPPO F35 series cameras Both smartphones feature a 50MP autofocus front camera with a 100-degree field of view. According to OPPO , the camera can automatically switch to a wider view for group photos. The F35 Pro is equipped with a 50MP rear camera with OIS and an 8MP ultra-wide camera. The front and rear cameras support 4K video recording. The standard F35 features a 50MP primary camera and can record up to 2.5K video. OPPO F35 series battery The F35 series features an 8,000 mAh battery and supports 80W SUPERVOOC charging. According to OPPO, the battery's ability to hold a charge is more than 80% after 1,800 charging cycles. Also Read | Vivo V80 India launch date, camera, battery and display details confirmed The models are also IP66, IP68, IP69, and IP69K-rated and have military durability per MIL-STD-810H. These phones are powered by ColorOS 16 and equipped with features such as AI Recording, AI Call Guard, and AI Ultra-Clear Documents. OPPO F35 series price in India The OPPO F35 Pro 5G starts at ₹ 45,999 for 6GB RAM and 128GB storage. The 8GB+128GB version costs ₹ 49,999, while the 8GB+256GB model costs ₹ 54,999. The OPPO F35 5G starts at ₹ 38,999 for 6GB+128GB, while the 8GB+128GB variant costs ₹ 42,999. According to OPPO's October 5, 2026 launch announcement, buyers can get offers including up to 10% instant cashback, exchange benefits and discounts on the OPPO Enco Buds 3 Pro+.

title: Flipkart Big Billion Days 2026: Are 1.0,000mAh batteries the new smartphone must-have?
content: Flipkart Big Billion Days 2026 is set to begin on October 8, bringing discounts, bank offers and No Cost EMI deals on smartphones across price segments. One of the most notable trends this year is the rise of larger smartphone batteries. Many new phones now pack 7,000 mAh batteries or more, while some exceed 9,000 mAh and 10,000 mAh. Realme, POCO, Vivo , Motorola and Nothing are all participating in Flipkart Big Billion Days. POCO is pushing battery capacity aggressively, while Nothing is taking a different approach with its Phone (4a), Phone (4a) Pro and Phone (4b). For buyers, Flipkart Big Billion Days sale offers an opportunity to compare phones focused on battery capacity with those offering a more balanced set of features. Realme P4 Power leads the battery race The Realme P4 Power 5G is one example of the larger-battery trend. It packs a 10,001 mAh Titan battery, which Realme claims is the first 10,001 mAh smartphone battery in India. It also supports 80W charging and 27W reverse charging. The phone is priced at ₹ 32,999. During Flipkart Big Billion Days, Realme is offering up to ₹ 3,000 off or up to nine months of No Cost EMI. After the maximum discount, the price comes down to ₹ 29,999. The P4 Power also comes with IP69, IP68 and IP66 protection, Gorilla Glass 7i and MIL-STD-810H certification. It is powered by the MediaTek Dimensity 7400 Ultra chipset and features a 6.8-inch 144Hz AMOLED display. Also Read | Nothing Big Billion Days Sale offers: Phone (4a), 4a Pro and 4b prices slashed POCO pushes 10,000mAh batteries into the mainstream POCO is taking the large-battery approach across several price points. The POCO X8 Power has a 10,000 mAh battery. It will be available for ₹ 29,999, down from ₹ 35,999. The POCO X8 Pro Max has a 9,000 mAh battery and is now priced at ₹ 42,999. The POCO X8 also has a 9,000 mAh battery. This will sell for ₹ 24,999, compared with its regular price of ₹ 29,999. The POCO M8 Power brings an 8,000 mAh battery to the ₹ 20,999 price point. Realme takes batteries below ₹ 25,000 Realme pushes large batteries into more affordable segments. The Realme P4x 5G carries a 7,000 mAh battery, a Dimensity 7400 Ultra processor and a 144 Hz display. Its ₹ 26,999 price gets up to ₹ 4,000 off during Flipkart Big Billion Days, bringing the price to ₹ 22,999. The Realme P4 Lite 5G also has a 7,000mAh battery and a 144Hz display. Priced at ₹ 18,999, it receives a ₹ 2,500 Big Billion Days discount, taking the price to ₹ 16,499. Also Read | iPhone Duo yield near 60%: Why Apple's foldable faces supply woes Vivo and Motorola join the battery race The trend includes Vivo and Motorola. The vivo T5x holds a 7,200mAh battery and 44W charging, while the vivo T5 has a 7,050mAh battery and 44W charging. The T5 is priced at ₹ 34,999. The vivo T5 Lite 5G has a 6,500mAh battery, 44W charging and a 120Hz display. It is priced at ₹ 22,999. Motorola's Moto G77 Power also packs a 7,000 mAh battery. It costs ₹ 27,999 and adds expandable storage through a microSD card. Meanwhile, the Moto Edge 70 Fusion focuses more on its 1.5K 144Hz AMOLED display, Snapdragon 7s Gen 3 processor and 68W charging. Nothing takes a different approach Nothing also offers benefits during Flipkart Big Billion Days 2026, but its smartphones show that a bigger battery is not the only way to compete. The Nothing Phone (4a) gets a ₹ 3,000 price cut on the 6GB+128GB variant, along with a ₹ 4,000 bank offer. After the bank offer, coupon and exchange bonus, its effective price is ₹ 32,999. It has a 5,400 mAh battery, a Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 processor and a 6.78‑inch 1.5K 120 Hz AMOLED display. The Nothing Phone (4a) Pro offers a ₹ 4,500 bank offer and a ₹ 500 exchange bonus. The price begins at ₹ 49,999 for the 8GB+128GB version. It has a 6.83‑inch 1.5K 144Hz AMOLED display and a Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 processor. The cheaper Nothing Phone (4b) offers a ₹ 4,000 discount and a ₹ 4,000 bank offer on its 6GB+128GB edition, bringing the price down to ₹ 27,999. It features a 6,000mAh battery, a Snapdragon 6 Gen 4 processor and a 120Hz Super AMOLED display. Are bigger batteries becoming the new smartphone priority? The numbers suggest that battery capacity is becoming a major competition. The Realme P4 Power and POCO X8 Power exceed 10,000 mAh. The POCO X8 Pro Max and POCO X8 provide 9,000 mAh batteries. Even phones priced under ₹ 20,000 now reach 7,000 mAh or more. Yet battery size alone does not decide how long a phone runs. Processor efficiency, display technology, refresh rate, software optimisation and charging speed also shape a phone’s endurance. During Flipkart Big Billion Days 2026, customers will have a variety of options. Those who prioritise maximum endurance can look at the realme P4 Power 5G, POCO X8 Power, POCO X8 Pro Max or POCO X8, while buyers seeking a more balanced package can consider the realme P4x 5G, realme P4 Lite 5G, vivo T5x, vivo T5, Moto G77 Power, Nothing Phone (4a), Nothing Phone (4a) Pro or Nothing Phone (4b). With the sale starting on October 8, 2026, the biggest change may be that a 7,000 mAh-plus battery is no longer unusual. This battery size is quickly turning into a selling point for brands that want to attract smartphone buyers.

title: Your student ID can get you free Gemini AI, Photoshop and more: How to claim
content: A college ID can be more valuable than just proof of enrolment. Students in India can use their student status to access discounted or free services across categories such as artificial intelligence, entertainment, travel, software and electronics. Several companies offer special plans and deals for students. Google, Spotify, Apple, IndiGo, Adobe, Samsung and GitHub are among the companies with student benefits. Eligibility criteria, verification requirements and offer periods can vary, so students should check the terms before signing up. Free Gemini AI and 400GB storage Google is currently offering university students aged 18 and above a free one-year subscription to Google AI Plus. The offer includes Gemini usage limits, 400GB of cloud storage and access to Gemini Omni . Students also get unlimited uploads for features such as Study Notebooks, Visuals and Live. Google announced the student offer on August 19, 2026. According to the company, students can claim the offer until December 31, 2026. After the free period ends, the plan costs ₹ 399 per month unless cancelled. Also Read | CMF Watch 3 Pro review: Can its heart rate tracking keep up with daily fitness? Spotify and Apple Music at ₹ 69 per month Entertainment subscriptions are also more affordable for students who are eligible. Spotify Premium Student in India costs ₹ 69 each month after the offer, and the student status is checked through SheerID. Apple Music also has a student plan that costs ₹ 69 each month. Apple Music includes Apple TV access with the plan. Students can keep the student price for up to four years as long as they are still eligible. YouTube also has a student membership in India. However, the ₹ 89 monthly price mentioned on some websites should not be treated as a confirmed current rate. YouTube requires students to study at an eligible institution and verify their status through SheerID. Student fares can mean cheaper flights IndiGo's Student Fare can give you up to 10% off the base price of domestic flights plus an extra 10 kg of baggage space depending on the airline's rules and availability. Students can use a real student ID or an acceptance letter to check, according to the IndiGo press release from November 22, 2024. Also Read | Zoho targeting WhatsApp Business with Arattai for Business? Here’s what we know Apple and Samsung offer discounts on gadgets Apple's Education Store gives prices on eligible Macs and iPads. Apple's India education store currently shows the MacBook Air starting at ₹ 137,900 with education discounts. Samsung has its Student Advantage programme. According to Samsung, students at select institutes can get up to 10% off on eligible Galaxy products, but the actual discount depends on the product and the school. GitHub benefits for student developers Students who like coding can apply for the GitHub Student Developer Pack. GitHub says the program includes GitHub Copilot Student and other partner benefits, which can include some domains and cloud credits. Adobe Photoshop is free for one year Adobe is giving students in India a free Photoshop annual plan for the first year. The checkout page shows the price as ₹ 1,999 per year, but the offer price is ₹ 0. Students should know that the offer will start charging ₹ 1,999 each year after the time unless it is cancelled. Adobes offers users the option to log in, share college information and finish UPI AutoPay authorisation. A small token amount of around ₹ 2 may be charged to set up the mandate. Once activated, Photoshop can be downloaded through Adobe Creative Cloud and used for the next 12 months.

title: Norway to propose temporary ban on AI glasses in some public places
content: COPENHAGEN, Oct 5 (Reuters) - Norway's government said on Monday it plans to propose a temporary ban on the use of AI glasses in selected places, saying it is concerned people could be photographed, filmed or audio-recorded without their knowledge. The proposal mirrors a broader global backlash against smart glasses equipped with cameras over privacy concerns * Ban could apply to places where the public regularly gather, such as parks, beaches, museums, shopping centres and public events, the government said in a statement * "I am worried that new, powerful technology is being introduced where people risk being photographed, filmed or audio-recorded without knowing it," Digitalisation and Public Governance Minister Torgeir Micaelsen said * It could also apply to schools, playgrounds and youth clubs and to privacy-sensitive places such as doctors' offices, swimming pools and gyms with changing rooms * The government said it was not eyeing a total ban and that private use, and use where others are not at risk of being filmed without consent, would still be allowed * It said it would examine which technology the ban would cover, including whether it would apply to glasses with camera and audio recording, glasses with camera and AI functions or also other body-worn technology with camera, audio recording and/or AI * The minority government said it would present a bill to parliament as soon as possible, and would also set up an expert group to advise on permanent national regulation of body-worn technology (Reporting by Stine Jacobsen, editing by Anna Ringstrom )

title: OpenAIs Altman says AI benefits warrant accepting some risks
content: Oct 4 (Reuters) - OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman said the benefits of artificial intelligence justify accepting some risks and argued the technology should remain broadly accessible to the public "We believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency," Altman said in an interview with Politico's technology-focused newsletter Decoded. Altman said there remained a fundamental difference in worldview between OpenAI and rival Anthropic on AI regulation, adding: "I think there's a lot of daylight." "I disagree, but I understand the perspective of people who are like, 'This technology is going to get so powerful, and it's so dangerous, that a single lab in San Francisco should have it and make sure nothing bad happens, and kind of figure out how to dole out the benefits,'" Altman said. He called that "a completely unacceptable trade-off" that runs counter to the "lighter-touch regulatory stance" backed by OpenAI. "I wouldn't take a trade of saying, 'We'll make sure there's no major hacks, there's no misuse of this technology, there's zero scams, there's zero all the other bad things that will happen,'" Altman said. "Because I think people will do tremendously — orders of magnitude more — good stuff than bad stuff." Altman's remarks come amid a growing debate within the AI industry over the pace of development and the risks posed by increasingly capable systems. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei in September published an essay calling on the industry to slow down to "pace the frontier," a stance that Altman publicly endorsed. Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned in September, saying the people building AI believe it "could kill us all by the end of the decade. Reuters reported in September that Anthropic warned that, despite AI's potential benefits, the technology can sometimes act in ways that run counter to its makers' intentions and penetrate other companies' systems. The company said advanced models could exhibit "self-preserving behaviors," including attempts to "resist shutdown," "conceal or manipulate information," or generate outputs that could be interpreted as "coercive, deceptive, or manipulative." However, US President Donald Trump has largely dismissed calls for new restrictions, arguing they would make it harder for American companies to compete with Chinese rivals. He has repeatedly said existing law enforcement agencies, including the Justice Department, provide sufficient safeguards and that no new rules are needed. (Reporting by Rishabh Jaiswal in Bengaluru)

title: Does Temple 'stick to your skin'? Can you bathe with it, swim with it? Eternal's Deepinder Goyal answers
content: Zomato founder and Eternal Vice-Chairman Deepinder Goyal has addressed a series of questions about his new wearable, Temple, after an X user @tyags6 raised concerns about everything from whether the device sticks to the skin to whether it can be worn while showering or swimming. Goyal responded to the questions on October 3, explaining how Temple is attached and how its adhesive Grips are designed to work. He said the device uses single-use Grips, with an unlimited supply included in the price. "Yes, with single use Grips (aka tapes). Price includes unlimited supply of Grips. Not weird – you don't even feel you are wearing Temple . Inventing the right Grips was as hard as making the device. We have now gotten them right for 99% of our audience," Goyal said. Can you shower or swim with Temple? One of the questions was whether the wearable would remain in place during activities such as running, jumping, swimming or bathing. Goyal said the device is designed to remain firmly attached during such activities. "Super sticky – can run, jump, sauna, swim, shower with it. Everything except scuba dive (but that's a device issue, not a tape issue). Doesn't move. Doesn't itch," he said. On whether the Grip can be removed and reused, Goyal said users would need to apply a fresh one each time. "You can remove Temple, but not reuse a Grip. Always use a fresh Grip," he said. How long does the Grip last? The X user also asked whether the wearable could accidentally come off when removing a T-shirt and whether the adhesive would remain effective after repeated use. Goyal said Temple's smooth edges are designed to prevent it from being displaced by clothing. He added that some users keep a single Grip on for about seven days, corresponding to the device's battery life, although the company recommends replacing it every two to three days. "Not at all. It has very smooth edges and everything just slides over. People sometimes use a single Grip for around 7 days (battery life of the device). We recommend changing the Grip every 2/3 days though," Goyal said. He added that users can carry out their regular routines while wearing Temple, including face washing, showering, skincare and applying makeup. What if your skin itches? The user also asked what would happen if the area under the wearable became itchy. Goyal said he had not heard of this issue so far and attributed the comfort to the medical-grade Grips. "Haven't heard this so far. Maybe our medical grade grips are so good and they keep your skin so nice and supple that it never itches :)" he said. Goyal also claimed that customers have described Temple as the most comfortable wearable they have used, while acknowledging that it can take about five minutes to get accustomed to wearing it. Temple colours and pre-orders The exchange followed Goyal's October 1 post on X announcing six colours for the launch edition of Temple. The options are True Gold, Rose Gold, Dark Mirror, Real Jade, Deep Blue and Purple Funk. Goyal said pre-orders were expected to open soon, subject to finalising a few remaining details. He also said people on the early-access waitlist would receive priority access. What is Temple? Temple is an experimental wearable developed to monitor blood flow in the brain continuously and in real time. The compact sensor is positioned near the temple to track cerebral blood flow, which can provide insights into neurological health and ageing. The device is being developed through Goyal’s personal research venture, Continue Research, for which he has pledged $25 million from his own funds. Temple is separate from Zomato and is not a product of the food-delivery company. It is being developed independently under Eternal.

title: India needs its own AI safety framework, not a copy of US pact: Industry experts
content: New Delhi, Oct 4 (PTI) India should build its own artificial intelligence (AI) safety framework suited to its languages, scale, and application-led AI ecosystem rather than replicate a voluntary pact signed by US President Donald Trump and top technology firms last week, industry experts said. They also called for a commitment that brings together all stakeholders and tackles risks such as deepfakes and cyberattacks, even as they differed on whether voluntary measures alone would be enough. The comments came after the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, a voluntary AI safety pact signed on September 29 by Trump and top executives from Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Nvidia and Elon Musk's xAI. Under the accord, the companies committed to internal controls to monitor their AI models, dedicated oversight teams, independent external audits and board-level oversight. They also agreed to meet regularly to set safety standards. Nasscom Chairman and Fractal Group CEO Srikanth Velamakanni said India should not simply replicate the US. Instead, it should use a domestic commitment as a building block towards a global understanding of AI safety. "As models become more capable and agentic, we are giving them greater access to systems and greater autonomy to make decisions. AI safety must be strengthened considerably and must stay ahead of capability to prevent catastrophic risks," Velamakanni said. He noted that the US accord is largely a push for self-policing by frontier AI companies. The European Union, by contrast, has taken a binding, risk-based approach, while China follows a state-directed control model. India, the Nasscom Chairman said, could use its role in the Global Partnership on AI (GPAI) and the momentum from hosting the AI Impact Summit in February to prevent worst-case outcomes, without citizens of India and the Global South being denied access to frontier models. "India doesn't need to copy the US model, but it can take inspiration from it and expedite efforts to build a trusted AI ecosystem," said Soumen Mandal, Principal Analyst at Counterpoint Research. He added that such a commitment should cover testing AI systems before deployment, independent audits, reporting serious problems, and naming people responsible for AI-related risks. Amit Khanna, Partner and Automation Ecosystem Leader at Grant Thornton Bharat, said any commitment should be suited to Indian market conditions. He noted that India's focus is on building AI applications rather than major foundational models. "An industry commitment in India should ensure AI works reliably across vernacular languages and unique cultural contexts and should not exploit AI knowledge asymmetry in the population," Khanna said. Ganesh Gopalan, co-founder and CEO of Gnani.ai, said any framework must ensure a level playing field. Global frontier models should be subject to the same rules as Indian ones, he said, since Indian AI companies compete with global firms for the same customers. The experts differed on whether self-regulation would be enough. "Voluntary, self-regulatory approaches are necessary but woefully insufficient," Velamakanni said. "Pharmaceuticals and aviation are great examples of industries where strong, technically competent regulators have strengthened safety and public trust without stopping innovation." He said India needs binding rules on transparency, incident reporting, and accountability when serious harm occurs. The IndiaAI Safety Institute should be strengthened to test newly released models, but without creating a bottleneck by requiring pre-release certification of every model, he added. Mandal backed a hybrid approach. Mandatory rules would apply to potential harms in defence, healthcare, banking, and government use cases, while voluntary standards would cover fast-moving technical areas where regulators may lack technical expertise. "This type of hybrid approach will provide flexibility to AI companies instead of restricting every line of code while ensuring safety and privacy are not compromised," he said. Khanna also called for a hybrid "techno-legal" approach. It would pair a strong voluntary layer with binding mandates, such as the provisions on synthetically generated information in the IT Amendment Rules, 2026. He said voluntary compliance alone leaves significant gaps, particularly in civil rights and public safety. Gopalan, however, favoured self-regulation. "Voluntary self-regulation is key given the technology is new. Having mandatory regulation can stifle competition and lead to concerns about a few companies getting preferential treatment. "India needs more than 100 frontier AI lab companies, and that's the need of the hour to prevent India from being colonised, which is inevitable if we lag behind in the AI race," Gopalan said. The Indian government is in the process of bringing in its own AI regulation. Earlier this year, IT Secretary S Krishnan noted that while existing legal provisions have so far been adequate in addressing initial concerns on issues like deepfakes and AI-generated synthetic content, an "additional regulation or law may be needed". "It is a conversation which has commenced, and my minister (IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw) and I have both been on record earlier that we will look at AI regulation when the time is right, and it appears that the time is getting right, and we will start looking at it," he had said. Vaishnaw had also said that the current information technology law was framed much before the rapid emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and that a new legal framework may be required to deal with the changing landscape. The industry agrees that any pact should go beyond AI companies. "This cannot be an agreement among AI companies alone," Velamakanni said. He said the government, frontier model developers, large deployers, including enterprises and public agencies, academia, and independent safety researchers should all have defined roles. Workers, users, and civil society should have formal channels to report harms. He added that safety evaluations of frontier models should be carried out by independent, expert institutions and published, with narrow exceptions where disclosure itself creates a security risk. Mandal said the agreement should bring together the entire AI ecosystem, from AI companies and their business users to regulators, universities, researchers, workers, and users. Khanna argued that it should include government and public sector bodies, which would be major users of AI, as well as civil society, worker unions, and technology companies. Meanwhile, Gopalan called for broader self-regulation across the AI ecosystem to ensure impartial access to limited compute resources. Velamakanni said the top concern must be preventing catastrophic and systemic harms. He listed large-scale cyberattacks, electoral interference, biological or chemical weapons, attacks on critical infrastructure, and loss of control over highly autonomous systems. Individual harms such as deepfakes, fraud, impersonation, privacy breaches, and self-harm come next. "Autonomy must lag behind assurance to provide a margin of safety. As AI systems gain the ability to act in the world (use tools, move money, change systems, make consequential decisions), the evidence that they are safe and controllable must grow faster than the autonomy we give them," he said. Gopalan said that given India's large population and democratic framework, the bigger concerns are deepfakes and cyberattacks targeting financial institutions. Khanna also named deepfakes as the top immediate priority. He described misinformation, deepfakes, and political manipulation as "existential threats to India's social fabric". He said rules on liability when AI systems fail, such as misdiagnosing a patient or wrongly denying welfare benefits, remain a critical gap. Mandal placed independent audits first, followed by accountability, data protection, deepfakes, and job impact. "Without independent testing and audits, the system will not be complete, as companies may sometimes overlook AI-related concerns," he said.

title: ‘Unconstitutional’: Advocacy group condemns BitChat's removal from India App Store on govt order, lists four demands
content: The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF), an advocacy organisation, criticised Apple's decision to remove BitChat from App Store as "unconstitutional". The organisation said, "Section 69A permits the blocking of unlawful information, not of a messenger for working during internet shutdowns." Bitchat is an offline messaging application associated with Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey. The IFF's statement came after Jack Dorsey said Apple removed Bitchat from the India App Store following a takedown demand from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). On Saturday, Dorsey shared a screenshot of Apple's notice on X, stating that the "government of India officially removes Bitchat from the App Store." IIF's full statement Condemning Apple's move, the IIF posted X, "The removal of BitChat from the India App Store is unconstitutional." It takes note of the Apple App Review notice published by Jack Dorsey on X. The notice records that BitChat has been removed from the India App Store "per demand from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology", issued under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000, on the ground that the application "includes content that is illegal in India." The notice adds that BitChat's TestFlight builds are no longer available for testing in India. The IIF said the notice "does not identify the content said to be illegal or the ground under Section 69A invoked." "The blocking order has not been published. The Internet Freedom Foundation condemns the order and calls for its immediate publication and withdrawal," the IIF added. In a lengthy post, the IFF made four demands: 1. MeitY must publish the blocking order, the ground invoked and the record of the committee's proceedings, and serve the developers with a copy and an opportunity of hearing. 2. The direction must be withdrawn. Any specific unlawful use must be met with targeted proceedings under due process, not the removal of a communications tool for everyone. 3.
